out.brandingAndContentModel:
All paths are relative to /Users/bozhidardenev/kodes/worktrees/rk-portal-redesign (current main, 878268bf1). There are two branding layers, and only one of them reaches guests.

(1) PROPERTY BRAND PROFILE, one per Property. This is what guests see. It lives in src/contexts/portal/application/ports/portal-experience.repository.ts and domain/portal-publication-snapshot.ts (PortalBrandProfileSnapshot).
- Fields: displayName (1–120), logoUrl, defaultHeroImageUrl, primaryColor, backgroundColor, textColor (each colour is a 6-digit hex), and version.
- Colour validation is in portal-experience.dto.ts. Text/background contrast must be at least 4.5:1. primary/background is only checked to be parseable, with no contrast floor.
- Only an AccountAdmin (portal.admin) can edit it. The save path is savePropertyPortalBrandProfile in use-cases/manage-portal-experience.ts. It hard-codes logoUrl and defaultHeroImageUrl to null, so a manager cannot set a URL.
- Default palette is #2563EB / #FFFFFF / #111827 (DEFAULT_PROPERTY_BRAND_PALETTE).
- displayName is also the AI-reply business name. It is edited in Property settings → Profile (property-public-display-name-card.tsx) and in the setup wizard. The portal editor only links to it.

(2) PROPERTY LOCALIZED CONTENT, per Property and locale: title (1–120) and shortDescription (1–500). Both are required for every enabled locale before publish. AccountAdmin only. UI label: 'Property-wide fallback'.

(3) PORTAL LOCALIZED OVERRIDE, per Portal and locale: title (≤120 or null) and shortDescription (≤500 or null). A null falls back to the Property content. heroImageUrl exists but is forced to null. Editable with portal.update.

(4) PORTAL ENTITY (domain/types.ts):
- name (≤100, internal/admin label), slug (2–64; there is no public slug route, URLs are /p/{token}), description (≤500, legacy/internal), heroImageUrl (nullable, historical only).
- theme {primaryColor, backgroundColor?, textColor?}. This is a per-Portal legacy palette, edited with ThemePresetSelector: Light #6366f1/#fff/#111827, Dark #a5b4fc/#111827/#f9fafb, Brand #b45309/#fffbeb/#1c1917, and Custom with a primary colour picker only.
- privateFeedbackThreshold (1–5, default 3), publicationState (draft|published|disabled|archived), primaryGuestLocale (en|bg), additionalGuestLocales (max 1).

Publication and resolution (repositories/portal-publication.repository.ts, infrastructure/portal-command-store.ts, use-cases/resolve-public-portal-token.ts):
- Every new publish builds a schema-v2 snapshot. Publishing is refused unless the brand profile exists and every enabled locale has content.
- The guest-facing values are resolved as follows. h1 = override title, falling back to Property title. Description = override shortDescription, falling back to Property shortDescription. The muted line under the title is brandProfile.displayName. Logo = brand logoUrl, which is null today. Hero = override hero, then brand default hero, which is null today. Theme colours = brand profile colours, which OVERRIDE portal.theme entirely.
- Consequence: the per-Portal Theme presets, portal.name and portal.description change nothing on a live v2 portal. They drive only the admin list swatch and the admin preview.

Rendering (portal-theme-style.ts): CSS variables --portal-primary, --portal-on-primary (black or white chosen by WCAG luminance in portal-contrast.ts), --portal-bg, --portal-text, --portal-accent-soft (12% primary), --portal-accent-border (40% primary), --portal-text-muted (72% text mixed into bg).

What an admin cannot set today:
- No fonts, layout or template choice, no radius/style options.
- No logo or photo: upload is safety-blocked and URLs are forced null. The organization logo upload in Identity is not wired to portals.
- No per-portal colours on v2.
- No custom guest UI copy: the question, button labels and receipts come from an immutable language pack (guest-ui-en-v1 / guest-ui-bg-v1) that the snapshot pins.
- No placement/channel label, no social icons, no address/phone.

Guest typography is the app font Satoshi, loaded from api.fontshare.com.
out.secondaryLinksModel:
Data model (domain/types.ts, dto/portal-link*.dto.ts):
- A Portal has ordered PortalLinkCategory rows: title 1–100, sortKey. Each category has ordered PortalLink rows: label 1–100, url https-only ≤500, iconKey ≤50 optional, destinationId, legacyDestinationState, sortKey.
- Labels and category titles are single strings, not localized per EN/BG.
- iconKey is stored but not rendered or edited anywhere.
- No description or image per link.

Approved destinations (domain/approved-destination.ts, portal-settings/portal-approved-destinations-editor.tsx):
- Every link URL must resolve to a Property-scoped Approved Destination.
- Hosts under booking.com, expedia.com, facebook.com, instagram.com, linkedin.com, tripadvisor.com, x.com and youtube.com are auto-approved ('recognized'). Anything else is 'pending' until an AccountAdmin approves it. States: pending, approved, disabled, quarantined.
- A job revalidates every 15 min. Public resolution serves a link only if its destination was validated in the last 30 min.
- Unapproved or lapsed links are silently dropped from the snapshot and from the public response. The server reports this; the guest and manager see nothing.

Admin editing:
- Links tab: LinkTree (link-tree/*) with add/edit/delete category, inline add/edit link (label + URL), dnd reorder of categories and links, and an empty state suggesting a 'Review sites' category.
- The destination request/approve list sits separately in Settings → Guest experience.

Guest rendering and behaviour:
- Links show only after a rating, inside the receipt ('More from {displayName}' → category headings → bordered rows). e2e/critical/guest-portal.spec.ts:76-88 pins that they are hidden before rating, so showing them from arrival is a proposed behaviour change.
- Clicking calls selectSecondaryLinkFn, which records a 'secondary_link' destination selection in the Reporting lifetime aggregate (secondaryLinkSelectionCount, never shown in UI), then assigns the URL.
- The no-JS GET fallback /api/public/p/{token}/click/{linkId} redirects 302 and records no metric.
- A Portal may have zero links.
constraints: Rating first: the guest's first act is a required private integer rating from 1 to 5, submitted explicitly. The submit implies responseConsent:true. The initial command cannot carry text (Guest CONTEXT invariant 1).

Anti-gating is an ADR 0044 invariant plus Guest invariant 2. After a durable rating, the Google Review Action comes first and is identical for 1–5 in position, wording and prominence. It is never hidden, reordered, demoted, delayed or emphasised by score. Designs may not vary the Google card's styling by rating (e.g. a celebratory treatment only for 5 stars).

Private feedback is additive only. It is offered at or below the threshold (inclusive, 1..5, default 3; 0 and 6 are rejected, so it cannot be disabled). It is never an alternative, prerequisite or replacement for Google. It is sent as a separate command, 2,000 characters maximum.
RepKey only records that Google was selected. Copy must never claim or thank for a written review. The Google URI reaches the browser only after the server selection call.
Degraded Google means the same slot shows gentle unavailable copy for every rating, while private feedback and links stay usable. A stale URI is never rendered.

No incentives or solicitation mechanics: no rewards, badges, leaderboards, or pre-filled five-star 'Rate us' cards. Ratestar's 'Google ★★★★★ Rate us' tiles and its multi-platform review grid are not reproducible. Tripadvisor or Booking can appear only as subordinate secondary links.
No guest contact collection (portal.guest_contact is safety-blocked) and no guest media. Guests enter no personal details.

Portal image upload is safety-blocked (portal.upload; SAFE-01 completion record needed). logoUrl, defaultHeroImageUrl and override heroImageUrl are forced null for new data. Every design must look finished with no photo and no logo. A historical hero_image_url can still render and must be handled (og:image uses it).

Essential telemetry is first-party and server-side only: no analytics cookie, third-party tracker, ad ID or fingerprinting. The disclosure notice must remain: region 'Portal analytics information' with a 'Got it' button, pinned by e2e.

CSP (src/shared/security/security-headers.ts) allows style-src self plus api.fontshare.com and fonts.googleapis.com, font-src self plus cdn.fontshare.com and fonts.gstatic.com, img-src https: and data:, frame-src none. Any new guest font must be self-hosted or from Google Fonts, and must cover Cyrillic for Bulgarian.
The unavailable posture must stay identical and brand-free for bad token, unpublished, suspended and denied, so nothing is enumerable. Pages are noindex with no canonical URL.

Locales are exactly en and bg. The admin UI always includes English and adds Bulgarian optionally, with a fallback locale. Guest UI copy comes from immutable, versioned language packs pinned by each publication snapshot. New copy needs new pack versions (e.g. guest-ui-en-v2 / guest-ui-bg-v2) plus updates to PORTAL_LANGUAGE_PACK_VERSIONS, the public-api type union and the publication checks. Live portals keep v1 until republished.

Brand colours: 6-digit hex. Text on background must be at least 4.5:1. Text on primary is auto black or white by luminance. In v2 the colours are Property-wide and owned by AccountAdmin, not per Portal.

Content limits: Guest title 1–120 and short description 1–500 per locale (required for publish). Override title ≤120 and description ≤500, nullable. Portal name ≤100. Link label and category title ≤100. Link URL is https-only, ≤500 characters, and must map to an approved destination.

Publication: the working copy never mutates a live snapshot. Publish is deliberate and creates an immutable snapshot plus an activation. Rollback appends; nothing is rewritten. Disable and archive close the activation. Archive is recoverable to Disabled. Snapshots also pin the Google destination binding and the language pack.

Publish prerequisites: a public address (token) already issued; no responsibilityNeededSince (at least one responsible manager); a verified Google destination; a complete brand profile; content for every enabled locale.

Stable tokens: printed QR/NFC codes keep working across content edits. The raw address is shown only once, at issue or rotation. Rotation is planned (grace 1–90 days, default 30) or immediate. Revoke kills all addresses.
Guest response rights: correction window 1 hour, private-feedback withdrawal 24 h, full response withdrawal 24 h, shared-device session reset. Receipts never echo the feedback text.

Metrics: exactly three governed measures (qualified_scans, portal_rating_count, portal_rating_average) at Property, Portal Group and Portal scope. Missing, stale or insufficient data is never shown as zero (use Data through…, Updating, Insufficient data or Temporarily unavailable). A rating comparison needs 10+ ratings in each period. Person and Team goals are prohibited.
Responsible manager assignment never grants property or portal access or staff attribution. The creator is the default. When the last manager is removed, nobody is auto-promoted.
Portal Groups are Property-scoped, with names unique per Property. A portal is in at most one active group.
Accessibility: main landmark, Storybook axe gate, WCAG AA text contrast, global reduced-motion rule. Inbox precedent: 36px targets on mobile (24px minimum under 2.5.8).

e2e pins these guest accessible names and flow: heading = portal title; radios '1 star'…'5 stars'; 'Submit private rating'; 'Thank you. Your private rating was submitted.'; textbox 'Private feedback'; 'Send private feedback'; 'Your private feedback was sent to the property team.'; 'You rated this experience N/5.'; 'Change your private rating'; 'Save rating correction'; 'Withdraw my entire response'; 'Your response was withdrawn'; 'Portal Unavailable'; 'Please try again later.'; links hidden before rating (e2e/critical/guest-portal.spec.ts).
Code budget from inbox precedent: ESLint max-lines is 300 counted lines per file. Every new state needs 320, 390 and 1440 stories.

out.inboxDesignLanguage:
Tokens (src/styles.css):
- Colours are all oklch on a cool 270 hue. Background oklch(0.98 0.003 270) is an off-white page; --surface/--card is white; --surface-elevated. Hairlines --border oklch(0.9…) and --border-strong 0.78. Text is tiered: --text-primary 0.18, --text-secondary/--muted-foreground 0.48, --text-tertiary 0.7.
- One accent: purple --accent/--primary oklch(0.42 0.18 290), hover 0.36, --accent-muted 0.93 for active or selected rows, --ring 0.58.
- Semantic colours: --destructive; --positive/--negative are text-grade, always paired with a sign or arrow; the --warn family (warn, warn-muted, warn-line, warn-track) means 'private/internal' only and is never used alone as a signal; --rating is gold for stars; the chart palette is purple-shifted.
- A full .dark mirror exists, applied by a root THEME_INIT_SCRIPT (light/dark/auto).
- Fonts: Satoshi for body/sans (Fontshare CDN), Plus Jakarta Sans as display (.display-title, not used in the inbox), JetBrains Mono.
- Radius base 6px (--radius 0.375rem): sm 4, md 6, lg 8, xl 12. The composer dock is rounded-xl.

Density and structure (docs/plan/inbox-detail-v2.md, docs/plan/inbox-workspace.md, docs/plan/dashboard-redesign.md):
- Regions are separated by 1px border-b or border-r hairlines, not nested cards. Cards appear only where an edge groups something.
- Header 56px (h-14 border-b), case toolbar 48px (min-h-12, wraps to 85px), list rows fixed at 78px, queue rail 224px (w-56) with 32px rows.
- Meta text is 13px (text-[13px]); secondary is 12px (text-xs muted); 11px uppercase appears only for the rail label; counts use tabular-nums.
- Controls are 32px on desktop and 36px on mobile. The inbox deliberately dropped the 44px rule, citing WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum. The dashboard redesign kept ≥44px.
- Dashboard sections are 24px apart, grids 16px; h2 is 18px semibold sentence case (no uppercase eyebrows). PageShell width tiers: 1200 dashboard, 5xl standard, 3xl narrow.

Principles:
(1) Facts, controls and details wear different clothes. A control is an outlined 32px button, with a chevron if it opens a menu, grouped in a ButtonGroup. A fact is plain 13px text with a glyph and no box (CaseFact). A detail is the same text with a dotted underline that opens a popover. Nothing else is a pill; chips are reserved for topics and reply state.
(2) Purple is interactive only. Status facts use a neutral bg-foreground dot; volumes use neutral ink.
(3) Private is said in words plus a dashed edge plus amber, never colour alone.
(4) A ledger/Timeline (ui/timeline.tsx): 32px indicator column, 2px connector, 12px gap, event sentences as actor · verb · object · time. Long runs of system events fold.
(5) One primary action per area. Guarantees are carried by a tooltip and the success toast, not by standing explanatory lines.
(6) Availability renders by exception. Thin data gets a number where there is one, otherwise one sentence plus one action, never a dash. Vocabulary is consistent (Portal scans / Private feedback / Updated).
(7) Search is a mode of the header; bulk selection is the header in another state; empty states name the queue.
(8) Measured, not guessed: stories at 320/390/1440, a metrics gate on geometry, axe, and e2e-pinned accessible names.

The admin should stay neutral and purple, while the guest page carries the property's brand.
out.languages:
Supported guest locales are exactly en and bg (src/contexts/portal/domain/portal-publication-snapshot.ts PORTAL_LANGUAGE_PACK_VERSIONS; portal-localization.ts).

Per-portal configuration:
- primaryGuestLocale (the fallback) plus additionalGuestLocales, max 1.
- The admin UI (portal-locale-configuration.tsx) always keeps English, offers an 'Offer Bulgarian' checkbox and a 'Fallback language' select, and saves separately with 'Save languages'.
- Locale changes cannot be bundled into a publish request.

Content per locale:
- Property-wide Guest title and short description, required for every enabled locale before publish (AccountAdmin), plus an optional per-portal override.
- Link labels and category titles are NOT localized.
- UI chrome copy comes from immutable language packs guest-ui-en-v1 and guest-ui-bg-v1 (src/components/features/guest/public-portal/guest-language-pack.ts, about 60 keys per locale). The pack is pinned by the publication snapshot and recorded as evidence on each guest response. getGuestPortalCopy throws if locale and pack mismatch.

Selection at request time (domain/portal-experience.ts selectPortalGuestLocale), in order:
1. the ?locale= query param,
2. the locale in the signed guest session cookie,
3. Accept-Language base tags,
4. the snapshot primary locale.
Legacy v1 snapshots are English only.

Switching is a full-page link reload to /p/{token}?locale=xx (portal-language-nav.tsx), shown as 'English' / 'Български' pills only when more than one locale is enabled.

Gaps:
- /privacy, the PortalUnavailable page and the admin UI are English-only.
- Deadlines are formatted with bg-BG/en date formats pinned to UTC with no zone label.
- The app font Satoshi is likely Latin-only (verify), so Bulgarian text probably falls back to Inter/system-ui.
out.analyticsToday:
Per-portal only, in the detail page's Analytics tab (src/components/features/portal/portal-analytics/*, data from getPortalAnalyticsFn in src/contexts/reporting/server/portal-analytics.ts, type PortalAnalyticsData in src/contexts/reporting/domain/dashboard-types.ts).

Access and range:
- Authorized by the dashboard.read permission (dashboard.use capability). The tab is hidden when that capability is off; a dark denial shows 'Analytics isn't available yet'.
- TimeRangePicker offers 7d/30d/60d/90d/180d/all, stored in localStorage and defaulting to All time. This is inconsistent with the dashboard's ?range= 30d/90d/6mo/All default and BETA's rolling-30 default.

Content:
- Four StatCards, each with an availability state and 'data through' evidence:
  - Scans (qualified), with a trend %.
  - Private rating avg, whose comparison needs 10+ ratings in each period.
  - Feedback (private feedback count).
  - Review Clicks (Google selections).
- Metric evidence summary (governed period), or a lifetime reconciliation summary for All time (revision, last check, anonymous baseline).
- Response integrity sentence: accepted, filtered automatically, or under review.
- Engagement Funnel chart: Scans → Private ratings → Review Clicks, with widths clamped to be monotonic.
- Private rating distribution and private rating trend charts.
- Empty state: 'No data yet · Share your portal to start collecting metrics.'

Governed measures: exactly qualified_scans, portal_rating_count and portal_rating_average (Property, Portal Group and Portal scope). They appear only in the Goals results matrix.

Not in the UI:
- A Property-wide portals overview, group-level analytics, cross-portal comparison or leaderboard-free ranking.
- A QR vs NFC or access-artifact channel split.
- Secondary-link selection counts (they exist in the Reporting lifetime aggregate as secondaryLinkSelectionCount).
- Portal Health status and reasons (healthy/degraded/unavailable; reasons such as responsibility_needed, google_destination_unavailable, public_address_unavailable), which exist as durable domain data in src/contexts/portal/domain/portal-health.ts. They only produce a 'portal.health_attention' notification.
- Observation-loss monitoring (an OperationsSnapshot field, not tenant-facing).

FleetEntry.scanCount exists in reporting for the fleet overview.

The tab's styling puts provenance (evidence, reconciliation revision) above the numbers, which is exactly what dashboard-redesign rows 8 and 12 removed elsewhere.
reusableForPortal:
Domain and back end, reusable as-is:
- Property Brand Profile, Property localized content and portal overrides (manage-portal-experience.ts, portal-experience.dto.ts).
- Immutable publication snapshots with an activation history, plus the rollbackPortalPublication and getPortalPublicationHistory server fns. Rollback has no UI yet.
- Stable tokens with QR/NFC access artifacts; planned and immediate rotation; revoke; tokenStatus.
- Responsible managers and responsibilityNeededSince; Portal Groups; approved destinations with auto-recognized hosts.
- Portal Health derivation (portal-health.ts), ready for a monitoring UI.

Guest journey logic, which can be re-skinned without touching behaviour:
- use-guest-response-controller.ts (rate, correct, feedback, withdraw both kinds, session reset, Google selection).
- guest-rating-form.tsx and guest-private-feedback-form.tsx (TanStack Form plus shared DTOs and honeypot).
- The GuestResponseView receipt contract.
- selectSecondaryLink and the no-JS click fallback.

Theming helpers:
- resolvePortalThemeStyle (the --portal-* CSS variables with opaque color-mix tints).
- readableForegroundOn and contrastRatio (portal-contrast.ts and the domain's portal-experience.ts), usable to enforce any new palette or preset system.

Localization plumbing:
- selectPortalGuestLocale, PortalLanguageNav, and the versioned language-pack mechanism (add v2 packs for new copy).
- guest-language-pack-types.ts as the copy inventory to rewrite.

Admin shell primitives:
- PageShell tiers and PageHeader; Tabs with URL ?tab= state and hidden-tab rules.
- Sheet-based preview, which already renders PublicPortalContent and could render the real snapshot and locale.
- PortalUnsavedChangesPrompt; EmptyState, ButtonGroup, CaseFact-style facts, Kbd, and Timeline (ui/timeline.tsx, suited to publication history as a ledger).
- Badge vocabulary for publication state (portal-publication-badge.ts).

Analytics UI:
- StatCard with availability; the availability-line and metric-availability-presentation helpers.
- ratingPresentation (10-rating comparison rule); RatingDistributionChart; ChartCard; the dashboard-range ?range= helpers.
- The goal results matrix pattern for Property, Group and Portal scopes.
Share tooling: useQrCodeGeneration, useCopyLink, the QR PNG download, and the once-shown-address copy patterns.
ui/star-rating.tsx (with tone='rating' amber and showValue) and the --rating token for star visuals in the admin; the guest page needs its own brand-aware star.
Storybook stories for every guest lifecycle state and the portal detail/list, plus the e2e guest-portal spec. These are ready to become the 320/390/1440 visual gate for a redesign.

Prior exploration assets in docs/design/portal-experience/:
- Reference screenshots: ratestar-guest.png, current-portal.png, current-admin.png, duve.png, inbox-content.png.
- Concept images: Quiet Welcome, Local Character, and Signature Stay (selected). Admin round 2: Refined Sections, Visual Studio, Guest Journey.
- The critique of the concepts (README.md, admin-round-2.md).
gapsAndRisks: GUEST BUG: the selected star has no visual state. All five boxes show an identical filled ★ and the label has no :checked style, so after tapping, a sighted guest cannot tell which rating is chosen (guest-response-fields.tsx).

Guests see manager and policy copy. The live entry card prints 'Guests start with a private 1–5 star rating. Google follows after the rating, with private feedback offered when eligible.' (previewRatingBody reused in InitialRatingForm).

The admin preview misrepresents the live page. It renders portal.name, portal.description, the legacy portal.theme and the organization name. Guests on a v2 snapshot see the localized title and description, the brand displayName and the brand colours. There is no locale switch and no post-rating, degraded or feedback state in the preview.

Two competing theme systems. The per-Portal Theme presets (creation form, Settings, list swatch) are fully overridden at publication by the Property Brand Profile colours (AccountAdmin only), so that UI is effectively dead for guests. There are also three 'description' fields (portal, property fallback per locale, override per locale) and two 'names'.

No 'publish changes' while live. A published portal's toggle only offers 'Disable public page'. Pushing saved changes requires disable then publish, which briefly takes the portal offline for guests. The rollback server fn exists without UI, and history is read-only.

Publishing prerequisites are scattered and partly admin-only. The link must be issued on the Share tab first; a responsible manager must exist; Google must be verified; brand colours and every locale's Property content need an AccountAdmin, so a Property Manager can be blocked with no guided checklist.

Public addresses are shown once. The QR/NFC URL cannot be re-displayed or re-downloaded without rotating, which is hostile to print workflows. There are no print templates (table tent or card), no placement/channel naming, and no QR styling.

Secondary links are not localized even though EN/BG is offered. iconKey is unused. Links whose destination is unapproved or lapsed are silently dropped from the published and public page. Links appear only after rating; showing them from arrival changes a pinned e2e expectation and should be reconciled with ADR 0044/BETA wording.

ADR 0044 (2026-07-15) says the review link is the touchpoint and private rating optional. BETA.md and the Portal/Guest CONTEXT say rating-first then Google. Code is rating-first. Designs must follow current BETA/CONTEXT and not silently resolve the ADR wording.

No photography or logo in beta. logoUrl, defaultHeroImageUrl and override hero are forced null and upload is safety-blocked (SAFE-01). Share previews therefore have no og:image. Signature Stay's architectural photo is future scope and needs a typographic no-photo variant as the shipping default. The organization logo upload exists in Identity but is not wired to portals.

Typography and privacy. The guest page inherits Satoshi from api.fontshare.com (a third-party request on a no-tracker guest page). Satoshi is most likely Latin-only, so Bulgarian falls back to other fonts (verify). Any premium serif or sans must ship Cyrillic and be self-hosted or on Google Fonts within the CSP.

App theme leaks into the guest page. THEME_INIT_SCRIPT applies .dark from the OS preference on /p routes. shadcn Button outline (bg-background, dark:bg-input/30), Textarea (border-input), the border-border card edges, the bg-muted skeleton, text-destructive errors and the analytics notice (bg-background) all use app tokens, not --portal-*. A dark-mode phone gets mixed palettes.

Primary colour is used as text (link headings) and as borders with no contrast floor against the background. Brand validation checks only text/background ≥4.5:1. Presets or palettes in a redesign need contrast rules per role.

Deadlines ('available until …') are rendered in UTC with no zone label, three hours off for Bulgarian guests. The receipt stacks three deadline sentences and four bordered boxes, and response withdrawal has no confirmation.
After a full withdrawal the guest sees only 'Your response was withdrawn'. There are no secondary links and no 'start a new response' on a shared device.

The privacy notice and PortalUnavailable are English-only. PortalUnavailable is also unstyled app chrome. It must stay non-identifying, but it can be calmer and bilingual via Accept-Language without revealing the portal.

Language-pack immutability. Any new guest copy means new pack versions (guest-ui-en-v2/bg-v2) plus type, constant and publication-check updates. Existing live snapshots keep v1 copy until each portal is republished, and many e2e strings are pinned.
The analytics disclosure bar is fixed to the bottom on first visit and can cover the rating CTA on small phones. Its dismissal is stored in localStorage and it is app-styled.

Admin information architecture. Settings is one long page mixing Property-wide (AccountAdmin) and portal-local scopes, with 6+ separate save buttons, nested bordered boxes and explanatory paragraphs. This contradicts the inbox rules of one primary per area, facts vs controls, and hairlines not boxes. The list page has no health, metrics, group, owner or live-version columns, and groups sit in a detached section.

Analytics: provenance-heavy (evidence, reconciliation revision, integrity) against dashboard rule 8 (availability by exception). Range model and default differ from the dashboard. Vocabulary ('Feedback', 'Review Clicks') differs from the dashboard's 'Portal scans / Private feedback'. There is no Property- or Group-level portal analytics, no health monitoring surface, and no link-selection or channel breakdown. 'Review Clicks' must never be presented as 'reviews written'.

Stale or misleading admin copy. The slug editor warns that hand-typed slug URLs will break, but no slug route exists (URLs are /p/{token}). The organization identity card says org-slug changes break guest portal URLs. The link-tree empty state suggests a 'Review sites' category, which invites multi-platform review solicitation.

Ratestar reference patterns that conflict with the rules: public platforms before any private step, pre-filled 5-star 'Rate us' cards, emoji as UI, and a crowded hierarchy. Keep the learnable parts: strong property identity, a full-bleed atmosphere, and useful link cards.

Tooling note for the later visual phase: the Figma MCP server needs authorization (claude.ai connector settings or /mcp in an interactive session), and the claude-flow MCP server failed to connect this session. Neither was needed for this read-only mapping.

competitors.name: Ratestar Digital Portal: immersive dark template (live: InterContinental Sofia, Therma Numera, Restaurant DOBRO; vendor video: Maxi Park Hotel & Spa)
competitors.category: Direct competitor (BG/EU): review gateway plus link hub for hospitality
competitors.guestFlow: The guest arrives from an NFC card, QR code or link. Cards use a short route, /r/[code] (seen in the x-matched-path header), and portals live at ratestar.io/{en|bg}/{slug}. Robots is set to 'follow, index', so the portals are publicly indexable. There is no private step on the page itself: it is one long scroll. The review CTAs come right after the identity block. Where a CTA goes depends on the property. InterContinental: the Google card opens a Ratestar form (ratestar.io/intercontinental-sofia/forms/RKOss), but the Tripadvisor card goes straight to tripadvisor.com/UserReviewEdit. Therma Numera: Google goes through a form (/forms/VWziK), Tripadvisor goes direct. DOBRO: both cards go through Ratestar forms. So the flow the guest meets under a 'Google Reviews' label differs by property and by platform. After the CTAs come secondary blocks: booking, spa, menu, an award vote, a promo discount, a map with directions, and contact. There is no completion state on the portal. Language: a floating white flag pill sits top-right. Switching /en vs /bg changes only the UI chrome. DOBRO under /en still shows all-Bulgarian content. Therma Numera under /bg shows English content with Bulgarian map strings ('Хотел', 'Упътване'). The result is mixed-language pages. I opened no live-business form and clicked no CTA.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Measured at 375x812 and 390x844. (1) An autoplay background video covers the full viewport; the hero area is about 480px tall. The flag pill (about 64x40, white, rounded, flag and chevron) is fixed top-right. (2) The name is centred H1, Montserrat 24px/600, white, followed by a blue 'verified' seal. (3) Below it come a tagline or address, phone (dotted underline) and emoji-led lines ('📍 София, ул. ...', '☎️ За резервации', '⛲ Longevity SPA'). (4) A row of 3–4 outline social icons, 24px each (website, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok). (5) Two side-by-side platform cards at y≈504, 156–163 x 120px, radius about 16px. Each has a photo background, the platform logo in the top-right corner, a centred label ('Google Reviews' / 'Tripadvisor') and a subline that is either 'Leave us a review' or five gold emoji stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️. Their top edge sits above the fold. (6) A centred one-line thank-you ('We value every review – it inspires us to make your next stay even better!'), placed above or below the cards. (7) Full-width photo link cards, 375x240, rounded, with a link glyph top-right and a centred title and subtitle ('Book your stay / The ideal room for concentration and relaxation'). Therma uses a 390x240 'Reservations' card plus two 163x120 half cards. (8) Full-bleed promo images (a 409px 'MICHELIN 2025' poster). (9) A blue-gradient pill, 375x70: 'Luxury Hotel Awards 🗳️ VOTE FOR INTERCONTINTENTAL SOFIA 🗳️', typo included. (10) An embedded Google Map in dark style (about 500px, with an expand icon); Maxi Park's version has an info popover with photo, emoji award lines and a 'Directions' button. (11) 'Contact:' block with phone, email and address, centred. (12) 'Powered by ratestar' footer, 40px. Total height is 1,065–2,193px. The Maxi Park demo video adds five stacked 240px cards: Book a room / Restaurants and bars / Spa and Wellness Center / Events and conference rooms / Activities.
competitors.visualStyle: Pure black ground behind moving video. One geometric sans for everything: Montserrat, H1 24/600, body 16/400. The text is white and almost all of it is centred. Photo cards with 16–20px radii. Emoji serve as the icon system (📍☎️⛲🗳️👉🍖♨️🔥), with gold emoji stars and a blue verification seal. It reads as dense, promotional and nightclub-like rather than quiet luxury. Cards whose images fail to load show as black boxes with tiny logos; I saw this on Therma Numera. No privacy or data notice appears on the portal page itself.
standoutIdeas: 'Same QR, new content, no reprints': blocks can be edited without reprinting codes. This matches RepKey's stable-token model.
The review action sits directly under identity and is above the fold at 375x812, even on a long hub page.
Photo-backed half-width destination cards make the public-review choice feel tangible and give it a premium feel.
Map plus 'Directions' and a contact block at the end make the page useful after the review moment.
The fixed language pill is always reachable, top-right.
One template serves 5-star hotels (InterContinental, IHG), spas and grill restaurants. In the BG market, the bar for 'premium' is set by this template.
antiPatterns: Five filled gold stars inside the 'Google Reviews'/'Tripadvisor' CTAs (and on the Maxi Park demo) prime a 5-star answer before the guest has rated.
A self-issued blue 'verified' seal next to the property name imitates platform verification and has no stated meaning.

The CTA says 'Google Reviews', but for some properties it opens a Ratestar rating form. The label doesn't say what happens next, and platforms are routed inconsistently (Google via a form, Tripadvisor direct).
The language switch only swaps the chrome. Content stays in one language, which gives /en pages in Bulgarian and /bg pages in English.
Heavy autoplay mp4 hero and background, served from Supabase storage. This costs LCP and data on hotel Wi-Fi and roaming.
Emoji used as UI icons and as decoration ('𓌉◯𓇋', '🍖♨️🔥🥩🥓🍳🍰🍔🍕').
Off-mission blocks (an award-vote CTA, a '10% discount' promo) compete with the review moment.
There is no designed no-photo state. Failed images leave black boxes.
Almost all text is centred, and there is no visible privacy notice on the portal.
competitors.adminBuilder: This comes from vendor pages. Portals are built from blocks, with '50+ integrations'. Block types appear in the public JS bundle: Google, Tripadvisor, Booking, HolidayCheck, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Wifi, Url, Email, Phone, Contact, Events, Ticket, plus Menu, Reservations, Promotions, Images and Directions. The vendor offers industry templates (12 verticals listed), one portal per location, and a unique card or QR per employee, table, room or campaign. Its claims include 'Editable anytime', 'Ready to use immediately. The main blocks are set up in minutes', and 'most clients live within 7 days'. Pricing is quote-only, in three tiers. Starter: NFC/QR, branded portal, forms, smart feedback routing, Google + Tripadvisor sync, 1 user. Growth adds Scratch + Wheel of Fortune gamification, email/SMS autopilot, Booking/Yelp/Facebook/HolidayCheck and 5 users. Enterprise adds a multi-location dashboard, SSO and an API.
competitors.analytics: Vendor pages: 'Views, Clicks, Reviews, CTR'. 'Reviews per card', e.g. '#0001 - Reception'. 'Clicks per block' across Google, Tripadvisor, Menu, Facebook, Instagram, Booking, Directions and Contact. A multi-location table with 30-day deltas and a team leaderboard (reviews tied to roles, shifts or staff). Date ranges of last 30 days, quarter or custom. Daily, weekly and monthly email digests with AI summary cards. Negative-feedback alert emails at a configurable threshold ('3 stars or lower') with a recipient list. 'Reviews' are attributed from taps and clicks, not verified reviews. The case-studies page shows 'Live' counters (6,545+ reviews collected, 113+ locations) and per-client 'Google / Maps / ChatGPT visibility %' claims. These are vendor claims.
competitors.compliance: The FAQ says: 'Customers always retain the option to leave a public review on any platform - we don't block or filter access' and 'we don't gate'. The hotels page says: 'A public review invite for every guest, with no rating filter'. The public JS bundle, however, shows configurable threshold routing (see the Ratestar feedback form entry). Gamification (scratch card, wheel of fortune, prizes like 'Free dessert', '€20 voucher') ships with the disclaimer 'not to buy or influence positive reviews'. Staff leaderboards and bonuses are promoted. The vendor claims EU hosting and a DPA.

competitors.category: Direct competitor template variant (Linktree-style)

The first button, 'Review us on Google ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️', links straight to search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=…. There is no rating step and no private option, so this template skips Ratestar's own feedback form entirely. Ratestar's own portal instead routes 'Review us on Google' through ratestar.io/ratestar/forms/wNLDY. The other buttons open Instagram, Facebook, the website and tel:.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: At 390x844. (1) Cover photo, full width, about 220px tall. (2) Circular logo, about 130px, white ring, overlapping the bottom-left of the cover. Ratestar's own version puts the social icons to the right of the avatar. (3) Left-aligned name, Montserrat about 26/600, with the blue verified seal. (4) Intro copy left-aligned, 16px, with emoji ('👉 Reservations: 📞 +359 …'). (5) Stack of full-width buttons with 16px side gutters and about 16px radius. The first is 'Review us on Google' over emoji stars, 70px tall. Then four 50px buttons: '👉 Instagram', '👉 Facebook', '🌐 Website', '📞 Call Us'. Alpen uses tan buttons on black; Ratestar's own uses black pill buttons on white. (6) 'Powered by ratestar' footer.
competitors.visualStyle: Linktree-like, with a Google-profile header (cover plus overlapping avatar). One brand-tinted fill colour for every button, Montserrat throughout, and emoji as icons. standoutIdeas: The cover plus overlapping avatar gives instant recognition with only a logo and one photo.
The whole portal fits on one phone screen.
antiPatterns: The review button is styled exactly like the 'Instagram' and 'Call Us' buttons, so the review moment has no hierarchy.
The direct Google link skips any private channel. Signed-out guests land on Google's sign-in page (see the Google entry).
Emoji-pointer copy ('👉') and emoji stars inside the CTA.
competitors.adminBuilder: The same block editor as the immersive template. Template choice appears to change the layout skin, not the content model (inferred).
competitors.analytics: Same as the immersive template (clicks per block).

competitors.name: Ratestar feedback form and routing (the step behind 'Google Reviews')
competitors.category: Direct competitor: private rating form and redirect logic
competitors.guestFlow: I viewed the form only on Ratestar's own portal, never on a client's, and did not tap a star. The observed first screen asks 'How would you rate your experience? *'. Everything after that comes from the vendor mock and from reading the shipped JS; I did not exercise it. The vendor mock shows 'What could we improve?' with a textarea ('Your opinion matters to us') and a black full-width 'Submit'. Next comes 'Thank you for your feedback 🙏 Please take a moment to leave us a review on one of the sites below', with bordered rows 'Review us on Google', 'Review us on TripAdvisor' and 'Write a review'. The shipped page bundle (page-7064e2f86527b425.js) does the following. When a Rating or EmojiRating field changes, and the rating is greater than nrpThreshold (default 3) and a redirect block is configured, it POSTs to a track_click API. It can mark an email or SMS 'review_campaign' request as 'converted'. Then setTimeout(200ms) sets window.location.href to the platform URL. So 4–5★ jump straight to Google, while 1–3★ stay for private questions. On submit it fires a 200-particle teal confetti burst and shows a thank-you title and subtitle. It shows an 'externalReviewInvite' only if the invite is enabled and some rating is at or above invite.minRating, where the allowed values are [3,4,5]. With the invite enabled, 1–2★ guests never see the public-review invite. A 'requirePersonalData' config handles contact capture. The page sends a device_id and handles HTTP 429. While the form is open it calls history.pushState and re-pushes state on popstate, which traps the back button.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: At 390x844. (1) A grey header band about 160px tall, showing a desaturated or blurred cover of the logo. A small translucent pill reads 'Customer feedback', with the name in white 24/600 and the verified seal below it. (2) A white sheet with a rounded top overlaps the band. (3) A large empty area, then a centred question at 16px with a red required asterisk. (4) Five outline star buttons, 52x52 each, 4px gaps, centred (x 50–326 at 375w), with aria-labels '1 star' … '5 stars'. There are no verbal labels. (5) Another large empty area. (6) A bottom footnote: '💡 98% of customers trust online reviews. Help others by leaving a feedback.' (7) 'Powered by ratestar'. Light mode is white; the bundle also has a dark (neutral-900) variant.
competitors.visualStyle: Generic shadcn/Tailwind form (rounded-full radios, the 'ring-offset-background' classes), Montserrat, grey and white, with little brand expression. The emoji tip line reads as persuasion copy.
standoutIdeas: One question per screen with large 52px targets.
The header band plus overlapping sheet keeps the property's identity on the form.
antiPatterns: Threshold auto-redirect (more than 3★ goes to the platform after 200ms) is score-dependent routing, even though the marketing says 'we don't gate'.
The public-review invite after feedback can be restricted to ratings of 3★ or more.
Back-button trap using history.pushState and popstate.
Celebratory confetti after a complaint as well as after praise.
A '98% of customers trust online reviews' nudge at the moment of rating.
A 'converted' review request is recorded on click. The click is treated as a review.
Device fingerprinting (device_id) for 'honest' leaderboard counts.
No verbal anchors on the stars; the only label text is the required asterisk.
competitors.adminBuilder: Vendor pages: 'Custom forms & surveys' with a rating or satisfaction score, 'What went wrong' categories (service, waiting time, cleanliness, food, room), open comment, 'Optional contact details' and auto-captured 'Visit context' (location, shift, campaign). Alert settings: 'Notify me when a rating is 3 stars or lower' plus recipients. Case states are Detected, Assigned, Follow-up, Resolved and Insight captured. The gamification panel covers active or paused, campaign type, device participation limits, reward outcomes and 'Preview before launch'.
competitors.analytics: Feedback feeds the same reporting layer, with topic and sentiment by location. Internal feedback becomes cases with owners.
competitors.compliance: Google Maps policy prohibits merchants from choosing to 'Discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers'. Ratestar's configurable nrpThreshold redirect and invite minRating let a customer set up exactly that selective routing. The vendor says customers 'always retain the option'. For RepKey this is the clearest point of contrast: offer an equal public destination for every rating and never auto-redirect.

competitors.name: Grade.us review funnel (vendor's own live funnel)
competitors.category: White-label review funnel (agency tool, US)
competitors.guestFlow: This profile has no rating step. The guest sees the invitation and picks a platform tile straight away. Each tile carries a label that says in advance whether login is needed. The vendor says funnels can also start with a branded 'stars/faces/thumbs' question and offer 'a variety of segmented layouts that provide customers a seamless path to the review sites of your choice'. I could not read the help article that describes what happens after a negative answer.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: At 375x812. (1) A white header: grey light 16px line 'Help us. Help others. You're invited to review:' then the business name as a huge bold blue wordmark (about 48px), then a hairline divider. (2) A light-grey (#ececec) body. (3) Four full-width rounded (about 20px) bordered tiles, about 68px tall, containing only platform logos: facebook, yp, Citysearch, judy's book. Under the YP and Citysearch tiles hangs a white strip, 'Login w/ [f]'. Under judy's book is a green 'NO LOGIN REQUIRED' pill. (4) Roughly 45% of the screen is empty below. The page title is 'gradeus | Review Us'. GTM and New Relic trackers load on the page.
competitors.visualStyle: Dated 2013-era utility: logo tiles, default system typography, one blue accent, no imagery. The vendor's 2019 re-skin added an optional 1024x138 header banner and a hex brand colour.
standoutIdeas: Friction labels on each destination ('Login w/ Facebook', 'NO LOGIN REQUIRED') set honest expectations before the handoff. It is the only vendor I saw doing this.
The 'Help us. Help others.' framing is brief and puts other travellers first.
antiPatterns: Its platform list has gone stale: it still offers Citysearch and judy's book. An unmaintained destination list erodes trust.
Logos only, with no hierarchy and no primary destination.
Third-party trackers (GTM, New Relic) on a consumer review page.
competitors.adminBuilder: From the vendor blog: brand colour picker, header image (1024x138, 450KB or less, PNG/JPG/GIF), rating-control styling, choice of review sites, white-label logo for agencies, widgets, invites (email, SMS, QR, website button).
competitors.analytics: Reviews monitored on Google, Facebook and 100+ sites; alerts on new reviews; reporting section. The funnel's dataLayer exposes recipients, reviews over 7, 30 and all-time, and average rating.

competitors.name: Birdeye (public review microsite and review-request landing pages)
competitors.category: US reputation platform (multi-location, 150–200+ sites)
competitors.guestFlow: Two surfaces. (a) The public microsite is observed live, on an unclaimed hotel profile. The primary button is 'Write a review'; the button carries no href, so I did not follow it. The kiosk 'Write a review' page is documented in the help centre: the guest rates 1–5 stars, taps 'Next', writes a text and taps 'Submit'. The result is a 'Birdeye certified review' hosted by Birdeye, not a Google review. (b) Review request email and landing, from the help centre: a branded header, heading (130 characters max) and message, and up to four review-site buttons that the admin reorders by drag and drop. A 'Contact us directly' path goes to a customizable Feedback page with an optional callback request, then a Thank-you page. Third-party descriptions say Birdeye also had a 'sentiment check' that routes dissatisfied customers to private feedback.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Microsite at 375x812. Birdeye header (logo, search, hamburger). A stock hospitality photo banner, about 150px. A breadcrumb (Byron Bay, NSW > Hospitality > name). A red 'Claim this profile' pill. H1 in Poppins 36px over two lines. '4.0 ★★★★☆ 1,134 reviews' with the count underlined. 'Open • Closes 12:00 a.m. tomorrow', category and city. A full-width blue '☆ Write a review' button, about 46px, radius 8px. Three square outline quick-action tiles with labels below: Call, Directions, Website. Then About and Reviews tabs.
competitors.visualStyle: Google Business Profile clone: white, Poppins, orange stars, one blue primary button, outline icon tiles. Clear but generic, with no property expression.
standoutIdeas: One unmistakable primary action, followed by a row of three equal utility actions (Call, Directions, Website). This is a clean model for 'review gateway first, link tree second'.
Review-site buttons are capped at four and ordered by the admin.
A separate 'Contact us directly' path sits beside the public sites rather than replacing them.
antiPatterns: 'Write a review' collects a first-party review on the vendor's own site, which can be confused with a public platform review.
Private-feedback routing based on a sentiment check (third-party claim) is gating-adjacent.
Stock imagery that doesn't belong to the business.
competitors.adminBuilder: The email or landing template has sections for General, Header branding, Review request email, Feedback page and Thank-you page. Site buttons are reordered by drag and drop. A callback option exists. Branding can be set per location.
competitors.analytics: Review reports and a 'Review NPS' report over time and by location; AI sentiment summaries; monthly reports. Vendor testimonials claim review increases, e.g. '+200%'.

competitors.name: Trustpilot evaluate page
competitors.category: Public review platform destination (write-review entry)
competitors.guestFlow: The page is a single question. Tapping a tile starts the review; I did not tap. From general knowledge (inferred, not observed this session), the tiles then fill with a colour graded from red for 1 to green for 5, a text, title and date form follows, and posting requires sign-in.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: At 375x812. (1) A near-black header about 56px tall with the Trustpilot logo. (2) A rounded beige card: a 66px screenshot thumbnail of the business site, the name at 16px/575 ('Premier Inn') and the domain below. (3) About 110px of whitespace. (4) The question 'How would you rate your experience?' at about 28px, Trustpilot Sans. (5) Five grey square star tiles, each about 49x46 with 2px gaps. They are radio inputs with accessible names '1 star: Bad', '2 stars: Poor', '3 stars: Average', '4 stars: Great' and '5 stars: Excellent'. (6) A reCAPTCHA and device-signal notice with a Privacy Policy link. Nothing else on the screen.
competitors.visualStyle: Stark and utilitarian: black header, beige identity card, big sans question, flat square tiles, lots of white space.
standoutIdeas: Each star position has a verbal anchor (Bad, Poor, Average, Great, Excellent). RepKey should show these visibly, not only in the accessible name.
The whole first screen is one question with no competing links.
Placing the privacy note right at the point of action.
antiPatterns: The only body copy is a bot-protection disclosure.
No language choice, and the business has no voice on the page.
competitors.compliance: Trustpilot owns the page. The business cannot alter its flow.

competitors.name: Tripadvisor write-a-review form (destination behind Ratestar's Tripadvisor cards)
competitors.category: Public review platform destination
competitors.guestFlow: The whole form renders for a signed-out visitor on one long page, and ends in 'Continue'. I infer the sign-in comes after 'Continue'; I entered nothing and did not tap it. It is the same deep link that Ratestar portals use directly.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: At 375 wide. (1) Tripadvisor header: menu, logo, download, AI, trips and search icons. (2) A bordered place card: a 66px thumbnail, 'Maxi Park Hotel & Spa', street and city. (3) 'How would you rate your experience?' in bold, with five outline green bubbles of about 40px (aria '1 of 5 bubbles' … '5 of 5 bubbles'). (4) 'When did you go?' as a pill dropdown prefilled 'September 2026'. (5) 'Who did you go with?' as chips: Business, Couples, Family, Friends, Solo. (6) 'Write your review' with a textarea ('Share your experience…') and aspect-prompt chips: Location, Atmosphere, Rooms, Value, Cleanliness, Noise level, Service, Amenities. A 'Help me write' AI helper and a '0/25 min' counter follow. (7) 'Title your review'. (8) 'Add some photos (Optional)'. (9) A long certification paragraph: own experience, no relationship, no incentive, 'zero-tolerance policy on fake reviews'. (10) A 'Continue' button. Type is Trip Sans VF 16px.
competitors.visualStyle: Tripadvisor green and black on white; a friendly rounded sans; bubbles instead of stars; chips everywhere.
standoutIdeas: Aspect chips (Rooms, Service, Cleanliness…) cure the blank-textarea problem. This pattern is useful for RepKey's optional private note.
Visible trip context (when, with whom) makes the review concrete.
Honest certification copy about incentives.
antiPatterns: A long multi-field page after a one-tap CTA. Guests from a portal meet far more work than the CTA promised.
An AI 'Help me write' on a first-person review.

competitors.name: Google write-review link (search.google.com/local/writereview) and Google policy
competitors.category: Primary public destination (RepKey's Google Review Action target)
competitors.guestFlow: On a signed-out mobile browser, the write-review link immediately redirected to the Google Accounts 'Sign in' page: Google G, 'Sign in', 'Use your Google Account', an 'Email or phone' field, 'Forgot email?', a Guest-mode note, 'Create account' and 'Next'. The guest never sees stars until signing in. Signed-in guests, or guests handed off to the Maps app, get Google's own review sheet (stars, text, photos); this part is inferred and was not observed this session. Ratestar's Alpen portal uses exactly this URL.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Signed-out result at 375x812: the Google sign-in page. Google logo top-left, a 'Sign in' heading of about 32px, a 56px outlined input, a text link and a pill 'Next' button bottom-right. Language picker and Help, Privacy and Terms are in the footer.
competitors.visualStyle: Google Material sign-in: white, blue primary, generous spacing.
standoutIdeas: RepKey's after-rating Google action should set expectations ('Google may ask you to sign in') and show which Google account posts publicly. Nothing else in this set does, except Grade.us's login labels.
Google itself recommends sharing a review link or QR code, so a portal is a legitimate channel.
antiPatterns: A login wall straight after 'Rate us on Google' is the biggest hidden drop-off in every competitor flow. None of the vendors warns about it.
competitors.compliance: Google Maps policy prohibits merchants from choosing to 'Discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers' and from choosing to 'Offer incentives – such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services - in exchange for posting any review'. The Business Profile help centre says incentives are 'strictly prohibited'.

crossCuttingPatterns: Every vendor page is the same vertical stack: identity (cover photo or video, logo, name, verification mark) → review CTAs → secondary links → map and contact → a 'Powered by' footer. This is 'review gateway first, link tree second', but without a designed completion state.

Destinations converge on one question, with near-identical wording on Trustpilot, Tripadvisor and Ratestar's form: 'How would you rate your experience?' over five equal controls. Only Trustpilot attaches verbal anchors (Bad → Excellent), and only in the accessible names. Visible anchors plus BG and EN copy would set RepKey apart.

Photography is assumed everywhere: video heroes, photo cards, stock banners. None of the vendors has a designed no-photo state. Failed images show as black boxes on Ratestar. A typographic or no-photo RepKey design has open space in this market.

Downstream login walls are universal (Google redirects to sign-in, Tripadvisor ends in 'Continue', and Trustpilot requires sign-in, inferred), yet only Grade.us labels the friction before the handoff. RepKey's Google action copy should say it opens Google and that Google may ask the guest to sign in.

Five filled stars inside public-platform CTAs (Ratestar) and persuasion footnotes ('98% of customers trust online reviews') are common priming devices. They clash with a no-gating, no-pressure position.

Languages are handled as a UI-chrome toggle only (a Ratestar flag pill). Property content stays in one language, which gives mixed EN and BG pages. Per-content translation with a preview of missing strings would be a real differentiator for BG guests.

Marketing says 'we don't gate', while product configurations allow score thresholds, auto-redirecting 4–5★ and invites limited to 3★ or more. Trustworthy, equal routing can be a selling point, provided it is shown in the UI rather than just claimed.

Analytics converge on the funnel Views → Clicks → Reviews → CTR, broken down per card, location and staff member, with leaderboards and threshold alerts (3★ or less). Competitors count a click as a 'review' or 'conversion'. RepKey's honest 'Google destination selected' metric needs a clear label in the admin UI, not an inflated 'reviews' number.

Admin models converge on a block editor with 'same QR, new content', per-location portals, a card or QR per placement, and alert recipients. Reordering review-site buttons with a cap of about four (Birdeye) is common.
Density and emoji-as-icons are standard in the BG market (Ratestar clients, including the IHG 5-star InterContinental Sofia). A calm, typographic, well-translated page would stand out in this market.
surprises: The owner's reference screenshot is Ratestar's own marketing demo: Maxi Park Hotel & Spa, Velingrad, from www.ratestar.io/digital-portal/mockup-website-en.mp4 (608x1330, 23.6s). The same video is reused on the hotel, restaurant and beauty solution pages, which suggests one flagship template.

Ratestar portals are public and indexable (robots 'follow, index') at ratestar.io/{en|bg}/{slug}. I found live slugs by probing the /[locale]/[slug] route: intercontinental-sofia, thermanumera, dobro, alpen-bansko, namoos-maxi, restaurant-svetla and ratestar. Card taps use a separate /r/[code] route. The owner may want these as benchmarks.

Ratestar's shipped form code auto-redirects ratings above nrpThreshold (default 3) to the platform after 200ms. It can limit the post-feedback public invite to ratings of 3★ or more (invite.minRating 3/4/5), traps the back button with history.pushState, fires confetti on every submit, and marks review-request campaigns 'converted' on click. This contradicts its 'we don't gate' FAQ. The evidence is inferred from reading the public JS bundle, not from exercising a live flow.

Ratestar's 'Google Reviews' label opens different things on different portals: a Ratestar rating form for InterContinental, Therma Numera and DOBRO, but a direct Google write-review link for Alpen. Tripadvisor is sometimes direct and sometimes via a form.
Visiting Google's write-review link signed out goes straight to the Google sign-in page. Many guests' first screen after 'Rate us on Google' is a login wall.

Ratestar's live 5-star client pages include a visible typo ('INTERCONTINTENTAL') and an award-voting CTA, and the language pill swaps only the UI chrome (Bulgarian content on /en). The polish bar in this market is lower than the marketing implies.
Ratestar sells Scratch Card / Wheel of Fortune gamification with prizes (on Growth), staff review leaderboards with bonuses, and device fingerprinting. RepKey permanently denies all of these.

Tooling notes. The session's WebSearch budget (200) ran out partway through, so I did not reach live Podium, GatherUp or NiceJob pages; their entries would rely on vendor claims only, so I left them out. When I opened the shared browser, the existing tab had already been navigated to trustpilot.com/evaluate/www.example.com with a 375x812 emulation I had not set, so another agent may have been using the browser at the same time. I then worked in my own tab (tab-2) and reset it to desktop at the end.

competitors.name: Trustpilot (evaluate / invitation review form)
competitors.category: Public review platform; invitation-link review form
competitors.guestFlow: Observed at 375px on the evaluate page. The first screen asks one question with a 1-5 star scale. Each star is a radio input with a word label read to screen readers: Bad, Poor, Average, Great, Excellent. Choosing a star opens the written-review form. That step was not entered because the research was read-only. Vendor docs describe invitation links: unique encrypted evaluate-link URLs, an embedded review form in checkout that needs no sign-in, and reviews labelled 'Invited'.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: 1) A near-black header bar, about 72px tall, with the green-star Trustpilot wordmark. 2) A rounded warm-grey card (radius about 16px, about 88px tall) holding a small screenshot thumbnail of the business site, the business name and the domain. It confirms which business you are rating. 3) About 150px of empty space. 4) The heading 'How would you rate your experience?', left-aligned, about 28px, bold, dark geometric sans, on two lines. 5) Five square star tiles (about 46px, 4px gaps, lavender-grey with white stars), left-aligned. On hover or selection the tiles fill with a colour for the score: 1 star is red-orange and 4 stars is light green. 6) Grey small print saying reCAPTCHA collects device and interaction signals, with a Privacy Policy link. The lower 40% of the screen is empty. On first load a cookie dialog ('Here's how we use cookies', with Manage / Reject all / Accept all) covers the page before any rating.
competitors.visualStyle: Utilitarian platform brand: a black bar, white page, one warm-grey card and a custom geometric sans. Colour appears only in the stars, where it encodes the score (red to green). It shows no business branding beyond a site thumbnail and looks institutional rather than hospitable.
standoutIdeas: The first screen does exactly one thing: one question and five large, unselected targets. That matches RepKey's rating-first core.
Each star has a word label (Bad / Poor / Average / Great / Excellent) exposed to assistive tech. RepKey should use translated EN/BG labels and show the chosen word visibly after selection.
A business-identity confirmation card sits above the question, so the guest knows which place they are rating. This is useful for portal groups, for example 'Spa, Hotel X'.
Invitation templates in 16 languages (vendor page) are a benchmark for EN/BG template quality.
Unique invitation links let a review be labelled 'invited', which is a transparency signal.
antiPatterns: A cookie wall appears before the core task, and the only secondary copy is a security/tracking notice (reCAPTCHA device signals). RepKey's no-cookie, no-tracker posture can show no banner at all, which is a visible premium difference.
The stars turn red at 1 and green at 4-5. The red reads as judgemental; a single brand accent (e.g. champagne) is gentler for private hospitality feedback.
The left-aligned question with large empty areas above and below makes an awkward phone composition.
competitors.adminBuilder: Invitation templates (16 languages), automatic invitations via integrations, a company API link, unique links and an embedded review form. Vendor claims reminder emails add about 35% more reviews (a claim, not evidence).
competitors.analytics: Not observed. The vendor page focuses on invitation volume and reminders.
competitors.compliance: Trustpilot is the public destination, so there is no private branch. Any business can be rated by anyone who follows the link.

competitors.name: Podium (review invite pages)
competitors.category: SMS-first messaging and review-invite SaaS
competitors.guestFlow: Reconstructed from the live app's route manifest and English locale file, since opening a real invite needs a personal uid. The routes are /invites/$uid, then /sites (platform list), then /sites.$site, then /feedback.$site. The guest sees a header saying the location has invited them to review. A preselected site comes next: 'Submit your review on [site], or select a different review site', with a primary 'Continue with [site]' (Google by default per vendor docs), a secondary 'Select a different site', and 'Text your feedback instead', which is a private SMS channel. There is no rating step, so every recipient gets the same public options. Returning from the site shows 'Thanks for your review of [location]', followed by a promotional-texts sign-up card and a Podium advert for business owners. The error states still send the guest to Google, for example when an invite is not found.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Only the loading shell rendered without a uid: a pale grey gradient band, about 250px, with a centred Podium logo over a white page. Screen order from the routes: an invite header, one recommended platform button, a 'different site' link, a private 'text your feedback' option, then a thank-you with promo opt-in and vendor ad.
competitors.visualStyle: Light, neutral SaaS shell with vendor logo in the hero band. The platform brand dominates rather than the business.
standoutIdeas: One recommended destination with an escape hatch to others. For RepKey, Google is the only public action, so it can be one confident button.
A private alternative is offered in the same screen as the public action and is never a replacement for it. This matches RepKey's 'additionally offered' private feedback.
Graceful error copy that still gives a way forward (go straight to Google). RepKey's stale-destination state needs the equivalent: gentle copy plus private feedback, never a dead end.
A regulated-industry disclaimer (healthcare) shows how legal notes can sit at the action rather than in a policy page.
antiPatterns: The thank-you page asserts 'Thanks for your review' although the vendor cannot know a review was written. RepKey must never claim this; it should say it opened Google for the guest.
The completion state is used for monetisation: an SMS promo opt-in plus a 'Run your own business?' vendor advert on the business's own guest page.
Personal-data collection (phone number for promos) at the end of a review journey.
competitors.adminBuilder: Invites are sent from the inbox (a star icon generates a link); the default site is Google, with many alternative sites available.
competitors.analytics: An invite list in Analytics shows who followed the link and who left a review as green checks (third-party / search summary). Review attribution is inferred by matching.
competitors.compliance: No rating gate: all recipients see the same platform choices.

competitors.name: NiceJob (review microsite + review modal)
competitors.category: SMB review-automation SaaS (home services)
competitors.guestFlow: On the business microsite, tapping 'Leave us a review' (five empty stars) opens a modal. It shows the business name, a line asking guests who like the business to tell others, and a list of review sites: Google as an elevated white card with a logo and chevron, G2 as a plain row, a divider, then 'Other review site options'. No rating is required first. The help centre says invite links lead to a review-site list (Google, Facebook, NiceJob first-party). Admins toggle each site, and the first-party option serves customers without Google accounts.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Observed at 375px, top to bottom. 1) A small logo top-left. 2) Business name as H1, about 28px bold. 3) Grey location line. 4) A large '4.9' plus five gold stars. 5) A row of per-platform scores with small grey icons: Google 4.9, G2 4.8, Facebook 4.8. 6) An outline blue 'Learn more' pill. 7) A white card saying the business has an overall 4.9 from 4263 customers. 8) The 'Leave us a review' heading with five grey stars, at about y=610, near the fold. 9) Carousel dots, then a review feed (initial avatars, names, dates, truncated text with 'More'). 10) A 'Get connected' contact block. 11) A floating 'Powered by NiceJob' badge bottom-right.
competitors.visualStyle: Generic light-grey SaaS microsite: Roboto-like sans, gold stars, blue outline buttons and white cards with soft shadows. The layout puts social proof first.
standoutIdeas: The platform list uses rows with real logos and chevrons. The primary option is lifted with a shadow, so the hierarchy is clear without clutter.
A first-party option for people without a Google account parallels RepKey's private rating and feedback, which needs no account.
Admins can walk their own invite link to experience the customer journey, a preview-as-guest idea.
antiPatterns: The modal copy is conditional ('Like X? Let others know!'), which frames the public ask for happy customers only. It is soft gating by wording.
The aggregate score and a wall of 5-star reviews appear before the ask, which anchors the guest's rating.
Third-party trackers load on the review page: Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and the Facebook SDK were seen in network requests.
A vendor 'Powered by' badge floats over content, and an 'Are you a business owner?' upsell appears.
competitors.adminBuilder: Settings > Product Settings > Review Sites, with toggles to show or hide each platform. Review invites are sent automatically by SMS and then email when a job closes in the connected CRM.
competitors.analytics: Not observed directly.
competitors.compliance: No rating gate before the site list, but the conditional copy biases who proceeds.

competitors.name: GatherUp (Request Setup flows)
competitors.category: Feedback + review-request SaaS (agencies / multi-location)
competitors.guestFlow: Three named flows. Survey & Reviews Flow (formerly Ultimate): an NPS 0-10 or Stars rating, then up to four survey questions plus open text (a first-party review), then the review-site page. Ratings & Review Flow (formerly Review Mode): a rating, then a positive or negative landing page that leads to third-party sites. Public Reviews Flow (formerly Direct): review-site buttons straight away plus a 'Direct Feedback' button; the vendor recommends it for businesses with NPS above 80. Low scores (0-6 by default, configurable) get a Negative Landing Page. It carries an apology, a 'Direct Feedback' button placed above the online review sites, and the same review sites as the positive page. Direct Feedback opens a private text field, and submitting it ends the journey.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: No live page observed. From the docs: a logo header, an optional banner image, an accent colour on small elements, the rating question (often embedded in the email or SMS), then a branched landing page. The low-rating page has an apology copy block, the Direct Feedback button, then review-site buttons. An optional copy/paste helper appears on both branches.
competitors.visualStyle: Template-driven email and landing pages: logo, one accent colour, an optional header image. Copy is short and plain by default.
standoutIdeas: A 'same experience' rule: every feature appears in both branches (review links and the copy-paste helper are on or off for both). Only the wording is personalised. This is the closest external precedent for RepKey's threshold model.
A configurable low-rating threshold with a sensible default, like RepKey's Private Feedback Threshold (default 3).

A new Request Setup screen shows each step of the chosen flow as an editable page with a live preview. This is a good pattern for RepKey's admin preview of entry, after-rating, private-note and completion states.
Multiple entry channels to one flow: email, SMS, TextBack (the customer texts a keyword), a Feedback URL, QR and kiosk mode.
antiPatterns: The Direct Feedback button sits above the review sites for low raters, which slightly demotes Google. RepKey rules forbid any demotion, so Google keeps its position and private feedback is added.
Admins can switch off third-party sites on the negative page when not requesting Google or Tripadvisor reviews, which is gating for other platforms.
An NPS 0-10 scale is heavy on a phone for a quick guest moment.
competitors.adminBuilder: Requests > Request Setup offers a flow dropdown, per-step page editing with preview, and Settings. Brand & Colors covers logo, accent colour and a banner image on the feedback landing page. SMS Requests sets how the SMS looks. Advanced settings cover send method, reminder type and count, and rating type (NPS or Stars). Manual or automatic send, CRM integrations, white-label reseller mode.
competitors.analytics: Reports: Insights (keyword sentiment, green/red), Success (NPS with promoters and detractors, keyword filters), Performance (a funnel of requests sent, opened, completed and clicked through to review sites) and Reviews (multi-source rating, star distribution, month-over-month trend). Breakdowns by location, keyword/tag and period.
competitors.compliance: States that all modes show review links regardless of score and were approved by the Google My Business team (vendor claim). The negative-page hide option weakens this for other sites.

competitors.name: Grade.us (Review Funnel landing page)
competitors.category: White-label review-funnel SaaS for agencies
competitors.guestFlow: A review funnel landing page reached by email, SMS, an embeddable review button, a live star widget (click a star to start) or QR. The sentiment question can use stars, faces or thumbs. Positive responses see a choice of review sites; the vendor supports review buttons for 37 sites plus custom links. A third-party summary says negative responses can be sent to a contact form instead of the review channel (not verified live).
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed. The Modern style has a page header with an optional coloured banner or a header image of 1024x138px (PNG, JPG or GIF under 450kb). A single site-wide 'Message to All Visitors' text block follows, then the sentiment control, review-site buttons and an optional stream of selected reviews.
competitors.visualStyle: Classic and Modern templates; one brand hex colour applied to the header and optionally to the stars, faces or thumbs. The thin 1024x138 banner strip suggests a dated, form-like page rather than an immersive one.
standoutIdeas: The rating can start on the business's own website, where a click on a star opens the funnel with that value. This is analogous to RepKey's rating as the first tap.
Admins can switch the page style (Classic or Modern) and switch back at any time, a low-risk template switch.
antiPatterns: Faces and thumbs used as a sentiment gate, with reported routing of negative answers to a private form instead of the review sites.
Streaming selected reviews on the landing page is curated social proof that biases the rating.
Banner-strip branding reads as a generic template.
competitors.adminBuilder: Dashboard > Funnel > Setup > Style Options (Classic/Modern), header image or colour banner, brand colour picker, and Content > 'Message to All Visitors'. Email tokens for first name, logo and funnel link. White-label for agencies.
competitors.analytics: Email alerts for new online reviews, monitoring across 100+ industry review sites, and auto-publishing reviews to Facebook (vendor page).
competitors.compliance: The product can gate negative responders (third-party description). Treat it as a gating-capable funnel.

competitors.name: Birdeye (review request templates, Write-a-Review kiosk, review QR)
competitors.category: Enterprise multi-location reputation platform
competitors.guestFlow: Review request: the landing page shows a heading and message with up to four review-site buttons in an order the admin sets, plus an optional 'Contact us' button for writing privately. That leads to a Feedback page with an optional callback request, then a Thank-you page. Write-a-Review (first-party, shown as 'Birdeye certified'): 1-5 stars, Next, a text screen, then Submit. Birdeye suggests bookmarking it on an in-venue iPad as a kiosk. The review QR opens a customisable landing page and thank-you page, with one unique code per location.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed live. Order from the docs: header branding (logo), a heading (130 characters max), a message (2030 max), up to four coloured site buttons, a Contact us button, then the feedback and thank-you pages.
competitors.visualStyle: Template-driven. Admins set button background and text colours and a logo. The vendor says pages are mobile-first and ADA-conscious (claim).
standoutIdeas: Public and private options coexist on one page with no score branch. This is simple and compliant.
Per-location QR codes with 'scan it with your phone to preview the end-to-end experience' before saving. RepKey's publish step could include a real-device test QR for the draft.
The QR artwork itself can be styled (background and text) to match the brand, relevant for RepKey's printed materials.
Tokens such as location name and phone keep one template reusable across many locations, like RepKey's property defaults with portal overrides.
antiPatterns: A callback request on the private feedback page collects contact details. RepKey safety-blocks contact collection.
Tight character limits alongside a very long message field invite walls of text on phones.
competitors.adminBuilder: Template sections: General, Header branding, Review request email, Feedback page and Thank you page, each edited through pencil icons. Drag-and-drop site order, custom review sites via a name and URL, and QR codes under Settings > Profile > QR codes > Reviews.
competitors.analytics: Review Reports and a 'Review NPS' report of sentiment over time and by location; an AI review-response agent.
competitors.compliance: The blog says gating creates a misleading picture and may violate platform guidelines. The template shows review sites to all recipients.

competitors.name: Trustmary (feedback forms / Trustmary Method)
competitors.category: EU (Finnish) feedback + review collection SaaS
competitors.guestFlow: The live demo form opens on an NPS question ('How likely are you to recommend...'). The rest was not advanced because the research was read-only. Vendor description of the three steps: measure satisfaction (NPS, stars, CSAT or emoji), ask open feedback on why, then ask for a review. Review connections add Google Business Profile links to the form, and reviews can also be collected first-party from people without a Google account. The feedback-forms page describes branching where low NPS scorers give constructive feedback and high scorers are asked for reviews. The Google-reviews article says to ask everyone and calls gating 'a big no-no'.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Observed at 375px. 1) A white header, about 70px, with the centred vendor logo. 2) A full-bleed saturated amber/yellow background with large soft concentric circle shapes. 3) A centred cream card (radius about 16px) from about y=290 to 590, holding a centred bold question of about 17px on two lines. 4) An inner lighter panel with eleven circular grey number chips (about 48px), 0-10, in rows of 5 / 5 / 1, leaving '10' alone on the last row. 5) A legend: 0 = Very unlikely, 10 = Very likely.
