No other content, and no business identity other than the logo slot.
competitors.visualStyle: Friendly, bright, rounded, card on a colour field. Customisable questions, colours, fonts and logo. Brand colour dominates the whole viewport.
standoutIdeas: A single-question card centred on an atmospheric colour field. The no-photo fallback is a colour and shape atmosphere, a model for RepKey's photo-less premium variant (e.g. deep ink with champagne arcs).
A scale legend directly under the control makes the meaning of the ends explicit.
Distribution channels include SMS limited to the EU/EEA and QR codes; it is an EU vendor with translations built in, relevant to EN/BG.
antiPatterns: An 11-chip NPS grid wraps badly at phone width and orphans '10'.
The vendor's own pages contradict each other on routing (low scorers to feedback, high scorers to reviews, versus 'ask everyone'), a sign of how blurry gating is in the market.
The vendor logo header takes the top of the page instead of the business identity.
competitors.adminBuilder: Survey editor with question types (NPS, star, CSAT, emoji), conditional branching, a 'Review connections' menu to add or edit platforms and Google review links, and customisation of all questions, colours, fonts and logo, plus translations. Share by email, popup, QR, SMS (EU/EEA), embed or email signature.
competitors.analytics: Per-survey analysis, trends over time, shareable reports, a Google review report / review insights, and data export to other systems.
competitors.compliance: Publicly anti-gating in its guidance, but its branching marketing describes score-based routing. It can be configured either way.

competitors.name: Senja (testimonial collection form)
competitors.category: Testimonial capture (text/video) SaaS
competitors.guestFlow: Observed on Senja's own form. A welcome screen with a founder video and a personal note offering the second month free for a video testimonial, with the CTA 'Send a testimonial'. The next screen is 'Share a testimonial', with a split primary button: 'Record a video' plus an upload icon. Vendor: in-browser recording without downloads, then details such as name, title, photo and website, consent to use, and a thank-you. Forms are made in about 30 seconds and shared as a link or embed.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Welcome screen at 375px. 1) A full-width video still with a centred play button, about 280px tall. 2) A row with a round founder avatar, a thin vertical divider and the purple heart logo. 3) The H1 'Thank you for using Senja' with a party emoji, about 26px, black, heavy geometric sans. 4) Three short grey paragraphs at 16px. 5) A full-width purple gradient pill button (about 56px) with a soft glow and a pointing-hand emoji. 6) Microcopy about 5 minutes and the customer controlling where the testimonial is shared. 7) A floating 'Collect testimonials with Senja' badge that overlaps the CTA. Step 2: a circular back arrow top-right, a left-aligned H1 and subtitle, and one split button, with the lower 55% of the screen empty.
competitors.visualStyle: Playful creator-SaaS: violet gradients, glow shadows, rounded pills and emoji in headings and buttons. Personal (a founder's face and first name).
standoutIdeas: Reassurance microcopy sits at the action, saying the person controls where their words go. RepKey can do the same with a line such as 'private to the property, no name or email'.
One decision per screen with a large primary action and a small secondary (upload) in the same control.
A human, first-person welcome works when the business has a real host voice (e.g. 'From the team at...').
antiPatterns: An incentivised testimonial: a free month in exchange for a video. RepKey permanently denies rewards for review solicitation.
Emoji used as UI in the title and CTA.
The vendor badge overlaps the primary CTA on mobile.
Screens are left mostly empty after the first step.
competitors.adminBuilder: Form builder in about 30 seconds, video and text, custom fields (name, title, photo, website, product), branding, share link or embed.
competitors.analytics: Filtering by tag, rating, job title, source and word cloud; transcription search; notifications for each new testimonial with rating and snippet; HD export.
competitors.compliance: Not a review-platform funnel. The incentive is typical in testimonial tools and incompatible with RepKey policy.

competitors.name: Testimonial.to (collection page)
competitors.category: Testimonial capture (text/video) SaaS
competitors.guestFlow: The landing page asks whether you would give a shout-out, lists four prompt questions, and offers two buttons: 'Record a video' and 'Send in text'. 'Send in text' opens a modal sheet: 'Write a text testimonial', the questions repeated, a 5-star control that is already filled at 5, a textarea with AI 'Fix grammar' and 'Improve writing' buttons, image attach, required name and email, title and company, a photo upload, a marketing-use consent checkbox, then Send / Cancel.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: At 375px. 1) A language switch top-right: a globe icon with the text 'English'. 2) A centred indigo circle, about 48px, with a thumbs-up (the logo slot). 3) A centred bold H1 of about 22px on two lines. 4) A centred grey paragraph with an emoji. 5) The label 'QUESTIONS' with a short indigo underline bar. 6) Four bulleted prompts. 7) A full-width indigo 'Record a video' button and a near-black 'Send in text' button, about 48px each, radius about 4px, both above the fold at about y=660 and 725. The text form is a bottom-anchored modal over a dimmed page.
competitors.visualStyle: Clean but generic SaaS: Inter-like sans, indigo accent, black secondary button, centred stack.
standoutIdeas: A visible, labelled language switch in the top-right corner (globe plus language name, not a flag). A good pattern for an EN/BG toggle.
Prompt questions shown before writing reduce blank-page anxiety. For RepKey's private feedback, optional gentle prompts (e.g. room, service, food) could help without steering sentiment.
Explicit consent wording at the point of submission.
antiPatterns: Stars are pre-selected at 5, a default-positive bias that contradicts RepKey's principle of five unselected stars.
AI 'Improve writing' on a review or testimonial undermines authenticity.
Name and email are required; RepKey guests enter no personal details.
A long modal form scrolls inside a dimmed page on a phone.
competitors.adminBuilder: Space/page per product with custom questions, logo, language, text or video, and consent text (from the observed page structure).
competitors.analytics: Not researched.
competitors.compliance: Not a review-platform funnel; the pre-filled rating is the notable ethics issue.

competitors.name: Famewall
competitors.category: Testimonial capture + wall of love
competitors.guestFlow: One shared collection link with no sign-up. The respondent submits text, an in-browser video, or audio with a waveform display. Optional AI helps draft. The admin approves before anything is published.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed.
competitors.visualStyle: Custom colours and fonts; separate collection pages per client, programme or service line.
standoutIdeas: Separate collection pages per service line under one brand, the same idea as RepKey placements (reception, restaurant, spa) sharing a property identity.
An approval step before public display.
antiPatterns: AI drafting of testimonials (authenticity).
competitors.adminBuilder: Per-page colours and fonts, approval workflow.
competitors.analytics: Not documented on the fetched page.

competitors.name: EmbedSocial (Leave-a-review collect forms)
competitors.category: Review widgets + collection forms (multi-location)
competitors.guestFlow: A collect form with a rating (admin-chosen icon), text and optional photos, plus 'Buttons to review sites'. For businesses with several Google places, the form finds each location's review link and lets the customer pick the place they visited. An 'AI Reviews Generator' helps customers put their experience into words. Low-rating handling is not documented.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed.
competitors.visualStyle: Admin sets language, font, rating icon and colours; a privacy-policy link is mandatory on each form.
standoutIdeas: A location picker that resolves the right Google review link per place. This is relevant to RepKey Portal Groups: a group portal could let the guest pick the outlet, each with its own verified Google destination.
A mandatory privacy-policy link on every form, with GDPR positioning and 10+ translations, available on the free plan.
antiPatterns: AI-generated review text offered to customers.
Photo-first testimonial capture does not fit RepKey's beta (uploads are safety-blocked).
competitors.adminBuilder: Build tab (rating icon, text/photo toggles, privacy link), design options (language, font, colours), embedding and display in review widgets.
competitors.analytics: Not documented on the fetched pages.

competitors.name: Okendo (response form + In-Mail)
competitors.category: E-commerce product reviews (Shopify)
competitors.guestFlow: The response form has three pages: Review (stars and text), Enhance (photos or videos, social login) and Post-Review (a 'Congratulations' message with an optional party emoji and configurable modules, including rewards and incentives). With In-Mail the shopper rates, writes and picks attributes inside the email, then is sent to the capture form to add media.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed. In-Mail star layout is configurable vertical or horizontal, ordered 1 to 5 or 5 to 1, with a custom label above the selector.
competitors.visualStyle: Over 55 styling options (hex colours, fonts, borders), a header logo with width and link, and an auto-style feature that derives a theme from the store.
standoutIdeas: The first answer is captured on the very first surface with no page load. RepKey's analogue is putting the stars in the first viewport, so the first tap is the rating.
Auto-styling from existing brand assets. RepKey could derive the portal palette from property branding so admins start from something beautiful.
Optional steps can each be switched off (Enhance page, social login, media).
antiPatterns: Incentive and reward modules on the completion page (denied for RepKey).
A 5-to-1 star order puts 5 first, a positional bias.
competitors.adminBuilder: Per-page styling, logo, toggles for pages and features, email layouts (side-by-side or stacked).
competitors.analytics: Not researched in this pass.

competitors.name: Yotpo (review request landing page with Smart Prompts)
competitors.category: E-commerce product reviews
competitors.guestFlow: The review request landing page (or an in-mail form) collects stars and text. Smart Prompts shows three AI-suggested topics. As the shopper mentions each one (synonyms count), the topic text turns green and a progress bar fills. It completes when all three topics are covered and the review has at least 200 characters. Topics are localised (EN/FR/ES/DE).
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed. Topic chips and a progress bar sit with the review text box.
competitors.visualStyle: Customisable, mobile-friendly email templates with in-mail forms.
standoutIdeas: Live, non-blocking writing guidance. A calm version could help RepKey's private written feedback, for example neutral topic hints (room, service, food, cleanliness) with no scoring.
antiPatterns: A progress bar with a completion target is a gamification pattern that pressures length. Avoid it in RepKey.
Topics with negative sentiment are filtered out of suggestions, which quietly steers content positive.
competitors.adminBuilder: Enable Smart Prompts per request; templates and languages.
competitors.analytics: Not researched.

competitors.name: Reviewflowz
competitors.category: B2B SaaS review collection (G2, Capterra) + monitoring
competitors.guestFlow: Collection campaigns with 'Magic Links' that send a reviewer to G2, Capterra and similar sites; per search summaries it offers 1,000+ reward options for incentivised requests. No guest-facing page was observed.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed.
competitors.visualStyle: Not observed.
standoutIdeas: Real-time Slack notifications of new reviews, a model for notifying responsible managers (RepKey already notifies them).
antiPatterns: An incentive catalogue for review requests (denied for RepKey).
competitors.adminBuilder: Campaigns, magic links, incentive management.
competitors.analytics: An aggregated review database across G2, Capterra, Trustpilot and app stores, AI sentiment, and a Slack app.

competitors.name: NFC / QR review cards and stands (Taps Reviews, GrowSEO, GetMoreReviews, ReviewsLink, TAPiTAG, Tapni; Taaply not found)
competitors.category: Hardware tap-to-review vendors with optional landing pages
competitors.guestFlow: Two models. (a) Direct: the tap opens the Google review page straight away. Taps Reviews and ReviewsLink say this can happen within seconds and with no search, and TAPro focuses on hardware. (b) A branded landing page: GetMoreReviews offers multiple platforms and says it captures feedback before reviews and routes unhappy customers to support. GrowSEO's page title promises only 5-star reviews go public, and per a search snippet 1-4 stars start a private manager conversation. Taps Reviews sells 'Review Filtration Plus+' to stop bad reviews. ReviewsLink lets the destination be changed after printing and supports Multi-Links (link tree). Tapni is an NFC business-card profile (link tree) rather than a review product; its demo profile URL rendered only a spinner for over 3 seconds (observed-live). Taaply.com turned out to be an identity, payments and education product with no review-card page found.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Direct model: none, the guest lands on Google's own mobile review sheet. Landing-page model (vendor descriptions): business logo and colours, custom message, a rating step, then Google or other platform buttons for high scores and a private form for low ones. Link-tree variants add phone, email, website and social icons.
competitors.visualStyle: Hardware-first marketing; black or white acrylic stands and cards printed with Google branding and '5 star' copy. Landing pages are generic templates with a logo and brand colour.
standoutIdeas: A destination that can be changed after printing, like RepKey's stable QR/NFC tokens that survive content edits. It is a selling point to state plainly to admins.
Tap and scan analytics per device or location (Taps Reviews, TAPiTAG), matching RepKey's per-portal qualified_scans. Per-placement comparison is what buyers expect.
Physical placement drives context: table stand, reception card, spa. Supports RepKey placement-specific copy.
antiPatterns: Gating sold openly as a feature ('stop bad reviews', only 5-star reviews go public). Hotels will compare RepKey to this, so the admin experience should explain why equal access is the honest, Google-compliant choice.
'Leave a 5-star review' printed on hardware and in copy.
A JS-only profile shell that shows a blank spinner on first paint (Tapni demo). A QR or NFC landing must render its content server-side instantly.
Link-tree profiles crowd social icons, phone and email with no hierarchy.
competitors.adminBuilder: Setup is choosing the business, often in under 2 minutes (vendor claim). Dashboards cover link management, logo, colours and custom messaging, team roles and per-device assignment.
competitors.analytics: Taps and scans per device or location, sometimes in real time. No outcome data beyond clicks.
competitors.compliance: Widely non-compliant: filtration and gating are marketed features.

crossCuttingPatterns: Compliant vendors converge on one rule: every rater gets the same steps and the same public links, and only the wording is personalised. GatherUp states this most clearly (its negative page shows the same review sites plus an apology and a Direct Feedback button), and Birdeye and Podium show public and private options together with no branch. This supports RepKey's model (Google always available, private feedback added at or below the threshold). RepKey should go one step further than GatherUp and never place the private option above or in place of the Google action for low raters.

Rating-first surfaces are one question per screen with large targets: Trustpilot's five 46px tiles, Trustmary's single card, Birdeye's stars then Next. Almost all leave the lower half of the phone empty. A premium hospitality portal can use that space for atmosphere (brand colour field, typography, optional photo) instead of blank white.

Word labels for star values (Trustpilot: Bad / Poor / Average / Great / Excellent) and end-point legends (Trustmary) are the accessible norm. Few vendors show the chosen word visibly; RepKey can, in EN and BG.

Business identity is usually weak or overshadowed by the vendor: vendor logo headers (Trustmary), 'Powered by' floating badges (NiceJob, Senja), vendor adverts on the completion page (Podium). A portal where the property brand leads and RepKey is a quiet footer mark is a clear differentiator.

Customisation across the category is shallow and uniform: a logo, one accent colour, a header banner (Grade.us 1024x138, GatherUp banner), copy fields, a choice of rating icon, occasionally fonts (Trustmary, EmbedSocial, Okendo's 55 style options). None offers curated, art-directed layouts. There is room for a small set of designed compositions with a guaranteed no-photo variant.

Completion states are routinely monetised or dishonest: promotional-SMS opt-ins and vendor ads (Podium), rewards and incentives (Okendo, Senja, Reviewflowz), and 'Thanks for your review' asserted without knowledge (Podium). RepKey's honest receipt (rating received, Google opened if chosen, correct / withdraw / reset device) has no close equivalent.

Personal data is commonly demanded: name and email required (Testimonial.to), callback requests (Birdeye), phone for promos (Podium). RepKey's 'no personal details' stance can be said at the action as reassurance microcopy, as Senja does with its sharing-control line.

Third-party tracking and cookie walls are common on review pages: Trustpilot's cookie dialog plus reCAPTCHA device signals, and NiceJob loading GTM, Google Analytics and the Facebook SDK. RepKey's first-party server-side telemetry means no banner, a faster and calmer first screen.

Platform choice follows 'one recommended plus an escape hatch' (Podium 'Continue with Google / Select a different site', NiceJob's elevated Google card plus 'Other review site options'). RepKey has a single public destination, so one confident Google action with an honest subline is enough.

Language handling is usually a text-labelled switch (Testimonial.to top-right globe plus 'English') or template translations (Trustpilot 16 languages, EmbedSocial 10+, Trustmary translations, Yotpo prompts in 4 languages). Flag icons, as in the Ratestar reference, are not the norm among these SaaS tools.

Admin analytics are funnel-shaped: sent, opened, completed, clicked through to the review site (GatherUp Performance report); invite status with clicked and reviewed checks (Podium); taps and scans per device or location (NFC vendors); plus NPS and keyword sentiment and location comparisons. For RepKey the honest equivalent is qualified scans, then ratings, then Google-destination selections (never 'reviews written'), plus private-feedback volume, broken down by placement and group.

Previewing the real guest journey is a recurring admin affordance: GatherUp's step-by-step Request Setup preview, Birdeye's 'scan with your phone to preview end-to-end', NiceJob's walk-your-own-link. This supports RepKey previewing every state (entry, after rating, private note, completion, stale Google, language) before a deliberate publish.

An AI writing-assistance trend has emerged (Testimonial.to 'Improve writing', EmbedSocial AI Reviews Generator, Famewall AI drafting, Yotpo Smart Prompts). For public reviews this is an authenticity and Google 'fake engagement' risk. At most, RepKey could offer neutral topic hints for private feedback, with no scoring or progress bars.
surprises: Testimonial.to's own text-testimonial form opens with all five stars already filled at 5, the opposite of the neutral, unselected default RepKey needs.

GatherUp, the most explicit about compliance, still lets admins switch off third-party review sites on the negative page when not requesting Google or Tripadvisor reviews. Its compliance is platform-specific. It also places the private Direct Feedback button above the review sites for low raters.
Trustmary's marketing pages contradict each other: one describes routing low scorers to feedback and high scorers to reviews, another calls gating a big no-no and says to ask everyone.

Podium's live locale strings show a thank-you that asserts the person reviewed, followed by an SMS-promotions opt-in and a Podium advert on the business's own page. There is also a healthcare disclaimer string, showing regulated-industry copy lives at the action.

NFC and QR hardware vendors openly sell gating in 2026 (for example 'Review Filtration Plus+' and pages promising only 5-star reviews go public), and 'leave a 5-star review' is printed on stands. These are likely the reference points hotel buyers bring, so RepKey's admin onboarding needs a short, confident explanation of equal access.

Trustpilot colours the selected stars by score (red-orange for 1, light green for 4). This is an effective signal but reads as judgement; a single calm accent suits private hospitality feedback better.
Yotpo's Smart Prompts filter out negative-sentiment topics and drive a progress bar to 200 characters, a subtle positivity nudge plus gamification.
Senja's own form offers a free month in exchange for a video testimonial, a norm in testimonial tools that is permanently denied in RepKey.
NiceJob's review microsite loads Google Tag Manager, Google Analytics and the Facebook SDK on the page where customers leave reviews.

Tapni turned out to be an NFC business-card and link-tree product whose demo profile showed only a spinner for over 3 seconds. Taaply had no findable review-card product (taaply.com covers identity, payments and education). The requested 'Tapni/Taaply review landing page' benchmarks do not really exist as described.

The Ratestar reference's vendor now markets its portal as a branded mini-website with an 'AI concierge' reachable by QR, NFC or link (observed on their marketing page). That is a link-tree plus concierge direction, useful context for how the reference's crowded hub came about.

Evidence caveat: no live business-branded portal page was opened for GatherUp, Birdeye, Grade.us, EmbedSocial, Okendo or Yotpo, because the research was read-only and had no public sample URLs. Their anatomy is taken from help-centre documentation. The Trustpilot, Trustmary, Senja, Testimonial.to and NiceJob descriptions come from 375px screenshots saved in the earlier agent's transcript.

competitors.name: Touch Stay (digital guidebook + 5-Star Review pop-up)
competitors.category: Digital guidebook / compendium for boutique hotels, B&Bs, glamping and vacation rentals
competitors.guestFlow: Observed at 390x844 on three public example guides: Paperbark Camp (luxury glamping), Le Mas Paraloup (multilingual), and Barnstead Inn (B&B). The arrival screen is a full-screen cover, and GET STARTED leads to a hub of 8 icon tiles. Each tile opens a content page of accordion topics. Language switching uses a globe tile that drops down a vertical list of two-letter codes (DE/EN/FR/NL). Rating comes from the vendor page, not observed live. It is a bottom-sheet pop-up over the guide, triggered after a positive interaction or 24h before checkout. The sheet shows a circular logo with the property name, 'Enjoying your stay?' and five gold stars. After 5 stars it says 'That's fantastic! You will be redirected to a Google Maps service to leave a public review' above a teal 'Leave a review' button. Vendor copy: 'Positive ratings send guests to public reviews; lower ratings ask for private feedback'. That is explicit review gating. A separate Ratings topic collects stars plus an optional comment, emailed privately to the host. A contact-collection feature also exists.
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
Top to bottom on the cover:
- A full-bleed property photo fills 100vh.
- Top right is a ~48px rounded-square globe button in the accent colour.
- Centre: the logo, an optional ~70px circular host portrait (Le Mas Paraloup shows its two owners), and a tagline in large light geometric sans (~34px, centred, up to 4 lines).
- Two thin-ring circle icon buttons (call, message), a short accent rule, the property name (~30px) and the address with a pin icon.
- One accent CTA 'GET STARTED' in uppercase letterspaced type.
- Barnstead adds two translucent navy chips: 'Check-in after 15:00' and 'Check-out before 11:00'.
- A persistent dark bottom tab bar with 4 uppercase letterspaced items (HOME/CONTACT, INFO/THE CAMP, MAP/FIND US, SEARCH) and a round chat FAB overlapping the photo.
The hub has a slim header (tiny logo, call/message, share/print icons) and a 2-column grid of pale-sage tiles, each with a thin line icon and a label.
competitors.visualStyle: A photo-led template that is identical across properties. Identity comes only from the photo, one accent colour (sage, ochre or olive) and the logo. The type is Montserrat/Figtree-like geometric sans, with uppercase tracking on buttons and nav. The hub is flat and light with line icons. The cover feels boutique because of the photography, not because of the system. The hub reads as generic SaaS.
standoutIdeas: The arrival screen works as a 'cover': one photo, the name, one action. It feels like opening a printed welcome book.
A circular host or owner portrait on the cover humanises a small property. A placement-specific equivalent (the team, the chef) could work for boutique hotels.
Useful facts shown at arrival as quiet chips (check-in/out times) instead of links.
Language behind a compact globe with two-letter codes that expands in place.
The rating is a separate lightweight surface (bottom sheet) rather than a form page.
The admin dashboard shows average rating, review count, public vs private response counts and sentiment trend: a small, understandable metric set.
antiPatterns: Paperbark Camp's dark logo is nearly invisible on its dark hero photo. The template has no logo-contrast treatment (scrim, light/dark logo variant).
Hierarchy is inverted: the marketing tagline (~34px, 4 lines) outranks the property name.
A mandatory 'GET STARTED' gate before any content.
The hub tile grid of line icons is interchangeable with any SaaS.
Uppercase letterspaced labels everywhere, plus a chat FAB overlapping content.
Rating-dependent routing: only happy guests are sent to Google, which Google's policy prohibits.
The pop-up interrupts reading.
competitors.adminBuilder: Logo, colours and fonts. Replicate content between rooms/properties. Scheduled guidebook notifications. QR codes and deep links. An AI guidebook generator. Per-guide feedback-form settings, where a public review link is entered (e.g. Google) and the pop-up message and timing can be customised from templates with shortcodes (guest name, property name).
competitors.analytics: Data Dashboard: guidebook views and engagement, average property rating, number of reviews, public vs private response counts, and guest sentiment over time. Ratings can be batch-downloaded and emailed to chosen addresses.
competitors.compliance: The pop-up routes by score, which conflicts with Google Maps policy ('selectively solicit positive reviews' is prohibited). Contact collection is offered, whereas RepKey keeps it safety-blocked.

competitors.name: Hostfully Digital Guidebooks
competitors.category: Digital guidebook (vacation rentals; used by small hotels)
competitors.guestFlow: Observed at 390x844 on the public demo 'YelloWee Saigon'. The flow is cover → 'Get Started' → a 3–5 s blank white screen with a purple spinner → House Manual. That screen has horizontally scrolling icon tabs (HOUSE MANUAL, ARRIVAL, DEPARTURE, MARKETPLACE, PLACES TO...), cards (title plus square photo, e.g. 'Smoking' with a no-smoking pictogram), and a bottom List/Map toggle. No rating or review step was observed.
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
Cover:
- A white top bar with a horizontally scrolling list of native language names (English in bold grey, others in mint).
- '日本語' wraps into a vertical 3-character stack and 'Nederlands' is clipped at 390px.
- A full-bleed interior photo.
- A centred translucent white rounded card with bold Roboto 'Welcome to our home!' (~30px, 2 lines), a pin and a 3-line address.
- A black pill 'Get Started'.
After entry the language bar stays AND a hamburger, tiny logo, search icon and globe icon row is added: two language controls. Below: the icon tab row and the card list.
competitors.visualStyle: A Material/Roboto default with mint links and black pill buttons. The frosted card is the only atmospheric device. There is no typographic identity, and vendor purple leaks in via the loading spinner.
standoutIdeas: Native-language names ('Español', 'Français', '日本語') are more respectful than flags.
List/Map toggle for recommendations.
Guidebook available as a PDF/print version (vendor), useful for reception desks.
antiPatterns: The language bar breaks at phone width (the vertical CJK stack, the clipped last item) and is duplicated by a globe icon after entry.
Blank loading screen with a vendor-coloured spinner between the cover and the content.
Generic Material cards and icon tabs; the property brand is invisible after the cover.
'Welcome to our home!' is generic copy on a frosted card over a photo, reducing both readability and the photo's impact.
competitors.adminBuilder: Templates ('no design required'). 16+ languages with instant auto-translation. Private links and QR codes. PDF export. Sections for house manual, arrival, departure and local recommendations with maps. Viator affiliate links and local gift cards (vendor).
competitors.analytics: Not documented on the pages read.
competitors.compliance: No review flow observed.

competitors.name: Duve (Guest App)
competitors.category: Web guest app / guest experience platform for hotels (check-in, upsells, messaging, guidebook)
competitors.guestFlow: The app is reservation-bound: one link from check-in to checkout, no install. Home is a personalised hub. The main reading path is greeting → reservation → shortcuts → sections of posts and upsells. Chat is always available. No first-party star-rating flow is shown. Reviews are promoted through 'Motion' videos in the app or messages (vendor). Content visibility can vary by tags, brand and room type (e.g. families see kids' activities, couples see spa).
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
From the vendor mock on duve.com and the interactive Navattic tour:
- A centred wordmark logo (e.g. serif 'DUVE HOUSE', 'coral sand') with a hamburger at top right.
- A rounded-corner hero photo with a '1/1' carousel counter; multiple cover images are supported.
- 'Welcome Alex!' in bold sans (~24px), then 'Oct 14 – Oct 19 • 2 Adults, 2 Children' and a 'See reservation' link in the accent colour.
- A row of outlined pill shortcuts with icons (Room key, Wifi, Room control).
- A 'When you arrive' list with thumbnails ('Arriving early? From $20').
- A 'Top picks for you' horizontal photo-card carousel, 'Upgrade your stay' cards, and a 'Places in the area' map widget.
- A floating purple chat bubble.
competitors.visualStyle: Clean white, rounded photos, a bold sans headline and one accent colour. The marketing site pairs a serif (Playfair-like) with a geometric sans, but the guest app itself reads as polished-generic. Commerce ('From $20', '$' markers) is threaded throughout.
standoutIdeas: The personal greeting and stay facts at the top are the strongest 'this is for me' signal in guest apps. RepKey has no reservation identity, so the analogue is placement-aware copy (reception, spa, restaurant table).
Pill shortcuts for the 2–3 most-needed facts, directly under the greeting.
Only three section formats (image carousel, image list, simple list) plus banners and widgets: curated composition instead of free layout.
Admin scope banner: 'You are editing 4 Brands, your changes will affect all selected brands', which states edit scope at the point of editing.
Admin preview beside the editor, with a language selector ('Original').
antiPatterns: Upsell prices threaded through information content make it feel like a shop, not a welcome.
The vendor's purple chat bubble persists on every hotel's app.
The rounded-card-plus-carousel look is shared by every guest-app vendor; the property brand is limited to the logo and one colour.
competitors.adminBuilder: Sections (Image carousel / Image list / Simple list), each holding posts and upsells, arranged by drag and drop. Banners (icon, title, message, colour, internal or external link). Widgets (Map, Recommended upsells, Room upgrade). A central Styles page with logo, brand colour, custom fonts, cover images (carousel, adjustable size), shortcuts, secondary button colour and background colours. Visibility conditions by tags, brands and rooms. Multi-brand editing with a scope warning.
competitors.analytics: Upsell conversion, segments that rebook, revenue leakage (vendor). Nothing specific to reviews.
competitors.compliance: No rating gate documented. Heavy commerce focus.

competitors.name: Canary Technologies (Digital Compendium + review surveys)
competitors.category: Guest management platform (US market leader): compendium, check-in, messaging, upsells, reputation
competitors.guestFlow: The compendium is reached by QR on property, the Wi-Fi login screen, a welcome message link, or in-room tablets. It is a hub with reservation access, property info, messaging, staff tipping, dining and amenities, and upsells ('$49 In-Room Breakfast', late checkout). Reviews are handled separately: at departure a 1–5 satisfaction survey is sent by SMS/WhatsApp. 'Guests that leave 5-stars are prompted to share their great experience on Tripadvisor & Google Reviews'. 4 stars or lower are routed to staff for internal recovery. This is explicit review gating.
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
Vendor mock ('The Statler'):
- A script wordmark at top left.
- 'Hello, Emily!' with the subline 'We hope you enjoy your stay with us'.
- A 2x2 grid of pale-blue tinted tiles with small icons: My Reservation, Property info, Message us, Tip Staff.
- A tab strip 'Restaurants | Facilities and amenities'.
- A 'Dining' row with a 'View All' link and horizontally scrolling photo cards with title and cuisine subline ('Orla by Michael Mina — Greek and Egyptian').
competitors.visualStyle: Light, friendly SaaS: pale blue tile tints, a rounded sans and small icons. The script logo is the only brand expression. It reads as competent but generic.
standoutIdeas: Curated typography: the admin picks one of 3 title styles and one of 3 body styles instead of a free font picker. Brand latitude without the risk of bad pairings.
Section visibility toggles (Reservation, Property info, Message us, Tip staff) with an adjacent live mobile preview.
Branding controls limited to primary text, secondary text and button colours: few knobs, hard to break.
'Preview updates to know exactly how they will appear to guests before publishing'.
Distribution through many placements, including Wi-Fi login.
antiPatterns: Explicit 5-star-only public review prompt.
A 'Tip Staff' tile and upsell prices mixed into information.
Uniform pale-blue tile grid; the property photo appears only in cards, never as atmosphere.
Vendor claim 'up to 350%' more 5-star reviews is marketing, not evidence.
competitors.adminBuilder: Toggle modules. Customize Branding (primary/secondary text colour, button colour). Typography choices (3 title × 3 body). Photos and menus per amenity or restaurant (title, cuisine, description, image). Automated translations with a Default language. Preview before publish. Multi-property management. Vendor claims setup takes under 10 minutes.
competitors.analytics: Not detailed for the compendium. The reputation product focuses on review volume and service recovery.
competitors.compliance: Score-based routing to Google/Tripadvisor conflicts with Google's prohibition on selectively soliciting positive reviews.

competitors.name: TrustYou (Survey / CXP)
competitors.category: Guest feedback survey and review marketing platform (hotels, chains)
competitors.guestFlow:
There are two surfaces.
1. A web survey (public link plus QR). The header shows the hotel name, address and website. It opens with a welcome message, then an overall score on a 5- or 10-point scale (mandatory by default), optional detailed ratings, a 'Review' free-text field (the only part that is semantically analysed), and custom questions (score, NPS, text, choice, date). The email field is mandatory by default; reviews without email are not published. A thank-you message follows. 'Google Push' and 'TripAdvisor Push' let guests push their review. Social share buttons can be set to show 'only if score is higher than 3' (an optional gate). Kiosk 'Auto-reload' resets the form 15–20 s after submit for shared tablets.
2. The newer CXP runs a WhatsApp AI-agent conversation: 'How was your stay?', a 4/5 rating, a contextual follow-up ('we'll work on improving the Wi-Fi'), then 'Here's a link if you'd like to share your review publicly 👉 Rate your stay'.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: The web survey is a single column. On phones, questions always stack above answers. The header is either Logo (transparent PNG above the hotel name and contact details) or Banner. Banners are max 860px wide on desktop; on mobile they have a fixed height and are cropped left and right, so content must sit centred. An optional progress bar sits under the header when paginated. Rating buttons are coloured red/orange/green on selection by default. A TrustYou attribution logo sits at the bottom, recoloured automatically for contrast.
competitors.visualStyle: The default is 'very light and clean', with no header image on mobile or desktop. The branded version gets a banner, three Google-Font slots and colour tokens. The result is a well-behaved form, not a brand experience. The WhatsApp flow inherits chat UI and uses emoji as UI.
standoutIdeas: A clear token model for branding: fonts in 3 slots (Text, Headings, Buttons); colours for page text, headings, background, foreground, progress bar, buttons, submit button, rating negative/neutral/positive and inputs; 'Use template' inheritance from a parent; 'Reset' per group.
Explicit warning that some fonts lack Cyrillic, which is directly relevant to BG.
Language hygiene: a default fallback language, plus 'Hide languages that don't have translated messages'.
Kiosk auto-reload for shared devices maps onto RepKey's shared-device reset.
Privacy levels per survey (Public / Restricted / Private).
Alerts with an assignee, due period in days and extra recipients.
antiPatterns: Mandatory guest email by default (RepKey collects no personal details).
Traffic-light red/orange/green rating buttons feel judgemental and clash with premium palettes.
The 'Show share buttons only if score is higher than 3' toggle is a built-in gating switch.
Facebook/Twitter share buttons above the header.
The 860px form-in-a-page layout reads as a questionnaire, not a welcome.
Emoji pointer as the review call-to-action in chat.
competitors.adminBuilder: Sections: General (name, type, privacy level, scale, default language, pagination, public link/QR, auto-reload, Google/TripAdvisor push, mandatory email), Messages (welcome and thank-you, per language, with the original shown while translating), Questions (basic, detailed ratings, custom questions with parent/child logic), Hotel Details (name, address, website, sharing), Look & Feel (fonts, colours, layout, header Logo/Banner per device), Alerts.
competitors.analytics: Survey tab. TrustScore and Meta-Review (for Public privacy level). Analytics KPIs, semantic analysis of the review text, mailing statistics, action alerts.
competitors.compliance: The share-button score threshold is an optional gate. Email is mandatory by default. The WhatsApp flow offers the public link after a 4/5 (example), with no evidence of lower-score handling.

competitors.name: Shiji ReviewPro (Guest Satisfaction Surveys)
competitors.category: Enterprise reputation + guest survey suite (chains)
competitors.guestFlow:
Observed live (read-only, nothing selected) at 390px on the public Apex Hotels group survey. The first screen asks the guest to pick one of 9 Apex hotels from a native select, with a disabled grey 'Continue'. The rest comes from the docs:
- The survey is post-stay or in-stay, with one rating scale for all questions (1–5 or 1–10) fixed at creation, and the overall rating recommended first.
- Skip logic allows e.g. 'Skip to the end of the survey if the Overall rating is 5/5'.
- The thank-you page offers 'Review Solicitation' buttons to Tripadvisor, Google or both, or a 'Collection Program' that embeds the Tripadvisor or HolidayCheck review form in the thank-you page.
- The docs I read show no score threshold on the solicitation buttons. Third-party claims that ReviewPro redirects only above a threshold were not verified.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Live entry page: white, no header image, no property logo. An 'Establishment' label, a full-width native select 'Select your establishment', and a small disabled 'Continue' button. The footer has 'Powered by' plus a large REVIEWPRO REPUTATION wordmark. Branded surveys (docs) get a header image of configurable height with the establishment name optionally below it. Animated GIF headers of 3–4 images are recommended at 760×240. A progress bar, section titles, question labels and choice elements are all themeable.
competitors.visualStyle: The live entry is bare and unbranded, with the vendor wordmark the most prominent element. The configured survey is a themed questionnaire (themes → fonts, colours, shapes, then per-element overrides).
standoutIdeas: Vendor data (62 surveys, 39 clients): average open rate 61.8%, conversion 22.5%. For in-stay surveys, 'One rating question, One comment question' performed significantly better. Multi-page surveys with heavy logic did worse, and mandatory free text lowers conversion. This supports a rating-first, one-note portal.
Survey builder shows yellow warnings for missing translations or header configuration: readiness surfaced before publishing.
Device-type preview in the Design Builder, with 'Preview Changes' and 'Undo Last Change'.
Per-establishment header images under one group design template.
NPS Competitors: mutual, opt-in benchmark sharing for at least 90 days.
antiPatterns: A group survey that opens with a 'Select your establishment' dropdown: guest effort before any welcome, and a flow that could have been avoided with per-property links or QR.
Vendor branding outranks the hotel on a live guest page.
'Save & Publish': all changes 'published immediately and cannot be undone'. No draft or rollback, which RepKey's publication model beats.
Animated GIF headers, which cheapen a premium look.
Rating scale locked at creation.
competitors.adminBuilder: Create from scratch or from templates (in-stay, post-stay, M&E) pre-translated into 9 languages. Establishments or groups. Drag-and-drop question builder with logic, skip questions, visibility by PMS fields and establishment labels. Header image widget. Survey Design Builder (themes, then element-level styling scoped by question type). Invitation email and thank-you page design. Departments mapping. Delivery rules. Management response.
competitors.analytics: Global Review Index, NPS and NPS Competitors, Top-Box score, departmental reporting, semantic analysis, auto case management, internal ranking across group properties.
competitors.compliance: Thank-you-page solicitation after survey completion. The docs describe no score gate on solicitation, but skip logic can shorten surveys for 5/5 guests.

competitors.name: Customer Alliance
competitors.category: Review management + guest surveys (strong in DACH/EU)
competitors.guestFlow: The survey (vendor page) is reached by email, QR, Wi-Fi or tablet. Scales can be 1–5, colours or yes/no, with conditional questions. After completion 'a thank you page where you can invite them to leave a review on Google, TripAdvisor, or other platforms', opening the platform's review page via API redirect. No gating is mentioned. Observed live: the public, certified review page for Hotel Berlin Leipzig. I did not click 'Book now' or any review action.
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
Live public review page at 390px, top to bottom:
- A dark grey bar with a hamburger and the Customer Alliance logo.
- A right-aligned 'CERTIFICATE' with 'what's this?'.
- The hotel logo, then a two-photo strip with a translucent 'BOOK NOW' band.
- A rule-flanked italic label 'Public Reviews Score'.
- Huge thin numerals '91%' with 'VERY SATISFIED' in caps, and 'Based on 3,909 reviews across 9 portals'.
- An accordion 'Average rating across 9 portals' listing portals with dotted leaders (Booking.com 87%, Google 92%, HolidayCheck 94%...).
- Sort selects, then review cards with a teal percentage ring (96%, 100%), reviewer name, traveller type, age band, date, the text, and an indented management reply.
competitors.visualStyle: Dated mid-2010s: Montserrat-like caps, percentage rings, grey panels, native selects. The dotted-leader portal list is a rare editorial touch.
standoutIdeas: Visible management replies under guest comments signal care, useful for a future public trust surface (not the beta portal).
Dotted leaders for aligned label/value pairs: an editorial device that could suit opening hours or useful facts.
Survey measures NPS, CSAT and CES with department drill-down (Spa, Restaurant, Gym, MICE).
antiPatterns: Scores as percentages with 'VERY SATISFIED' labels feel clinical.
Vendor 'CERTIFICATE' and logo chrome above the hotel.
Shows reviewer age band publicly.
Photo strip under a 'BOOK NOW' band: a commercial action displaces welcome.
competitors.adminBuilder: Fully customisable questions and conditional logic, multi-language, branded surveys (specifics not documented), channels, review widgets for the hotel website.
competitors.analytics: NPS, CSAT, CES; filter by location or brand for portfolio benchmarking; departmental drill-down; 'Semantic Trends' (e.g. WiFi, StaffFriendliness); custom KPIs; API export to BI.
competitors.compliance: Thank-you page review invitation; no threshold described on the product page.

competitors.name: GuestRevu
competitors.category: Guest survey + reputation (South Africa/UK; Tripadvisor Platinum Review Collection Partner; Mews marketplace)
competitors.guestFlow: Observed live on the vendor's public demo survey (read-only; I did not press NEXT). Page 1 asks for personal data: first name, last name, email, arrival and departure dates, room number. It is 'skipped if we already get this guest data from an integration'. Later pages hold ratings. Vendor copy: an 'embedded Tripadvisor review section' lets guests review 'without logging in or even being a member', plus a Google push. No threshold is documented. Customisable alerts fire on high or low scores.
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
At 390px:
- A line 'Questionnaire available in:' followed by 10 language names as blue text links wrapping over 3 lines.
- A ~150px wide banner photo (terrace with sea view).
- A square white logo tile overlapping the banner's bottom edge (placeholder 'Your Logo').
- A blue info callout.
- Stacked form fields with Bootstrap-style inputs, an envelope add-on and calendar add-ons.
- An uppercase 'NEXT' button.
competitors.visualStyle: Bootstrap-era form styling: blue links, grey borders, a stock banner. Brand expression is limited to a banner image and a colour palette.
standoutIdeas: Vendor research: custom CSS branding lifted response to 22.3% vs 19.4% unbranded. That is a vendor claim that brand fidelity matters.

Vendor research: smileys matched traditional formats, while hearts and stars produced lower average scores. Sliders were skipped more on mobile, and 11-point scales were hard to show horizontally on phones.
1–3 open questions gave 20–22% response; 6 dropped to ~14%.
Logo tile overlapping the banner edge: a simple layered-depth device.
antiPatterns: Personal data before any rating.
Language chooser as a wall of wrapped links.
Content changes require a support 'survey changes form', so admins cannot self-serve copy.
Stock placeholder branding in the public demo.
competitors.adminBuilder: Self-serve: banner image (JPG/PNG, ≤2MB) and colour palette. Question and content changes go through GuestRevu support. 'Ultra-custom' CSS for brands with strict identities. Multiple surveys by stage, room type or length of stay.
competitors.analytics: Online guest intelligence reports filtered by date, room type and sentiment. AI-powered themes. Monthly management reports ('the good, the bad and the ugly'). Instant notifications.
competitors.compliance: Embedded Tripadvisor collection; score-based gating not documented.

competitors.name: Akia
competitors.category: AI guest messaging (SMS/WhatsApp) with in-thread surveys and review asks
competitors.guestFlow: There is no web page. An NPS 0–10 question arrives in the SMS/WhatsApp thread 'right where they'd text you back'. Promoters (9–10) get 'a warm thank-you and a link to Google or Tripadvisor'. Detractors (0–6) trigger a staff task and an AI message to the guest. Passives are unspecified. This is gated routing.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Native messaging bubbles. The sample is branded 'Hotel Segundo', with location details and unsubscribe text.
competitors.visualStyle: Inherits the messaging app; there is no brand surface.
standoutIdeas: Recovery before checkout: low scores create a task immediately. RepKey's inbox and manager notifications are the analogue.
Dashboard shows NPS, period-over-period change and promoter/passive/detractor split.
antiPatterns: Review link only for promoters.
NPS 0–10 is awkward on a phone and for casual QR guests.
competitors.adminBuilder: Messaging automations, survey timing, review platform links (a user review notes a limit on how many review links can be added).
competitors.analytics: NPS, change vs prior period, promoter/passive/detractor percentages, natural-language queries on comments by property.
competitors.compliance: Promoter-only review ask conflicts with Google policy.

competitors.name: Revinate (Guest Feedback / Surveys)
competitors.category: Hotel CRM + guest feedback surveys
competitors.guestFlow: Post-stay, in-stay and anonymous 'Flex' surveys. Tripadvisor publishing uses 'a simple two-page survey' of internal questions, then a Tripadvisor review widget. Vendor best practice recommends reserving the Thank You email with social and booking links 'for promoters/positive respondents only', i.e. selective follow-up. The help centre requires login, so it was not read.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed; no public survey found.
competitors.visualStyle: Unknown (not observed).
standoutIdeas: 'Flex' anonymous surveys solicited without guest identity are the closest structural analogue to a QR portal.
Guidance: 1–5 scales or yes/no, 1–2 optional comment boxes, no required fields, 20–25 questions max for post-stay.
antiPatterns: Promoter-only thank-you and share follow-up (selective solicitation).
Content behind a login wall; little public evidence of guest-facing design quality.
competitors.adminBuilder: Custom surveys (details behind login).
competitors.analytics: Consolidated reputation plus survey reporting (vendor).
competitors.compliance: Recommends promoter-only follow-up.

competitors.name: Ratestar.io (user-supplied reference)
competitors.category: QR/NFC review portal + link-in-bio for hospitality (Bulgarian market presence)
competitors.guestFlow: From the user-supplied screenshot of a live Bulgarian spa hotel portal (not loaded by me): no private rating step. The guest lands on a page with two platform cards (Google and Tripadvisor), each showing five pre-filled gold stars and 'Rate us', and taps straight out to public platforms. Link cards follow. Ratestar's own smart-feedback page says the opposite configuration is possible: 'At any rating - both a public review and a private form', including complaint topics, a comment and optional contact details.
competitors.mobileAnatomy:
From the screenshot, top to bottom:
- A dark full-bleed hero video/photo (festive lobby with the hotel sign) and a white rounded flag+chevron language switcher at top right.
- The white bold hotel name with a blue verified check.
- A pin-emoji address and phone-emoji number, with a dotted underline on the phone.
- Three outline icons (web, Facebook, Instagram).
- A centred thank-you-for-reviews sentence.
- Two side-by-side photo cards with platform logos, five gold stars and 'Rate us'.
- The name repeated with a fleur-de-lis emoji description.
- Full-width photo link cards ('Book a room — Comfort and coziness for your stay') with a link icon.
The background is black and the type Montserrat-like.
competitors.visualStyle: Nightlife-dark, photo-heavy, crowded hierarchy, emoji as UI, platform logos as decoration.
standoutIdeas: A hero with real property atmosphere, plus a language switcher that is immediately visible.
Full-width photo link cards make secondary links feel like places, not URLs (image upload is blocked in RepKey beta, so this needs a typographic equivalent).
Per-card/per-placement tracking IDs for QR/NFC (vendor).
antiPatterns: Five pre-filled gold stars on 'Rate us' cards imply the expected answer.
No private path, and multiple public platforms compete.
The name is repeated twice, with emoji for address, phone and description.
A 'verified' badge that the property itself asserts.
Black background with photo cards everywhere: no rest for the eye.
competitors.adminBuilder: 'Fully branded with your logo, colours, language and rules'. Alert thresholds ('3 stars or lower'), recipient lists, location routing.
competitors.analytics: Tracking ID per NFC card or QR code. Performance by location, employee and campaign. Conversion by touchpoint (vendor claims). Issue topics by location.
competitors.compliance: The vendor page claims equal public access; the observed configuration skips private rating entirely.

competitors.name: Other guest web apps: Enso Connect Boarding Pass, Bookboost, STAY
competitors.category: Guest web apps (boutique hotels / STR / chains)
competitors.guestFlow: Enso: a 'Boarding Pass' web app styled after an airline boarding pass, Apple Wallet compatible. It runs from booking to checkout with verification, check-in, smart-lock access, guidebook, upsells and messaging. The public demo is gated behind a lead form, which I did not submit. Bookboost: branded check-in, digital keys, local guide and in-stay feedback. STAY: in-app Instant Feedback with 'Personalize thank-you messages based on the survey score', push notifications and staff alerts.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed. Enso's metaphor is a single pass-like card holding stay essentials.
competitors.visualStyle: Not observed. All three advertise logo, colours and fonts as the customisation surface.
standoutIdeas: Enso's boarding-pass metaphor: one familiar object that holds the essentials. A RepKey receipt could borrow the 'stub' idea for the completion state without adding wallet scope.
STAY: score-aware thank-you copy (tone can vary by score while actions stay identical).
STAY is used by chains such as Barceló and has a luxury reputation; it goes live immediately after updates.
antiPatterns: Demo behind a lead-capture form.
Feature sprawl: the '7 systems in one' super-app positioning.
competitors.adminBuilder: Logo, colours, fonts, images, social links, conditions by booking attributes (Enso), drag-and-drop journey builder with 80+ personalisation tokens (Bookboost).
competitors.analytics: Revenue and automation claims (Enso: '28% more revenue', vendor claim); survey score analysis by service/department (STAY).
competitors.compliance: Not documented.

competitors.name: Other review boosters: Loopon, Olery, Hotelinking, GuestJoy (SiteMinder), ReviewFilter (Mews marketplace)
competitors.category: Survey + review-generation tools; Mews itself has no native survey and relies on marketplace partners
competitors.guestFlow: ReviewFilter (Mews marketplace, vendor-page): 'If the feedback is positive, the customer is automatically redirected' to TripAdvisor, Yelp, Facebook or Google. Loopon: one-page post-stay surveys in the brand identity, then one-click Tripadvisor/Google posting; tuned to 'Nordic feedback culture'. Olery: surveys by QR, Wi-Fi, SMS, email or TV; 'Review Routing'. Hotelinking: in-stay surveys triggered from the captive Wi-Fi portal, with the review channel chosen by guest country of origin (Tripadvisor, Google, HolidayCheck, Zoover). GuestJoy (now SiteMinder): 'Review Booster' for boutique hotels.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed.
competitors.visualStyle: Not observed.
standoutIdeas: Loopon's culture-aware tone and one-page format fits Bulgarian/EU guests, where brevity and politeness matter.
Hotelinking chooses the review platform by guest country. RepKey is Google-only, but EN/BG language could adjust copy tone.
Loopon benchmarking against peer brands is a desirable GM feature (future analytics).
antiPatterns: Positive-only redirects (ReviewFilter), advertised openly on the Mews marketplace.
'Up to 400%' review uplift claims (Loopon, vendor).
competitors.adminBuilder: Not researched in depth.
competitors.analytics: Alerts, case management, sentiment, benchmarking (Loopon, Olery).
competitors.compliance: ReviewFilter's positive-only redirect conflicts with Google policy.

crossCuttingPatterns: Two archetypes, and none of them merges both. (A) The guidebook/guest-app 'cover' (Touch Stay, Hostfully, Duve, Canary): a full-bleed photo or rounded hero, a centred logo and name, one CTA or greeting, then a tile grid or card carousels and a bottom tab bar. (B) The survey form (TrustYou, ReviewPro, GuestRevu, Customer Alliance): a 760–860px banner header, a white single column, a progress bar and rating buttons. Opportunity for RepKey: cover-quality arrival where the private rating IS the hero, with no 'Get Started' gate and no form feel.

Review gating is the industry default, and it is often a headline feature: Canary ('Guests that leave 5-stars are prompted...'), Akia (NPS 9–10 only), Touch Stay pop-up ('Positive ratings send guests to public reviews'), TrustYou toggle ('Show share buttons only if score is higher than 3'), ReviewFilter on the Mews marketplace, and Revinate's promoter-only thank-you email. Google's policy prohibits merchants from choosing to 'Discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews'. RepKey's equal Google access after every score is a real differentiator. The design should make the Google action visually identical at 1★ and 5★, and give the private-note offer its own quieter card rather than a replacement.

Premium signals observed:
- Real property atmosphere (photo or video) used once, big, then restraint.
- One accent colour.
- A logo with correct contrast.
- A human touch (Touch Stay's host portrait, Duve's greeting).
- Useful facts as quiet chips (check-in/out).
- Very few actions on the first screen.
Generic-SaaS signals:
- Line-icon tile grids and pale-blue tints (Canary, Touch Stay hub).
- Material cards and Roboto (Hostfully).
- Traffic-light rating buttons (TrustYou default).
- Percentage rings (Customer Alliance).
- Uppercase letterspacing everywhere.
- Vendor wordmarks and spinners (ReviewPro, Customer Alliance, Hostfully purple).
- Upsell prices inside information.
- Emoji as UI (Ratestar, TrustYou WhatsApp).

Personalisation is the strongest 'for me' cue in guest apps ('Welcome Alex!', dates, party size in Duve and Canary). RepKey has no reservation identity, so the honest substitute is placement-aware wording set by the admin (Reception, Spa, Restaurant). Never fake a name or room.

Language handling varies and is often broken at 390px. Seen: a globe tile with two-letter codes (Touch Stay), a horizontally scrolling bar of native names that wraps CJK vertically and is duplicated by a globe after entry (Hostfully), a wall of wrapped blue links (GuestRevu), and a flag dropdown (Ratestar). Best practice for EN/BG: a small always-visible two-option segmented control at the top, native names or codes rather than flags, hiding untranslated languages (TrustYou has this option), and fonts verified for Cyrillic (TrustYou explicitly warns that some fonts lack it).

The branding surface converges on a small token set:
- Logo, and a cover image or carousel.
- Brand/accent and button colours.
- 2–3 type slots (TrustYou: Text/Headings/Buttons; Canary: 3 title × 3 body curated choices).
- Module order and visibility toggles (Duve sections, Canary tile toggles).
- Themes first, then element overrides (ReviewPro).
Curated choices (Canary) look better with less risk than free pickers. Every vendor puts the live phone preview beside the editor.

Scope and publication safety are weak spots, and GM-relevant:
- Duve shows an explicit multi-brand scope banner.
- ReviewPro shows yellow readiness warnings (missing translations or header) but publishes immediately with 'cannot be undone'.
- Canary advertises preview before publishing.
RepKey's draft vs published snapshot, rollback and stable QR tokens can be sold as confidence.

In-stay feedback research favours minimalism. ReviewPro (62 surveys, 39 clients, vendor data): one rating question plus one comment question converted significantly better. Mandatory free text lowers conversion, and adding languages may help. GuestRevu (vendor data): branded surveys 22.3% vs 19.4% unbranded; hearts and stars yield lower average scores than other formats; sliders and 11-point scales work poorly on phones. These support RepKey's rating-first, optional-note flow and a considered star control with verbal endpoints.

Analytics offered to managers are usually simple at small-property scale. Touch Stay: average rating, count, public vs private split, sentiment trend. Akia: NPS with period change and promoter split. Enterprise tools add departments, semantic topics, benchmarking (ReviewPro NPS Competitors, Loopon) and per-touchpoint attribution (Ratestar tracking IDs per QR/NFC). RepKey's qualified_scans / portal_rating_count / portal_rating_average by Property, Group and Portal map well. Add 'Google destination selected' framed honestly as a click, never as reviews written.

Channel shift: post-stay surveys are moving into WhatsApp/SMS AI conversations (TrustYou CXP, Akia, Canary). The branded web page stays essential for on-property, identity-free moments (QR at reception, table, spa; walk-in restaurant guests), which is RepKey's niche.

Shared devices: TrustYou's kiosk 'Auto-reload' clears the form 15–20 s after submission. That is precedent for designing RepKey's shared-device reset as a calm, obvious state rather than a buried link.

No product handles the no-photo case well. TrustYou's default is 'no header image', which is just a plain form, and every premium-feeling example depends on photography. With image upload safety-blocked in the RepKey beta, a typography-led, material-textured no-photo identity is both necessary and a gap in the market.

What a general manager is sold on, as repeated across vendor pages (inferred as their desire):
- More public reviews with less staff effort.
- Catching unhappy guests before checkout (alerts, tasks).
- 'Looks like our own app, not a vendor'.
- Setup in minutes (Canary <10 min, Akia/Canary <30 min).
- No app download.
- Multi-property consistency with local control.
- Printed QR codes that keep working.
- Benchmarking against competitors.

Direction implications for the three research-backed guest directions:
1. An evolved Signature Stay: an 'editorial cover' with one restrained hero (photo optional, with a tonal or gradient fallback), the rating visible in the first viewport, and fixed logo-contrast handling. Touch Stay and Ratestar show photo power; their contrast and hierarchy failures show what to fix.
2. A typographic 'printed stationery' identity for the no-photo beta: letterpress-like wordmark, paper or ink tokens, dotted-leader useful facts (the Customer Alliance idea), Cyrillic-safe serif pairing.
3. A calm 'concierge card' utility layout inspired by Duve and Canary's greeting-plus-shortcuts: placement-aware greeting, 2–3 fact chips, the rating as a card, then a quiet ordered link list. Avoid tile grids and upsell pricing.
surprises: Almost every mainstream hospitality vendor openly advertises rating-based review gating (Canary, Akia, Touch Stay, ReviewFilter, a TrustYou toggle, Revinate guidance), despite Google's explicit prohibition. RepKey's policy is a real differentiator, not table stakes.

The enterprise leader's live guest page (ReviewPro, Apex Hotels group survey) opens with a bare white 'Select your establishment' dropdown, a disabled 'Continue' button and a large 'Powered by REVIEWPRO REPUTATION' wordmark. It was the least premium page observed.
TrustYou makes the guest email field mandatory by default. Reviews without an email are not published and do not count toward public KPIs.
Touch Stay's showcase luxury example (Paperbark Camp) renders its dark logo almost invisibly over its dark hero photo. The template has no contrast safeguard.
Hostfully's public demo breaks its own language bar at 390px ('日本語' stacks vertically, the last item is clipped), then shows a second language control after entry.
ReviewPro's 'Save & Publish' goes live immediately and 'cannot be undone'. RepKey's draft, snapshot and rollback model is a sellable admin advantage.
Vendor research (ReviewPro) found that in-stay surveys with just one rating plus one comment convert best, which validates the minimal rating-first portal.

Ratestar's own feature page promises public and private paths 'At any rating'. The live portal the user supplied shows only public platform cards pre-decorated with five gold stars: configuration, not product, decides whether a portal is ethical.

GuestRevu's vendor research reports that stars and hearts produce lower average scores than other formats. That is worth remembering when designing and labelling the star control, though it is a vendor claim.
The Enso Connect guest-app 'example' is gated behind a lead-capture form. Several vendors hide the guest experience behind demos, so polished public guest pages are rarer than the marketing suggests.

competitors.name: sunday (pay-at-table, reviews module)
competitors.category: Restaurant QR pay-at-table with post-payment Google review prompt
competitors.guestFlow: Guest scans the table QR, pays the bill. The help centre says that right after payment the guest is 'instantly prompted to leave a rating from 1 to 5 stars', then 'Depending on your setup, they're redirected to your restaurant's Google page, with the rating already prefilled', and claims it takes 'less than 30 seconds'. A sunday blog post describes two post-payment questions, 'How was your meal?' and 'What could we improve?'. Satisfied guests get an optional button ('Loved your experience? Share it online for others to see!'). Dissatisfied guests are invited to 'voice their concerns privately, offering to make the situation right'. The same post-payment surface also has tip presets (15/18/20% plus custom), an optional loyalty opt-in offering perks such as 'a free cocktail on their next visit', and a thank-you line written in the venue's voice ('It was a pleasure cooking for you tonight! You're always welcome here.'). Low rating: private path plus instant staff notification (vendor search summary). Language handling is not documented.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed live; a guest review screen needs a real payment. Inferred order at phone width: venue name/logo, then bill lines and split/tip, then Apple Pay/Google Pay, then a payment-success state with a 5-star row directly below it, then a conditional Google button OR a private 'what could we improve' field, then loyalty opt-in, then the thank-you line. sunday's own marketing (observed at 375px) shows the brand language it sells to owners: a white page, huge black grotesk headline '5x your Google reviews', a black pill 'Book a demo' CTA, and a staff photo overlaid with floating chips (a 'G 4.9' card with magenta bar chart and '+350 5 on Google', three reviewer pills each with 5 gold stars).
competitors.visualStyle: sunday platform branding: white, black neo-grotesk sans, a magenta scribble logo, black pill buttons, floating white cards with soft shadows. As far as can be seen, venue identity is limited to the restaurant's name and logo on the bill. The premium feel comes from the payment-grade polish, not from venue art direction.
competitors.adminBuilder: The dashboard 'Get more reviews' section has a 'share review form' link that can be put on a QR code. The setup decides whether guests are redirected to Google.
competitors.analytics: Review dashboard: average rating, its evolution, and the 'share coming from sunday'. Reply directly with templates or AI answers ('Answer in one click'). A morning 'snapshot of your online reputation from the day before'. KPI reports by Food & Drink, Service Quality, Ambiance and Value for Money. A Staff Performance dashboard. Vendor claims, not evidence: '5X more 5* Google reviews', '50% of guests leave a review', 'Increase your rating up to 0.1 point per month'.
competitors.compliance: sunday's own blog says 'Google's guidelines prohibit review gating', yet its post-payment article describes a Google button for satisfied guests only and a private channel for dissatisfied ones. That is gating as defined by Google's Maps policy ('selectively solicit positive reviews') and by Tripadvisor's identical-UI rule. Prefilling a Google star rating is an attempt to influence the rating. A loyalty perk offered on the same screen as the review ask risks being read as an incentive.
standoutIdeas: Tie the rating ask to a natural completion moment (bill paid). The RepKey equivalent is the placement: the table card or the check-out desk.
Close with a thank-you line written in the venue's own voice, which feels hospitable rather than transactional.
Morning reputation digest email, plus per-staff and per-category breakdowns.
One reusable 'review form' link that the owner can print as a QR code.
antiPatterns: Google star rating prefilled from the private rating (manipulative, and RepKey cannot observe or claim what happens on Google).
A Google button that depends on the score (review gating).
Tip, loyalty perk and review ask stacked on one screen: cognitive overload and an incentive smell.
Marketing framed as 'guaranteed to get more reviews'.

competitors.name: me&u (formerly Mr Yum)
competitors.category: QR order-and-pay web app with post-purchase star rating and threshold Google prompt
competitors.guestFlow: Per the help centre (observed live), feedback is a 'beta feature' but 'Guest feedback collection is on by default'. 'Post-purchase, guests are prompted to optionally leave a star rating out of 5.' Next, 'Guests are asked to leave a Google review based on the minimum star rating that has been set in Manage'. Guests below the threshold are instead 'prompted for written feedback after leaving their star rating, if they aren't asked to leave a Google review'. That written feedback goes to 'Fast Feedback' in the Crew staff app so staff can act while the guest is still in the venue. Food halls: the Google review goes to the food hall and the feedback goes to the operator. Contact collection is not described. Mr Yum domains now redirect to me&u.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: The guest review screen was not observed. The venue menu (Market House Altrincham, meandu.app/mha) was measured live at 375px. Top to bottom: full-bleed header photo 375x131; H1 'Market House Altrincham' in Manrope 24px/700, #181819, at y=131; two 36px circular icon buttons (grey #F0F0F0) to the right of the title; pill chips 'Dine-in' and 'Table number (e.g. A1)' in 14px/700 with the venue's single burgundy accent rgb(93,9,35) at y=183; a section 'Start with a drink' followed by a wave emoji; a horizontal carousel of 'Trending' product cards, each 96px wide with a 94px square photo, name and price; a venue voice blurb ('Home to 9 Independent Kitchens & Bars. Dogs welcome, people can come too.'); H3 'Explore vendors' (18px/700) with a grey 'Open a group tab' pill; a 2-column vendor grid of 166px cards with 110px photos and wait badges ('30 min wait', '20 min wait'); footer 'Follow us on instagram!' and a fees disclaimer. White background throughout.
competitors.visualStyle: Clean white commerce UI in platform typography (Manrope). The venue brings a header photo, one accent colour used for chips and text, food photography in cards, and a single sentence of personality. Dense but tidy; menu imagery does most of the brand work.
competitors.adminBuilder: Manage > Feedback tab: master toggle (on by default); Google reviews toggle; the Google review link is 'pre-filled based on your venue address' with a 'View link' check; a Google Place ID finder to correct it; a configurable 'minimum star rating' for the Google prompt.
competitors.analytics: Feedback is visible in the Crew & Staff Upsells app. Reporting requires contacting an account manager ('Reach out to your account manager ... for access to reporting'). The Pay page claims 'More positive reviews' and tips up by 'up to 10%' (vendor claims).
competitors.compliance: The configurable minimum-star threshold for the Google prompt is textbook review gating: it breaks Google's Maps policy on selective solicitation and Tripadvisor's identical-experience rule. Because it ships on by default, an owner can be non-compliant without having chosen to be.
standoutIdeas: Verify the Google destination in the admin ('View link', Place ID lookup). This maps directly to RepKey's verified Google destination and its stale-URL degradation.
Real-time routing of private comments to a staff app. The RepKey analogue is notifying responsible managers.
One accent colour plus one voice sentence gives a venue identity cheaply.
Operational badges (wait time) show live, useful state instead of decoration.
antiPatterns: A Google prompt gated on a star threshold.
A beta feedback feature switched on by default.
Reporting locked behind an account manager.
Emoji used as section decoration.

competitors.name: Toast Guest Feedback and Toast Pay Menu Item Review
competitors.category: POS-integrated in-venue and digital-receipt feedback (private, no Google push)
competitors.guestFlow: Handheld (Toast Go), shown after payment: star rating, then selection from predefined experience descriptions (examples: food quality, wait time), then a 'Share feedback' contact opt-in, then email or phone, then receipt choice, all on the same screen as the receipt selection. Digital receipt link: rating (thumbs up/down in the 2019 launch coverage), an open text box, and then 'regardless of their answer' the guest is asked whether the restaurant can reach out. Toast Pay (QR on the receipt): after mobile payment the guest is asked 'how their meal was' and shown up to three of the ordered items, prioritising the more expensive ones. Each item gets thumbs up or down, with optional open text per reviewed item. No Google prompt is documented, and Toast Pay passes no guest contact details to restaurants.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed live. Inferred: a Toast-branded, utilitarian receipt page; a rating row; reason chips; a text area; a contact opt-in. Item review is a short list of up to three dish rows, each with a thumbs pair.
competitors.visualStyle: Toast system UI; venue branding is limited to the name and logo on the receipt (inferred). Functional, not premium.
competitors.adminBuilder: Toast Web > Guests > Guest feedback settings: master toggle; a per-handheld 'Guest Feedback Options' setting; 'Display Feedback on Text & Email Receipts'; notification presets 'Notify for negative feedback only' / 'Notify for all feedback' / 'No notification'; recipients by email or SMS per user. Menu item review has its own email-recipient settings.
competitors.analytics: SMS and email alerts include date/time, server name, feedback type, reasons, and contact details if the guest opted in. The Guest Feedback Report filters by manager, server, table, rating and reason, with linked checks and a 'Respond' button offering a status field, an internal notes field, AI response suggestions, and 'Mark resolved without responding'. Guest Feedback Insights (30 days): AI summary, rating and sentiment over time, top and lowest items, rating by theme ('Atmosphere, Service, Food Quality, Wait Time'), by order type, and sentiment by time of day. Menu Item Review: a weekly Thursday email per location plus Reports > Marketing > Menu Item Review.
competitors.compliance: Feedback stays private and does not steer anyone to Google, so there is no gating exposure. Collecting ratings on a staff-held device at the table is 'on premises' pressure territory if it were used for public reviews. The contact opt-in is something RepKey has safety-blocked.
standoutIdeas: Reason chips shown after the rating turn one tap into a diagnosable theme.
Item-level thumbs for up to three dishes is granular yet costs almost no effort.
Case statuses including 'resolved without responding' match the RepKey inbox discipline.
Theme and time-of-day breakdowns are good seeds for the Portal analytics design.
antiPatterns: Feedback taken on a device the server hands over (social pressure, biased scores).
Binary thumbs lose the nuance a 1-5 scale gives.
A contact-details opt-in on the rating screen (blocked for RepKey).

competitors.name: OpenTable post-dining Ratings and Reviews
competitors.category: Reservation platform verified-diner review form (email-triggered)
competitors.guestFlow: An email follows a seated or completed reservation, and the guest must be signed in to the booking account. The review form has 'star ratings' (overall 1-5 plus sub-ratings such as food, service, ambience and value, per third-party summaries), written comments, optional photos, and an optional private note to the restaurant. The Dining Feedback Form 'includes a field for adding a confidential note to the restaurant', intended to 'sing the praises of specific staff members' or share something particular to the visit. Reviews are moderated for up to 72 business hours, and negative reviews are published if they meet the standards. A review can be edited; if deleted it cannot be recreated. Restaurants reply publicly or privately, and the diner receives the reply by email. Restaurants that do not take part in public reviews get a private feedback form instead.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Not observed (sign-in required). The help article (observed live) confirms the component order: ratings, then written review, then photos, then optional private note, then submit.
competitors.visualStyle: OpenTable platform style; the restaurant appears as name and photo only. Trust comes from verification and moderation, not visuals.
competitors.adminBuilder: Restaurants opt into the Ratings and Reviews program; the respond-to-reviews feature offers public or private replies.
competitors.analytics: Aggregates feed the Diners' Choice awards (Best Overall, Ambiance, Service, Outdoor Dining) and an AI review summary on the profile.
