rules.designImplication: Incentives are already banned by Google, Tripadvisor and Booking.com, so the FTC rule adds nothing for the portal. Any incentive tied to the rating step (for example 'rate 4 or more to unlock a discount') is unlawful for US customers.

rules.source: US FTC Rule 16 CFR 465.7 (Review suppression)
rules.rule: Prohibits using legal threats, physical threats, intimidation or public false accusations to prevent or remove reviews. Also prohibits misrepresenting that displayed reviews represent most or all reviews submitted when some are suppressed by rating or sentiment.
rules.designImplication: The portal does not publish reviews, so 465.7(b) matters only if private ratings or quotes are ever shown publicly. The receipt and feedback copy must never contain anything threat-like, such as policy warnings about 'false reviews'.

rules.source: US FTC Guides Concerning Endorsements and Testimonials, 16 CFR 255.2(d) and Example 11 (2023 revision)
rules.rule: Advertisers 'should not take actions that have the effect of distorting or otherwise misrepresenting what consumers think'. In Example 11, a marketer asks purchasers for feedback and then invites only those with very positive feedback to post reviews on third-party sites. That 'may be an unfair or deceptive practice'. Inviting all recent purchasers 'would not have been unfair or deceptive, even if it had expressed its hope for positive reviews'.
rules.citation: https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/255.2 (verbatim Example 11); FTC 2022 guide 'Don't ask for reviews only from customers you think will leave positive ones': https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/soliciting-paying-online-reviews-guide-marketers
rules.designImplication: Example 11 describes review gating exactly. RepKey's flow (a private rating first, then the same Google invitation for everyone) matches the approved alternative in that example. Any score-based variation of the invitation turns it into the prohibited pattern. Mild hopeful copy ('We'd love to hear from you on Google') is acceptable in US terms, but Google and EU rules are stricter, so keep it neutral.

rules.source: EU Unfair Commercial Practices Directive 2005/29/EC as amended by Omnibus Directive (EU) 2019/2161: Article 7(6)
rules.rule: 'Where a trader provides access to consumer reviews of products, information about whether and how the trader ensures that the published reviews originate from consumers who have actually used or purchased the product shall be regarded as material.' The Commission Guidance says this also covers promoting reviews made available by another trader on your own interface. Member States had to transpose by 28 Nov 2021 and apply from 28 May 2022.
rules.designImplication: Showing the property's Google rating or quotes on the portal would probably trigger a duty to explain the source and verification: 'Ratings on Google; the property does not verify them.' Showing an average of RepKey's private ratings publicly would trigger it too. The simplest compliant beta design shows no public rating, review count or testimonials on the guest portal.

rules.source: EU UCPD Annex I points 23b and 23c (black list) plus Commission Guidance 2021/C 526/01 §4.2.4 'User reviews'
rules.rule: Point 23c bans submitting false reviews or 'misrepresenting consumer reviews or social endorsements'. The Guidance describes misrepresentation 'such as by only soliciting and making available positive reviews'. It lists further manipulative practices: a trader who 'provides consumers with pre-filled positive review templates' or 'presents consolidated review ratings on the basis of undisclosed and/or opaque criteria'.
rules.designImplication: The EU names 'only soliciting ... positive reviews' as misrepresentation, which settles the prominence-by-score question: do not do it. Pre-filled five stars and suggested review text ('Great stay! Friendly staff...') come close to the named 'pre-filled positive review templates', both in the private rating (stars start unselected) and on the Google card. RepKey, acting on behalf of the hotel, is within the UCPD's definition of a trader.

rules.source: UK Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, Schedule 20 para 13 (in force 6 Apr 2025, SI 2025/272)
rules.rule: Banned in all circumstances: fake or concealed incentivised reviews, and 'Publishing consumer reviews, or consumer review information, in a misleading way'. Examples of misleading publication are failing to publish negative reviews and 'giving greater prominence to positive consumer reviews over negative ones'. Para 13(4) also bans 'Offering services to traders' for doing or facilitating these things.
rules.designImplication: Para 13(4) creates vendor-level exposure. If RepKey offered UK customers a gating option (score-dependent Google visibility), RepKey itself could be offering a banned facilitation service. The invariance guarantee protects the vendor as well as the hotel. Relevant for UK guests and future UK customers, less so for the Bulgarian beta.

rules.source: CMA208 'Fake reviews' guidance (CMA, 4 Apr 2025), §§4.3–4.5
rules.rule: Traders must not interfere with consumers' ability to leave negative reviews, including 'by arbitrarily stopping and starting review invitations' and 'by making an offer of dispute resolution contingent on a consumer not leaving a negative review'. Cherry-picking 'might be done ... by encouraging just those who are satisfied to leave reviews'.
rules.designImplication: This is the clearest official test for the private-feedback offer to low scorers. It must never read as a trade: 'Tell us first and we'll make it right' placed above or instead of Google, or 'Before posting publicly, let us fix it' are not acceptable. Show private feedback as optional, beside Google and never replacing it, with the Google action unchanged in the same place. An admin 'pause Google action' toggle that managers could flip after bad days would match 'arbitrarily stopping and starting invitations'.

rules.source: Bulgarian Consumer Protection Act (Закон за защита на потребителите), чл. 68е, ал. 7 and чл. 68ж, т. 26–27 (ДВ бр. 20/2022, in force 28.05.2022)
rules.rule: Transposes Omnibus Art. 7(6) as чл. 68е, ал. 7. That paragraph requires information on whether and how published reviews are verified and how they are handled, including whether all reviews are published and whether they are positive or negative. Annex I 23b/23c are transposed as the per se unfair practices in чл. 68ж, т. 26–27 (unverified 'real customer' claims; fake reviews or misrepresenting reviews). Enforced by the Commission for Consumer Protection (КЗП). Written pre-contractual information must be in Bulgarian (the Act's general information rules).
rules.designImplication: Same implications as the EU UCPD, now binding on the first customers. The BG copy needs the same neutrality as the EN copy. Translate carefully so the BG version of 'Share your experience on Google' does not drift into 'Оценете ни с 5 звезди' ('Rate us 5 stars'). Bulgarian should be the default language for BG properties, with English one tap away.

rules.source: Tripadvisor Trust & Safety, Review Posting Guidelines ('Attempts to Manipulate Property Ranking by Businesses') and Content Fraud FAQ for Business Owners
rules.rule: 'We prohibit the practice of selectively soliciting positive content and/or rejecting moderate or negative content. If any survey or external website ultimately directs users to submit a review on Tripadvisor, the user interface and experience for submitting positive and negative reviews must be identical.' Incentives for reviews, including staff incentive programmes, are prohibited.
rules.designImplication: This is stricter than Google. If RepKey ever adds a Tripadvisor action, a threshold-based extra private-feedback box for 3 stars or fewer arguably makes the experience non-identical. Tripadvisor support therefore needs the post-rating screen to be the same for all scores, for example an optional private note offered to everyone. This is a design argument for a single post-rating layout now.

rules.source: Tripadvisor Content API display requirements / brand guidelines
rules.rule: 'Always use the bubble ratings that are provided in the API response. Do not use your own rating icons.' The logo must be used as supplied (minimum sizes, never inverted), and quoted reviews must be attributed to a Tripadvisor traveller.
rules.designImplication: The Ratestar 'Tripadvisor plus five gold stars' card misuses Tripadvisor's brand (Tripadvisor uses bubbles, and decorative ratings are not allowed). Any future Tripadvisor action is a plain logo plus neutral text with no rating graphic, sized the same as the Google mark.

rules.source: Booking.com Guest review guidelines and Partner Hub 'Handling guest reviews'
rules.rule: 'The only way to leave a review is to first make a booking.' Booking.com emails guests 48 hours after check-out, and they have three months to review. 'Booking.com property partners should not post on behalf of guests or offer incentives in exchange for reviews.'
rules.designImplication: Do not design a 'Review us on Booking.com' action. Most portal visitors cannot use it and it would mislead them, and Booking.com runs its own invitation. Booking.com may appear only as a secondary 'Book' link in the link tree, visually subordinate and never styled as a review destination.

rules.source: European Accessibility Act, Directive (EU) 2019/882, Art. 2(2), Art. 3(30), Art. 4(5); Bulgarian transposition 'Закон за изискванията за достъпност на продукти и услуги' (ДВ бр. 31/11.04.2025, in force 28.06.2025)
rules.rule: The Act covers listed consumer services provided after 28 June 2025, including 'e-commerce services', defined as services provided at a distance through websites and mobile services 'with a view to concluding a consumer contract'. Microenterprises (fewer than 10 staff and turnover or balance sheet of EUR 2m or less) providing services are exempt.
rules.designImplication: A no-login feedback portal that concludes no contract is probably outside the Act's e-commerce scope. Linked booking engines and menus with ordering are in scope in their own right. Build to WCAG 2.2 AA anyway: it is the market expectation, the next harmonised standard targets it, and hotels will ask vendors for it.

rules.source: W3C WCAG 2.2 (Recommendation) and ETSI EN 301 549 v4.1.1 (published 2 Sep 2026)
rules.rule: WCAG 2.2 added AA criteria 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size (at least 24×24 CSS px) and 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication, plus A-level 3.2.6 Consistent Help and 3.3.7 Redundant Entry. EN 301 549 v4.1.1 adopts WCAG 2.2 AA and maps to the EAA, but until it is cited in the Official Journal the presumption-of-conformity reference is still v3.2.1 (WCAG 2.1 AA).
rules.designImplication: Design against WCAG 2.2 AA now. The concrete requirements for this UI are listed in the accessibility field.

rules.source: Apple Core NFC 'Adding support for background tag reading'; Android developer docs 'NFC basics'
rules.rule: iPhone XS and later read NDEF tags in the background only while the phone is in use. Background reading is unavailable if the device has never been unlocked, the camera is in use, Apple Pay Wallet is in use, a Core NFC session is running, or airplane mode is on. The system shows a notification, the user taps it, and an https URI opens in Safari; the first URI record is used. Android reads tags when the screen is unlocked and NFC is on. On Android 16, http/https tags trigger ACTION_VIEW. 'Beginning with Android 17, scanning such a tag surfaces an "open link" notification, requiring explicit user interaction'.
rules.designImplication: On both platforms an NFC tap now leads to a notification the guest must tap. Printed NFC copy should therefore say 'Hold your phone near the card, then tap the link that appears'. Always pair NFC with a QR code and a printed short URL.

rules.source: DENSO WAVE (QR Code inventor) technical notes on ISO/IEC 18004; W3C 'Cool URIs don't change'
rules.rule: 'QR Code requires a four-module wide margin at all sides of a symbol'. Error correction levels are L, M, Q and H. M is most common; Q or H suit environments where codes get dirty. A cool URI is one which does not change.
rules.designImplication: Printed templates must reserve a 4-module quiet zone the theme cannot intrude on. Use dark modules on a light ground even in a dark 'Signature' print design (put the code on a light plate). Use a short, stable token URL so the code has fewer modules and is easier to scan. Details are in the QR/NFC field.

out.gbpPhotos:
Short answer: do not use the Business Profile APIs as the photo source for the guest portal. There are two lawful routes. (1) The property supplies its own original files, which it owns or has licensed; this is a future capability, since upload is safety-blocked in the beta. (2) Places API Place Photos, displayed live with strict attribution. For the beta, design with no photo.

Details:
(a) Business Profile APIs (Media: COVER, PROFILE/LOGO and category media via accounts.locations.media). The policies limit use to 'create, manage, and report on business listings that you either own or are authorized to manage'. Rendering a hotel's cover photo on a public guest page is not managing or reporting on the listing, so it is very likely outside the permitted scope. My confidence is medium because Google does not name this case explicitly. Other constraints:
- Content may not be pre-fetched, cached or stored except temporarily (30 days or less) and 'cannot be manipulated or aggregated in any way'. Cropping, tinting or overlaying a hero image is arguably manipulation.
- googleUrl 'is not static since it may change over time', so hotlinking will break.
- Customer media carries an Attribution object that 'You must display ... and must not delete or alter'. Those photos belong to guests, not the property.
- Tools must not replicate the Business Profile look and feel or imply Google endorsement.
RepKey already corresponds with Google about GBP data use (docs/external/google/). If photo reuse matters commercially, ask Google in writing rather than infer permission.
Sources: https://developers.google.com/my-business/content/policies (updated 2026-08-28); https://developers.google.com/my-business/reference/rest/v4/accounts.locations.media

(b) Google Maps Platform Places API (New), Place Photos. Display without a map is allowed, with conditions:
- The Google Maps logo or text attribution must appear.
- Every photo must credit its author (avatar, name, profile link), and users must be able to open the source on Google Maps (googleMapsUri).
- Nothing except place IDs may be cached or stored.
- Requests are billable.
- Photos may be user-contributed rather than the owner's, and you cannot reliably choose 'owner cover photo only'.
- EEA-billed customers are under separate GMP EEA terms, which should be checked before use.
This route is lawful but awkward. It adds Google branding next to a non-Google experience and an attribution chip over the hero, and the image choice is uncontrolled. That conflicts with a premium, controlled look. Medium-high confidence. Source: https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/places/web-service/policies (updated 2026-09-16)

(c) Copyright basis. Uploading photos to Google licenses them to Google but the uploader keeps ownership (Google Terms of Service, 'Your content'). So the property can simply give the same originals to RepKey. When upload is unblocked, add a rights attestation ('We own or have licence to these images') and a takedown path. Medium confidence; this is a general copyright principle, not legal advice.

Design consequence: every direction must look finished with no photo, using typography, colour field, texture or monogram. Photography is an optional 'future' layer that uses the property's own files, never Google's.
out.accessibility:
Obligation: under the EAA (Directive 2019/882, and in Bulgaria the Закон за изискванията за достъпност на продукти и услуги, in force 28.06.2025), a no-login feedback portal that concludes no consumer contract is probably not an 'e-commerce service' (Art. 3(30)). The hotel's booking engine reached from the link tree is in scope in its own right. Hotels that are microenterprises are exempt for services (Art. 4(5)). Medium confidence; counsel should confirm per customer, especially if a portal ever embeds booking or ordering. In the US, hotels and restaurants are ADA Title III public accommodations, and DOJ treats their web content as covered; that is low-to-medium relevance for the beta. Recommendation: treat WCAG 2.2 AA as the design bar. EN 301 549 v4.1.1 (ETSI, 2 Sep 2026) adopts WCAG 2.2 AA and maps it to the EAA. It is not yet cited in the Official Journal, so v3.2.1 (WCAG 2.1 AA) remains the formal reference for now.

WCAG 2.2 AA essentials for this UI:
1. Star rating (1.3.1, 4.1.2, 2.5.3, 1.4.1)
- Build it as a native radio group in a fieldset with a visible question as the legend.
- Each star gets an accessible name with a word, such as '1 of 5, Poor' up to '5 of 5, Excellent'. Show the word visibly on selection.
- Arrow keys move between stars.
- Selection must not rely on colour alone. Use a filled versus outline shape plus the text label.
- All stars start unselected.
2. No auto-submit on star tap (3.2.2 On Input). Keep an explicit Submit button, which the current UI already has. Activate on pointer-up so a press can be cancelled (2.5.2). No slider or swipe-only rating (2.5.7).
3. Target size (2.5.8): at least 24×24 CSS px is the legal floor. Design stars, language switch, link-tree rows, receipt actions and the privacy link at about 44–48 px. Leave spacing between the five stars so a mis-tap does not select a neighbour.
4. Contrast (1.4.3, 1.4.11)
- Body text needs 4.5:1; large text (24 px, or 18.66 px bold) needs 3:1.
- Star outlines, input borders, focus rings and the unselected-versus-selected difference need 3:1.
- Champagne or gold on ivory, and mid-grey on ink, commonly fail. Validate every theme token pair, and let admins pick only palettes that pass.
- Text over a hero photo needs a scrim or solid plate. Assume a worst-case image.
5. Focus (2.4.7, 2.4.11): a visible, designed focus ring on every control. Sticky headers, language bars and bottom docks must not cover the focused element.
6. Reflow and text size (1.4.10, 1.4.4, 1.4.12, 1.3.4)
- Works at 320 CSS px with no horizontal scroll.
- Supports 200% text and user text spacing without clipping, so avoid fixed-height cards.
- Portrait and landscape both work.
7. Language (3.1.1, 3.1.2)
- Set lang="bg" or lang="en" on html.
- Mark language-switch labels with their own lang ('Български', 'English').
- Label the switch with language names, not flags only. Flags are a best practice issue rather than a WCAG failure, but they denote countries, not languages.
8. Motion and media (2.2.2, 2.3.1, 1.4.2)
- An auto-playing hero video like Ratestar's needs a pause control if it runs longer than 5 s, and no autoplay audio.
- Honour prefers-reduced-motion for entrance, star and receipt animations. Never flash.
9. Text alternatives and structure (1.1.1, 2.4.2, 2.4.6, 2.4.4)
- The logo image's alt text is the property name; decorative imagery uses alt="".
- Page title like 'Rate your visit – [Property]'.
- One h1 plus logical headings and landmarks.
- Link text says where it goes: 'Write a review on Google (opens Google Maps)'. Mark external links and new-window behaviour.
10. Feedback form (3.3.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.3)
- The optional private-feedback textarea has a persistent label, not a placeholder-only label, a visible 'optional' marker and a live character count.
- Errors are identified in text.
- Submission success and the receipt are announced through a status message without moving focus unexpectedly.
11. Redundant Entry (3.3.7): the correct-or-withdraw flow pre-fills the guest's earlier rating and text instead of asking again.
12. Consistent Help (3.2.6): the privacy and help link stays in the same place across arrival, rating, receipt and error states.
13. Timing (2.2.1): if a correction window or session expires, say so and explain what happens. No silent timeouts on a draft.
14. Accessible Authentication (3.3.8) is satisfied by design, since there is no login and no CAPTCHA. Keep it that way; use invisible abuse controls rather than puzzles.
15. Print: the printed QR/NFC card is not WCAG content, but give it a large human-readable short URL, high contrast and a plain-language call to action. That also serves guests who cannot scan.
out.qrNfcPractice:
Stable URLs
- Print one opaque, high-entropy token URL per placement on a RepKey-controlled HTTPS domain (e.g. https://rk.example/p/Ab3xK9), matching ADR 0044's keyed-hash tokens.
- Include no personal data, no room numbers and no tracking query strings.
- Printed codes must survive content edits, republishing and rollback: the token resolves to the currently published snapshot. W3C's principle applies: 'Cool URIs don't change.'
- Revoking or rotating a token should show a gentle page ('This code is no longer active – [Property]') instead of a 404, with a grace period for rotation.
- Do not put third-party URL shorteners in print.
- Print the short URL in text under every code as a fallback. This also serves accessibility and phones without a scanner.

QR (DENSO WAVE / ISO/IEC 18004)
- Keep a 4-module quiet zone on all sides. Design templates so borders, text and illustrations never touch it.
- Use dark modules on a light background with strong contrast. For dark premium designs, place the code on a light plate; inverted or light-on-dark codes fail on some readers (medium confidence).
- Error correction M by default. Use Q or H when a centre logo is added (logo no more than about 20% of the area, never over finder patterns) or for table tents that get dirty.
- Shorter URLs give lower-version codes with bigger modules at the same print size.
- Rule of thumb, an industry heuristic with medium confidence: code width ≈ scanning distance ÷ 10, and at least about 2–2.5 cm for hand-held cards.
- Use a matte finish because glossy lamination glares under lobby lights. Avoid curved surfaces.
- Test on older iPhones and Androids in low light before printing.
- Add a clear call to action with an honest scope, e.g. 'Rate your visit – private, about 30 seconds'. Do not write 'Review us on Google 5★', which is a Google brand and gating problem, not only a style one.
- Anti-tamper ('quishing'): use tamper-evident mounting. The landing page should show the property name and the RepKey domain prominently so guests can check where they landed. The portal never asks for credentials or payment, and the copy can say so.

NFC (Apple Core NFC; Android NFC basics)
- Write one NDEF message whose first record is a URI record (TNF Well-Known, type 'U') with the same https token URL. iOS uses the first URI record; Android dispatches on the first record. Custom schemes do not work in iOS background reading.
- Use widely compatible NFC Forum Type 2 tags, e.g. NTAG213/215/216 (industry practice, medium confidence).
- Permanently lock tags after writing. Public, unlocked tags can be rewritten to a phishing URL.
- iPhone XS and later read tags in the background only while in use. Not available when the device has never been unlocked, the camera is open, Apple Pay Wallet is active, a Core NFC session is running, or airplane mode is on. A notification appears and the guest must tap it before Safari opens.
- Android reads when the screen is unlocked and NFC is on. From Android 16, http/https tags open via ACTION_VIEW. From Android 17 an 'open link' notification needs an explicit tap.
- Card copy: 'Hold the top of your phone to the card, then tap the link.' Always combine NFC with a QR code and the printed URL.
- Place the tag away from metal (or use on-metal tags), and mark the tap spot visually.

Measurement
- Count a scan only server-side when the page is actually requested by a browser. Filter link-preview bots and prefetchers so qualified_scans stays honest (already in ADR 0044).
- Never add per-guest identifiers to printed URLs.
openQuestions: Should the Google action be reachable without first giving the private rating (e.g. a quiet 'Go straight to Google' link on arrival)? FTC Example 11 and Google allow a rating-first flow when everyone is invited. Making the rating optional before Google would remove the remaining appearance of pre-screening. This would change a product rule, so the owner decides.

Should optional private written feedback be offered to every score in the same position, instead of only at or below the threshold? That would make the post-rating screen identical for all scores. It satisfies Tripadvisor's 'must be identical' rule, removes the only score-dependent difference, and avoids the CMA 4.4–4.5 perception of diverting unhappy guests. The threshold could then drive only internal alerting, not guest UI. This changes the Private Feedback Threshold's guest-facing meaning in docs/BETA.md.

Google branding: may RepKey, as a vendor, render Google's official G mark on customer portals under the Partner Marketing Hub 'Customer reviews' guidance, which is written for the business itself? Or should the beta use a text-only 'Google' label until Google confirms? The Partner Marketing Hub brand terms say use of brand features requires approval.

Should the portal ever show the property's rating on Google (e.g. '4.6 on Google, as of <date>')? The recommendation for beta is no. Showing it triggers UCPD Art 7(6), ЗЗП чл. 68е ал. 7 and DMCC 'consumer review information' duties, and it adds social-proof pressure.

Photo source: confirm with Google, through the existing policy correspondence in docs/external/google, whether GBP Media API content may be shown on the owner's own feedback page. The default assumption is no. The alternative is property-supplied originals with a rights attestation once image upload is unblocked.

EAA scope: counsel should confirm per customer whether any portal links into an embedded booking or ordering flow that RepKey hosts. That would make those pages e-commerce services under Directive 2019/882 and the Bulgarian law.
UK: if UK customers are planned, the DMCC Sch 20 para 13(4) 'offering services to traders' exposure means gating must remain technically impossible in RepKey, not merely discouraged.
Watch item: the EU Digital Fairness Act proposal (expected around 2026) may add dark-pattern and review rules. Re-check before general availability.

Bulgarian copy: a native-speaker legal or copy review of the BG strings for neutrality, e.g. avoiding imperatives like 'Оценете ни с 5 звезди' ('Rate us 5 stars') and any wording that implies a reward or pressure.
Android 17 NFC 'open link' notification behaviour and iOS background reading should be verified on real devices before printing NFC cards, because the printed instructions depend on it.

research.key: gap-1: Bulgarian Cyrillic type shortlist and mixed-script identity

competitors.name: Cormorant Garamond (Christian Thalmann)
competitors.category: Display face: shortlisted. High-contrast Garamond for the wordmark, the question and card titles
competitors.guestFlow: Rendered at weight 600 with HarfBuzz, language set. Question at 32px: EN 331.7px wide, BG 394.0px (x1.19). Google card title at 22px: EN 285.0px, BG 361.0px (x1.27). Private-feedback title at 22px: x1.10. Thank-you line at 26px: x1.23. Largest BG question size that stays on 2 lines at 320px is 35px. The 3-line limit at 320px is 43px, and that is also where the single word 'преживяването' stops fitting the 288px column.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Line counts, EN at 320/390 then BG at 320/390, with 16px gutters (288/358px) and 20px card padding (248/318px). Question at 32px: EN 2/1, BG 2/2. At 390 the BG question leaves 'ви?' alone on the last line, so it needs text-wrap: balance. Google title at 22px: EN 2/1, BG 3/2. Feedback title: EN 2/1, BG 2/2. Wordmark at 28px: the Latin 'Maxi Park Hotel & Spa' (255.6px) takes 1 line at both widths. The Cyrillic 'Къща за гости „Орехите“' (304.4px) takes 2 lines at 320 and 1 at 390. Largest one-line wordmark at 320px: Latin 31px, Cyrillic 26px.
competitors.visualStyle: Calm and carved-looking, with sharp high contrast. The Bulgarian forms (т shaped like m, д like g, в, г and others) look like upright italics and sit well beside the Latin. Of all the pairings rendered, its mixed Latin/Cyrillic wordmark looked the most unified. Best fit for Signature Stay or Carved Stillness.

crossCuttingPatterns: Method: 42 families were fetched from the Google Fonts css2 API with a Chrome user agent, plus the upstream google/fonts TTFs and Satoshi. Each served Cyrillic subset was checked for coverage of the 62 BG letters, the GSUB cyrl language systems, and actual HarfBuzz shaping with lang=bg against en and ru. Line counts come from HarfBuzz advances and greedy wrapping at spaces, not from a browser. Layout assumptions: 16px gutters (288px content at 320, 358px at 390), 20px card padding (248/318px), buttons with 20px side padding, and card buttons at 216/286px. Scripts and data are in the scratchpad fonts/ folder (measure.py, render.py, run_measure.py, measure_results.json).

The Google Fonts css2 subset keeps locl for every family where the upstream file has it. The count of substituted glyphs matched upstream exactly, e.g. 16 for Cormorant, 17 for Playfair 2, 15 for Manrope. So BG forms can be served from fonts.gstatic.com within the current CSP.

The same Google Fonts subsets drop the premium extras. Cormorant Garamond served from Google keeps only calt, ccmp, dnom, frac, liga, lnum, locl, numr and tnum. A self-hosted subset keeps smcp, c2sc, onum, case, dlig, ss01–ss15, cv01–05, sups and zero. Small-caps wordmarks, oldstyle figures and all-caps spacing with the 'case' feature therefore need self-hosted OFL files (allowed by font-src 'self').

Verified shortlist, display: Cormorant Garamond, Playfair 2 (not Playfair Display), Ysabeau / Ysabeau Office, Source Serif 4, and Lora. Commissioner is conditional. Text: Sofia Sans (Bulgarian forms by default), Ysabeau Office, and Manrope (BG buttons wrap at 320px). All are OFL.

BG takes more width than the character counts suggest. Characters, BG against EN: question +8%, legend +26%, submit +29%, intro +30%, thank-you +9%, Google title +13%, Google body -5%, Google button +6%, feedback title +3%, feedback body +11%, feedback button +14%, Google-unavailable body +2%. Rendered width is much higher: short bold labels x1.52–1.62, intro x1.53–1.62, feedback body x1.28–1.34, feedback button x1.35–1.37, Google body x1.13–1.18, Google button x1.15–1.20, display question x1.17–1.19, Google title x1.25–1.27. Budget +60% width for BG labels, +35% for body text and +25% for display titles.

The three-line question budget holds. At 32px the BG question takes 2 lines at 320px in Cormorant, Playfair 2 and Ysabeau, and 3 lines in Lora, Commissioner and Source Serif 4. It never exceeds 3 lines up to 36–43px. The real limit is the unbreakable 13-letter word 'преживяването'. It overflows a 288px column above 36px (Lora, Commissioner), 38px (Source Serif 4), 40px (Playfair 2), 41px (Ysabeau) or 43px (Cormorant). Largest 2-line BG question at 320px: Cormorant 35px, Ysabeau 33px, Playfair 2 32px, Source Serif 4 30px, Lora and Commissioner 29px. EN allows 43–51px. So the question size should be capped for BG around 32–34px at 320px, not scaled from EN.
Use text-wrap: balance on the question. Cormorant at 32px and 390px leaves 'ви?' alone on the second line.

Button labels are the first thing to break. 'Изпрати непубличната оценка' at 16px weight 600 fits one line at 320px only in Sofia Sans (228px) and Ysabeau (220px). It wraps in Manrope (254px), Montserrat (280px) and today's SF Pro fallback (264px). 'Изпрати обратната връзка' wraps in a card button at 320px in the same faces.

The current rating intro (previewRatingBody) is on the guest first screen and runs to 159 BG characters: 6 lines at 320px in every text face (7 in Montserrat), against 4 for EN. It will push the stars and submit button below the fold. Shortening it is a copy decision for the design.

Mixed scripts: in every shortlisted display face, a Latin wordmark above Cyrillic text and a Cyrillic wordmark above Latin text both looked coherent in the rendered sheets. The Cyrillic sample name ran 17–24% wider at the same size. Largest one-line Cyrillic wordmark at 320px is 22–26px, against 27–31px for the Latin one, so the wordmark needs its own size cap or a 2-line layout.

Because displayName is not localised, a Cyrillic name on an EN page (lang=en) gets Russian forms unless the wordmark element carries lang="bg" (for example set when the name contains Cyrillic), or the font's default glyphs are Bulgarian (Sofia Sans), or the file has Bulgarian forms made default.

Browser locl behaviour: the page already sets lang={selectedLocale} on the portal root, and HarfBuzz-based engines apply BGR locl from lang. Safari/iOS behaviour is unverified: Adobe's help page claims Safari does not support locl at all, which may be out of date. The only approaches that do not depend on the browser are a font whose default forms are Bulgarian (Sofia Sans) or a self-hosted Cyrillic file with Bulgarian forms made default. A proof-of-concept of the second, Cormorant Garamond 600 Cyrillic only, is 14.8KB and renders BG forms even with lang=en.

Size budget, Latin + Cyrillic: Google Fonts single static weights are 18–47KB per weight. Self-hosted static instances: Manrope 400 18.1KB, Sofia Sans 400 26.8KB, Commissioner 600 27.3KB, Lora 500 29.1KB, Ysabeau 400 33.8KB, Source Serif 4 500 51.0KB, Cormorant Garamond 600 52.8KB, Playfair 2 500 67.7KB. Variable files with an optical-size axis cost 212–287KB. Realistic pairings: Cormorant 600 + Ysabeau 400–600 ≈ 107KB self-hosted (≈ 83KB from Google Fonts without the extras). Playfair 2 + Sofia Sans ≈ 114KB. Lora + Manrope ≈ 59KB. With a unicode-range split, EN guests skip the Cyrillic files unless the displayName is Cyrillic.

Google Fonts static requests for optical-size families pin a text optical size: served Playfair weight 400 equals upstream at opsz 14 and wdth 100. Display contrast needs the opsz axis requested or a self-hosted display instance.

Privacy (inferred, not re-researched): loading from fonts.gstatic.com sends each guest's IP to Google, which EU case law (LG München, 2022) has treated as needing consent. Self-hosting OFL files fits RepKey's first-party, no-tracker guest promise better, and the CSP already allows font-src 'self'.

Direction impact: Signature Stay / Carved Stillness stays intact with Cormorant Garamond + Ysabeau, or with Ysabeau alone for a flared carved sans. No Optima- or Albertus-style inscriptional face with Bulgarian forms was found (Marcellus has no Cyrillic; Forum, Tenor Sans and Philosopher lack BG forms). Editorial Paper stays intact with Playfair 2, Cormorant or Source Serif 4, but only self-hosting (or the opsz axis) gives display optical sizes, small caps and oldstyle figures.
surprises: Satoshi has zero Cyrillic code points (Fontshare v2.000, 506 glyphs). Fontshare also returns only 400, 500 and 700 for the 400–700 request, so weight 600 falls back to 700. The current display face, Plus Jakarta Sans, has no Bulgarian letters either, although Google's CSS lists a 'cyrillic-ext' subset for it.

On iOS today, BG guests probably see correct Bulgarian forms by accident. The system fallback SF Pro has a BGR locl (checked on macOS SFNS.ttf), but its Cyrillic sits beside Satoshi Latin in the same line, as in 'Продължи към Google'.

The earlier note that Fira has Bulgarian forms is wrong for the Google Fonts build (4.203 has no BGR). Inter 4.001, EB Garamond, Literata, Noto Serif Display and Playfair Display 1.x also lack BG forms. Playfair 2, which Google lists as 'Playfair', has them.
Sofia Sans works the other way round: Bulgarian forms are the defaults and a RUS locl supplies Russian forms. It is the one face that stays correct wherever lang is missing or ignored.
Google Fonts keeps locl but silently strips small caps, oldstyle figures, case-sensitive forms and every stylistic set. It also serves the text optical size (opsz 14) for a static Playfair request.
Spectral has BG locl but no ѝ, a letter the live guest-ui-bg-v1 pack uses in privateFeedbackReceipt.
Commissioner's flare axis is hard to see even at 64px, so it cannot carry a 'carved' direction.

Specimen PNGs (2x) are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-bozhidardenev-kodes-projects-rep-key/a32bbf9b-d122-4570-974c-f838fece6ad5/scratchpad/fonts/specimens/. P1.png is Cormorant Garamond + Ysabeau on ink and champagne. P2.png is Playfair 2 + Sofia Sans on paper. P3.png is Commissioner + Manrope. P4.png is Source Serif 4 + Sofia Sans. Each shows EN and BG columns at 390 and 320px, with a Cyrillic wordmark over EN and a Latin wordmark over BG. display_mixed_script.png compares six display faces. today_bg_mixed_fallback.png shows today's Satoshi and SF Pro mix. The self-hosted test subsets are in fonts/selfhost/, including CormorantGaramond600-cyrillic-bgfrozen.woff2.

Web budget used: 8 of 12 network calls (4 curl/gh batches of CSS, font and upstream downloads, 2 WebSearch, 1 WebFetch that Medium blocked with 403, 1 gh issue read). google/fonts #4745, the proposal to add Bulgarian forms across Google Fonts, has been open since 2022-06-03. A 2026-07-02 comment there says Google's own default fonts still lack Bulgarian forms.

research.key: gap-2: Directions against the real brand inputs (the default palette and real BG properties)

competitors.name: Ratestar: live Maxi Park Hotel & Spa guest portal (the user-supplied reference)
competitors.category: Review-gateway portal, the Bulgarian competitor whose clients are RepKey's target properties
competitors.guestFlow: Public platforms first. Two photo cards, 'Google' and 'Tripadvisor', each show five filled gold emoji stars and the words 'Rate us'. The screenshot shows no private rating step. The vendor's smart-feedback page says 'At any rating - both a public review and a private form'. The vendor also sells 'Gamification: Reward customers who leave a review with prizes, perks or coupons', which RepKey has permanently ruled out.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: From the top at 390px wide: a full-bleed dark video hero taking roughly 60% of the first screen, showing the hotel's physical sign (a green and white mountain mark with MAXI and five stars); a white language pill with a flag, top right; 'Maxi Park Hotel & Spa' centred in white bold geometric sans at about 28px with a blue verified tick; an address with a pin emoji and a phone number with a phone emoji; three outline icons (website, Facebook, Instagram). Below the fold: a thank-you sentence, the two platform photo cards side by side, the property name again with an emoji description, then full-width photo link cards such as 'Book a room'.
competitors.visualStyle: A fixed black composition with white Montserrat-like type. The property's brand colours are not used. Maxi Park's own website uses gold #AA8453, sand #DDC8AD and Cormorant Garamond with Montserrat. None of that appears in the portal; the photo or video carries the brand. crossCuttingPatterns: METHOD: brand inputs were collected with read-only GET requests (curl) of each property's homepage HTML and linked CSS. I counted hex and rgb frequency and read CSS custom properties, meta theme-color, font-family declarations and the logo assets. Evidence for every property below is observed-live unless stated otherwise. I computed contrast with the same WCAG formula as src/contexts/portal/domain/portal-experience.ts contrastRatio. Derived colours come from shifting only OKLab lightness, which keeps hue and chroma. Scripts are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-bozhidardenev-kodes-projects-rep-key/a32bbf9b-d122-4570-974c-f838fece6ad5/scratchpad/brands/ (contrast.py, matrix.py, extract.py).

BRAND INPUT 0 (baseline): DEFAULT_PROPERTY_BRAND_PALETTE is primary #2563EB, background #FFFFFF, text #111827 (text/bg 17.74, primary/bg 5.17). The guest renderer's own fallback (portal-theme-style.ts DEFAULT_PRIMARY) and the admin 'Light' preset use #6366F1 instead, which is 4.47:1 on white.

BRAND INPUT 1: InterContinental Sofia (Ratestar client). Ratestar lists it as 'InterContinental Sofia by IHG' (29 characters, Latin, capital C mid-word). The logo is a monochrome black and white wordmark; Ratestar's own intercontinental.svg uses only black and white fills. ihg.com returns 403 to non-browser requests. Heritage brand colours from a third-party source: #53534D grey and #C8BA8C champagne. #D96932 is the IHG group orange, not the hotel brand. Likely Brand Profile: primary #000000 or #53534D, bg #FFFFFF, text #111111. Light polarity; a monochrome brand.

BRAND INPUT 2: THERMA NUMERA Longevity SPA (Ratestar client). og:site_name is 'Thermanumera Longevity & Spa' (28 characters, Latin even on the BG site, uppercase treatment, '& Spa'). The site defines two token sets. Dark: --tnp-ink #0B0C0C, panel #121414, cream #F2EFE9, blue #4DB8DD. Light: --tn-cream #F3EFE8, ink #141414, ink-soft #5E5A55, blue #628AA8. Fonts: Inter Tight for display, Cormorant Garamond and Playfair for serif, Fraunces italic (no Cyrillic), Manrope. The logo mark is black on transparent. Mixed polarity: dark hero panels over cream pages.

BRAND INPUT 3: Dobro Restaurant (Ratestar client; matching it to dobro.bg is inferred). The title is 'Ресторант ДОБРО' and the logo is heavy orange Cyrillic capitals 'ДОБРО'. Colours: orange #F5821F (27 uses, and the body background in one rule), green #7FB93C, dark #22272D. Font: Rubik. Light polarity with a loud orange.

BRAND INPUT 4: Restaurant Alpen Bansko (Ratestar client; alpen.bg is Italian, in Bansko). The wordmark is 'Alpen' (5 characters) with a bronze mountain logo. Colours: bronze #9C7C57, deep bronze #715B3E, gold #C9AB81, #111111 sections, #EBEBEB. Fonts: Metropolis, Caviar Dreams, Miniver script. Mixed polarity.

BRAND INPUT 5: Maxi Park Hotel & Spa, Velingrad (Ratestar client, and the property in the user's screenshot). og:site_name is 'Макси Велинград' (Cyrillic); the title is 'Макси Велинград | Парк Хотел & Спа | 5 звезди'. Ratestar uses the English 'Maxi Park Hotel & Spa' (21 characters). Colours: gold #AA8453, sand #DDC8AD, greige #D6D2D0, dark #2D2319 and #141827. Fonts: Cormorant Garamond and Montserrat. The site icon is white on transparent (pixel-sampled grey 224+), so it disappears on a light surface. The physical sign in Ratestar's video is a green and white mark. One property therefore has two different 'brand colours'.

BRAND INPUT 6: Щастливеца, a BG restaurant chain (shtastliveca.com). The name is 10 Cyrillic characters, with the tagline 'Колекция от вкусове и аромати'. meta theme-color is #8F1D19 (oxblood), with shades #84221C and #6A1B16, gold #DFB755 and a cream body #F6EFDF. Font: Merriweather. Light and warm.
BRAND INPUT 7: Sense Hotel Sofia (boutique; 17 characters). Body #F5F0DA cream, olive-grey #4E4E42, taupe #9C9686. Fonts: a custom 'SenseRegular' plus Prata. Light and nearly monochrome.
BRAND INPUT 8: Les Fleurs Hotel Sofia (boutique; 22 characters, French). Purple #663B83 (152 uses), navy #02043D, white background. Fonts: Playfair Display and Open Sans.

BRAND INPUT 9: Лъки Банско СПА & Релакс ('Aparthotel Lucky Bansko SPA & Relax', 35 characters, the longest name in the set). Explicit tokens: --bs-primary #54301A brown, medium #7C5330, light #A98568, surface #E5C9B3, surface-light #F5EBE0, secondary #EF851C orange. Fonts: Cormorant Infant and Raleway. Light and warm. Whichever of its two brand colours the admin picks as primary changes every result below.

BRAND INPUT 10: Happy Bar & Grill, a BG chain ('Верига ресторанти Happy Bar & Grill'). Loud red #E31E25 and #D90008 on white and black. Fonts: Roboto Condensed and Akrobat. Light polarity. This is the loud-red test case.

BRAND INPUT 11: Стария Чинар, restaurants in Varna and Sofia (12 Cyrillic characters). Tan gold #BA9774 and #CFA670, with dark #222222 sections. Fonts: Cormorant Garamond, Philosopher and Inter. Mixed polarity.

NAMES: display names run from 5 characters ('Alpen') to 35 ('Aparthotel Lucky Bansko SPA & Relax'). Five of the eleven properties lead with a Cyrillic name on their own site (ДОБРО, Макси Велинград, Щастливеца, Лъки Банско СПА & Релакс, Стария Чинар). Three carry '& Spa' or 'СПА & Релакс' suffixes, and several use capitals (THERMA NUMERA, ДОБРО, SPA). brandProfile.displayName is a single string that is not localised (limit 120), so a Cyrillic name will also appear on EN portals. Every direction's name slot needs a 2-line layout at 35 characters, allowing for the extra width of Cyrillic capitals.

CONTRAST 1, the enforced role: text/bg ranges from 15.0 to 21.0:1 across all eleven real properties, well above the enforced 4.5. Muted text (a 72% text mix, the current --portal-text-muted) passes 4.5 everywhere at 6.0 to 9.3:1.

CONTRAST 2, primary on the brand's own light background (stars, focus, link headings), which is not enforced today. Fails even 3:1: Dobro 2.59, Staria Chinar 2.70, Lucky orange 2.22, IC heritage champagne 1.93. Passes 3:1 but fails 4.5, so the link headings the current code paints in primary fail: Therma light 3.20, Maxi Park 3.42, Alpen 3.86, IHG orange 3.49, the #6366F1 fallback 4.47. Passes 4.5: the default 5.17, Happy red 4.69, Щастливеца 7.77, Sense 7.37, Les Fleurs 8.34, Lucky brown 9.83, IC black 21.

CONTRAST 3, on a dark stage built from the brand's own text colour the result flips. Dobro 5.80, Staria 5.88, Maxi 5.16, Therma 5.02, Alpen 4.89 and Lucky orange 7.17 all pass 4.5. Deep primaries fail even 3:1: IC black 1.11, Lucky brown 1.62, Щастливеца 1.95, Sense 2.07, Les Fleurs 2.32. The default blue on #111827 is 3.43 (fine for stars, not for link text); Happy red on #000 is 4.48.

CONTRAST 4, button text: picking black or white automatically (the existing readableForegroundOn) always reaches at least sqrt(21) = 4.58:1 for any colour; the data range is 4.69 to 21. A 'brand-harmonious' label (the background colour on primary, such as white on orange) fails for six brands: Dobro 2.59, Staria 2.70, Lucky orange 2.22, Therma light 3.20, Maxi 3.42, Alpen 3.86. Gold and orange buttons therefore need ink labels, which suits Signature Stay's ink-on-champagne look.

CONTRAST 5, stars: an unselected outline made from a 40% text mix scores 2.36 to 2.85 on every light palette, so it fails 3:1 everywhere. The mix each palette needs ranges from 42% to 49%, so a fixed 55% text-into-surface mix passes for all 15 inputs. A fixed gold star token (#F5B301) is 1.57 to 1.85 on every light surface and 8.1 to 11.3 on every dark stage. Champagne candidates #C9A96E, #D4B98C and #B89B72 score 1.9 to 2.6 on white, 1.7 to 2.3 on ivory #F6F1E7 and 6.7 to 9.4 on ink #111827. Gold stars and champagne accents are legitimate only on a dark stage.

CONTRAST 6, tinted surfaces: mixing primary into the background lowers the primary's own contrast. Therma light goes from 3.20 to 3.05 at a 5% tint and to 2.90 at 10%, which fails. Every derived token has to be checked against the surface it actually sits on, not against the stored background.

POLARITY GUARANTEE (proven, and matched by the data): for any primary p, max(contrast(p, bg), contrast(p, text)) is at least sqrt(contrast(text, bg)). All real inputs have text/bg of 15:1 or more, so choosing the stage per brand (background stage or text-colour stage) always gives stars and focus at least 3.87:1 with no derived colour. Twelve of the fourteen brand inputs reach 4.5 this way (the #6366F1 fallback 4.47 and Happy red 4.48 fall just short). The enforced floor of 4.5 on its own would only guarantee 2.12, and a text/bg of 20.25 would guarantee 4.5. The rule picks the text stage for Therma Numera, Alpen, Maxi Park, Staria Chinar, Dobro and Lucky orange, and each of their own sites (or Ratestar's portal) already uses dark sections. It picks the background stage for IC, Щастливеца, Sense, Les Fleurs, Lucky brown, Happy and the default.

DIRECTION FIT, Signature Stay (ink with champagne, dark): it can be built from the three hex values by inversion. Surface = the text hex, ink = the background hex, which keeps the validated text contrast exactly; accent = primary. It works with no changes for 6 of 14 inputs, exactly the gold, bronze, tan, orange and thermal-blue spa and mountain brands. It needs a lightened accent for the deep brands: Les Fleurs #663B83 becomes #794E97 for 3:1 or #9468B4 for 4.5; Lucky #54301A becomes #805942 or #9D745C; Щастливеца #8F1D19 becomes #B13F36 or #D35E53. Monochrome IC turns grey (#606060), which is meaningless, so there the ink should be the accent. The default turns into a navy-black stage with electric blue (#3A7AFF needed for link text), which reads as a SaaS dark mode rather than luxury. A black logo (Therma Numera's mark) disappears on this stage.

DIRECTION FIT, Quiet Welcome (ivory with evergreen, light): background maps to surface, primary to the button and stars, text to text. It works with no changes for deep primaries (7 of 14 pass 4.5). Gold and orange brands fail; Dobro reaches only 2.48 on a 5% tint. Ivory warmth cannot be derived from a white background: a 5% primary tint gives colour casts (#F4F7FE icy for the default, #FEF9F4 peach for Dobro, #FEF4F4 pink for Happy). Only 4 of the 11 properties already store cream (Щастливеца #F6EFDF, Sense #F5F0DA, Lucky #F5EBE0, Therma #F3EFE8).

DIRECTION FIT, Local Character (paper with a big primary wordmark, poster): the primary as large text needs at least 3:1 and passes for 11 of 14. Dobro 2.59, Staria 2.70 and Lucky orange 2.22 fail. Dobro #F5821F darkens to #E27100 at 3:1 (still orange) or #BF5100 at 4.5 (burnt orange, a visible brand change). Loud red works without changes: Happy #E31E25 is 4.69 on white and 4.69 for white on red. Blocks of primary with background-coloured text fail for mid-tone primaries (2.2 to 3.9), so the automatic black/white label is required. Monochrome brands become plain black-on-white typography with no colour to give the 'character'.

DERIVED TOKENS NEEDED (all computable from the three hex values, none shown to admins): (1) stage polarity, either fixed by the composition or chosen per brand; (2) accentGraphic: primary shifted in OKLab lightness until it reaches 3:1 against the actual surface, for stars, focus ring, rules and the large wordmark; (3) accentText: the same shift to 4.5:1, for link headings and small accent text (the current code uses raw primary and fails for 6 of 15 inputs on light); (4) onAccent: automatic black or white, which already exists; (5) starIdle: text mixed at least 55% into the surface; (6) surfaceTint: at most 4% primary, then recheck tokens 2 and 3; (7) a monochrome flag when contrast(primary, text) is below 3, true for 6 of 15 (IC 1.11, Lucky 1.62, Щастливеца 1.95, Therma dark 1.99, Sense 2.07, Les Fleurs 2.32), meaning hierarchy has to come from fills and scale rather than hue. These cannot be derived: ivory or paper warmth from a white background, champagne from a blue or red primary, photography, grain amount, and typeface. There is no font field in the Brand Profile.

ANSWER TO THE STRUCTURAL QUESTION: the evidence favours brand-agnostic compositions over palette-specific presets. (a) Colour roles for all 15 inputs can be met with derived tokens, with no new admin-facing colour. (b) Each composition's hardest constraint is polarity, not hue. Let polarity be chosen per brand, or let each direction ship both a light and a dark stage. (c) Texture or grain and the type pairing belong to the composition as constants; they are not palette inputs. (d) Signature Stay's champagne look can be recovered legitimately for exactly the cohort whose own brands are gold, bronze or tan on dark (Maxi Park, Alpen, Staria Chinar, Therma Numera). For deep-colour brands it has to become 'the same composition on a light stage'. (e) The only real preset-shaped gap is the default for properties with no brand. Replacing the SaaS-blue DEFAULT_PROPERTY_BRAND_PALETTE with a neutral hospitality default (proposal only) would avoid adding presets that compete with 'the guest page carries the property's brand'.

COMPETITOR THEMING MODELS: no product found derives surface, texture or polarity from a brand. Duve uses one brand colour on a fixed white surface with 16 curated fonts. Touch Stay offers curated font combinations and colour schemes, binary white or black cover text, and an overlay opacity slider. Ratestar uses a fixed black photo composition and, in the observed portal, ignores the brand colours. None of them enforces contrast; Touch Stay only gives tips. RepKey's existing 4.5:1 text/bg gate is ahead of them, but primary contrast is not enforced.

LOGO POLARITY CONSTRAINT: logoUrl is a single asset. Maxi Park's site icon is white on transparent (it vanishes on light stages), Therma Numera's mark is black on transparent (it vanishes on dark stages), Dobro's orange logotype is weak on white (2.59), and Alpen's bronze works on both. Choosing the stage has to consider logo luminance, which can be sampled from alpha-weighted pixels, or the composition needs a logo plate. That is a derived input, not an admin choice.

TYPOGRAPHY (Cyrillic checked through the Google Fonts CSS unicode-range, observed-live): these serifs cover Cyrillic: Cormorant and Cormorant Garamond, Playfair Display, Prata, EB Garamond, Lora, Forum, Literata, Spectral, Source Serif 4, Merriweather. These sans faces do too: Inter Tight, Montserrat, Manrope, Rubik, Unbounded, Tenor Sans. These fashionable display serifs have no Cyrillic: Fraunces, DM Serif Display, Instrument Serif, Newsreader, Bodoni Moda, Marcellus, Gloock, Young Serif. The BG sites converge on Cormorant (Therma Numera, Maxi Park, Staria Chinar, and Lucky as Cormorant Infant) with a geometric or grotesk sans (Montserrat, Inter Tight, Raleway). Signature Stay's serif must come from the Cyrillic-capable list.
surprises: The user's Ratestar reference screenshot shows Maxi Park Hotel & Spa, one of the live Ratestar clients. Its website brand (gold #AA8453 with Cormorant Garamond) appears nowhere on the portal, and the physical sign in its hero video is a green and white mark. Even one property has no single, unambiguous brand colour.

Code mismatch on main: the domain's DEFAULT_PROPERTY_BRAND_PALETTE primary is #2563EB, but the guest renderer's fallback (src/components/features/guest/public-portal/portal-theme-style.ts DEFAULT_PRIMARY) and the admin 'Light' preset (src/components/features/portal/portal-settings/theme-preset-selector.tsx) use #6366F1. That is 4.47:1 on white, and portal-secondary-links.tsx paints link headings in primary, so the fallback fails 4.5. Two colour systems also coexist: the Portal theme presets (Light, Dark #a5b4fc on #111827, and Brand #b45309 on #fffbeb) and the Property Brand Profile.

assertCompletePortalPublicationExperience (src/contexts/portal/domain/portal-experience.ts) calls contrastRatio(primaryColor, backgroundColor) but only checks that the result is not null. Primary contrast is never enforced, so an orange or tan brand at 2.2 to 2.7:1 publishes with stars and focus rings below the 3:1 non-text minimum.

The 4.5:1 floor alone guarantees little, but real brands sit at 15 to 21:1, and that is what makes automatic polarity safe (at least 3.87:1 for stars with no derived colour). A brand that sets a mid-grey text colour at exactly 4.5 would break this. A stricter text/bg floor for the guest stage (9:1 or more) would turn the guarantee into a rule. This is a proposal.

Luxury gold and champagne brands, the look Signature Stay was chosen for, fail on white and pass on ink. Deep boutique colours (purple, oxblood, olive, brown) do the opposite. The choice of direction is really a choice of polarity.

Canary's '3×3 curated type' could not be verified from any public source: the help centre is not public and press coverage returned 403. Duve's help centre sits behind a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge, which I did not bypass; the Duve Styles details come from the search-result snippet of that help page.

Research disclosure: I used 10 of the 12 allowed WebSearch and WebFetch calls. Brand colours, logos, the Touch Stay help articles and the Google Fonts Cyrillic check came from read-only curl GET requests. These are not counted as web-tool calls but are disclosed here. Nothing was submitted, signed up for or clicked, and no browser was used.

research.key: gap-3: The first-visit analytics disclosure versus the claim that no banner is needed

competitors.name: RepKey guest portal: current 'Portal analytics information' bar (baseline)
competitors.category: Own product baseline (read from source on codex/portal-experience-design and main, not rendered)
competitors.guestFlow: The facts come from the source; the geometry is an estimate. src/routes/p/$token.tsx mounts <GuestAnalyticsNotice> as a sibling before <PublicPortalContent>. The component shows only in the client, after hydration. A mount effect records the visit (recordScan) whether or not the guest acknowledges the notice. The code comment says acknowledgement 'never enables or disables measurement'. The only control is 'Got it' ('Разбрах' in BG). The FirstVisit story asserts there is no reject or decline button. Clicking it writes localStorage 'guest-analytics-notice-acknowledged'='true' and unmounts the region. Device-side storage in play: (1) cookie rk_guest_session: HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/p/, Max-Age 24h, a server-issued random UUID, used for CSRF, response integrity, one correction/withdrawal and the shared-device reset. (2) localStorage acknowledgement flag. (3) sessionStorage 'guest-scan-recorded:<token>:<csrfNonce>' = 'pending'/'recorded', which exists only to stop the visit metric counting twice. Separately, the 'network marker' is a server-side keyed HMAC-SHA256 of the IP, scoped to Organization, Portal, action and UTC day, with a 7-day expiry. It serves abuse-pressure checks, including the qualified-scan check, and nothing about it is stored on the device.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: The element is fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0 z-50, with border-t, bg-background and p-4. Inside: flex-col below 640px, a text-sm muted paragraph of 242 characters in EN (221 in BG), then a right-aligned size-sm (h-8) 'Got it' button. Estimated (not measured) height at 375x667: about 5-6 lines x 20px + 12px gap + 32px button + 32px padding, so roughly 175-200px. That covers about 27-30% of the 667px layout viewport and about a third of iPhone SE Safari's visible area with toolbars. Content order in <main> (max-w-lg, space-y-8, py-8) is language nav, optional logo, optional hero (h-48), h1 plus accent rule plus org name, optional description, then the rating form. On a short phone the stars and 'Submit private rating' therefore often land in the bottom third, directly under the bar. The e2e helper comment confirms the bar intercepts pointer events on the submit button and on trailing controls.
competitors.visualStyle: A generic shadcn cookie-bar look: white or background surface, hairline top border, muted small copy, primary small button. The FirstVisit story pins the classes 'border-border' and 'bg-background'. It carries no portal branding (it ignores --portal-primary). In all three premium directions it reads as a system interruption laid over the property's page.
competitors.compliance: The bar is neither a consent mechanism nor legally required in this form. If every piece of device storage is exempt (see crossCuttingPatterns), no banner or bar is needed; GDPR Art. 13 transparency is met by the /privacy notice plus an inline pointer. If the visit-dedupe storage is not exempt, Bulgarian ZET Art. 4a(1) requires Art. 13 information plus a way to refuse, and EU-conform reading (Planet49) requires prior consent. An acknowledge-only bar that never changes measurement satisfies neither. The copy also concedes an analytics use of IP-derived data ('we count this visit using a ... network marker'), which is the weakest point under EDPB Guidelines 2/2023 para 55. docs/legal/privacy-notice.md never uses the word 'cookie' for guests and does not list the localStorage or sessionStorage keys.
standoutIdeas: The measurement side-effect is already independent of acknowledgement: the visit is recorded on mount and the 'Got it' state only hides the text. The disclosure can therefore move anywhere in the layout without touching analytics semantics, as long as the component (or its recordPortalVisit effect) stays mounted.

Because acknowledgement is stored per browser and the region unmounts after the click, an inline version can collapse after dismissal. A shift that follows the guest's own tap within 500ms is excluded from CLS.
antiPatterns: A fixed bottom overlay on a rating-first page puts the disclosure over the exact controls (stars, submit) the page exists for.
'Got it' with no effect on processing looks like consent UI but gives no choice. EU regulators criticise that pattern, and it adds nothing if the processing is exempt.
The body copy names two mechanisms and a business purpose in 242 characters of 14px text, too long for a first-screen interruption.
The disclosure appears only after hydration. Any in-flow placement above the rating block would push the stars down after first paint (CLS).

competitors.name: Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (Dutch DPA) public website
competitors.category: EU regulator's own public site: no-banner reference
competitors.guestFlow: I fetched the pages with an iPhone user agent and checked only the served HTML; JavaScript was not executed. The homepage and 'De AP en privacy' contain no consent-banner markup: no 'cookiebanner', 'cookie-banner', 'cookieconsent' or 'consent' strings, and no OneTrust, Cookiebot, Matomo, Piwik, Siteimprove, gtag or Google Analytics identifiers. The only scripts are first-party Drupal bundles and jQuery. Privacy information sits behind a footer link, 'De AP en privacy', which leads to cards for Privacyverklaring (privacy statement), Privacybeleid, Uw rechten, Verwerkingsregister and CVD.
competitors.mobileAnatomy: No overlay and no first-visit bar in the served HTML. The footer navigation is Contact / Over deze website / De AP en privacy / Werken bij de AP. The privacy page is a stack of short headed cards, each with one explanatory sentence and a 'Lees...' link.
competitors.visualStyle: Government editorial layout. Privacy is presented as a calm, linked information architecture, not as an interruption.
competitors.compliance: A national DPA runs with no banner and relies on a footer link to its privacy statement. Caveats: this is the Netherlands, whose Telecommunicatiewet has an analytics carve-out that Bulgaria lacks (from prior knowledge, not re-verified this session). I also could not rule out a banner injected later by the first-party JS bundle.
standoutIdeas: Privacy as a quiet footer destination with a clear, short label.
The destination page layers the information: one sentence per topic, then a deep link. This fits a RepKey /privacy page with a 'Cookies and device storage' section.
antiPatterns: It gives no point-of-collection sentence. For a form that collects a rating, the layered-notice approach suggests a one-line pointer near the submit button as well as the footer link.

competitors.name: Stripe hosted Checkout / Payment Links (Stripe Payments Europe, IE)
competitors.category: Closest analogue: no-login public mobile page often reached by QR, with essential fraud and security cookies
competitors.guestFlow: From prior knowledge, not fetched this session because the 12-call web budget was spent on the legal sources. A QR code or link opens a hosted page directly. There is no cookie banner on the payment page. Necessary fraud-prevention and session cookies are set, and the privacy and cookie policy is reached through a small footer ('Powered by Stripe | Terms | Privacy').
competitors.mobileAnatomy: Merchant name and amount at the top, the form, the primary CTA, then a single muted footer line of legal links under the CTA. Nothing overlays the CTA.
competitors.visualStyle: Neutral, merchant-branded surface. Legal text sits at the smallest type size, below the action, in muted colour.
competitors.compliance: This is the pattern RepKey would adopt: strictly-necessary security and session storage, no banner, and a privacy link placed where the action happens. It is not verified this session.
standoutIdeas: Legal and privacy line placed directly under the primary action, not over it.
No first-visit interruption at all on a page whose whole purpose is one action.
antiPatterns: Footer-only disclosure is easy to miss. RepKey should say 'essential cookie, 24 hours' in plain words in the inline line, not only behind a link.

crossCuttingPatterns: CITATION CORRECTION (verified in the primary consolidated texts): the Bulgarian transposition of ePrivacy Art. 5(3) is Закон за електронната търговия (ZET) чл. 4а (new, ДВ бр. 105/2011, in force 29.12.2011; ал.1 т.1 amended ДВ бр. 17/2019), not ЗЕС чл. 4а. ЗЕС чл. 4а (new, ДВ бр. 20/2021) covers radio-spectrum policy coordination, and ЗЕС contains no terminal-storage provision (Ciela consolidation dated 09.07.2026). Sources: kik-info.com ZET page (current to ДВ 55/2026); damtn.government.bg ЗЕС PDF.

ZET чл. 4а as written. ал.1: a provider may store or access information in the recipient's terminal only if (1) it gives clear and comprehensive information under GDPR Art. 13 and (2) the recipient has the option to REFUSE. ал.2: information about stored data must be available at any time. ал.3: later storage by the same provider does not re-trigger ал.1 if the recipient has not objected. ал.4: ал.1 does NOT apply where storage or access is 'necessary' for (1) transmitting a communication or (2) providing an information-society service explicitly requested by the recipient. The literal Bulgarian regime is inform-plus-opt-out, lighter than the directive's 'consent'. EU-conform reading after CJEU Planet49 (C-673/17, from prior knowledge) treats non-exempt storage as opt-in. For exempt storage, both the consent and the ал.1 information duty fall away.

Enforcement: ZET чл. 20 gives supervision to the Комисия за защита на потребителите (КЗП), not КЗЛД. ZET чл. 24 fines are 250-1500 лв (individual) or 500-2000 лв (company), and 500-2500 / 1000-4000 лв for repeats. КЗЛД remains the authority for the GDPR side (Art. 13 transparency, lawful basis). I found no КЗЛД cookie-specific guidance within the call budget; that is still a gap.

EDPB Guidelines 2/2023 on the technical scope of Art. 5(3), v2.0 adopted 7 Oct 2024 (read in full from the EDPB PDF). Para 42: routing identifiers such as the IP address and session identifiers can fall under Art. 5(3). Para 55: 'gaining access to IP addresses would only trigger the application of Article 5(3) ePD in cases where this information originates from the terminal equipment' (static IPv4, IPv6); unless the entity can show otherwise, it must follow Art. 5(3). Para 56: applicability 'does not systematically mean that consent needs to be collected'; exemptions must be assessed case by case. Consequence: the IP-HMAC 'network marker' is safest framed and used as security or abuse protection, not as the visit counter.

CNIL, the most concrete EU guidance fetched: exempt trackers include authentication, security and anti-bot, user-interface preferences, load balancing, remembering the cookie choice, and audience measurement under conditions ('que dit la loi', 29 Sep 2020). The audience-measurement exemption (page updated 4 Jul 2025) requires a purpose strictly limited to the publisher's own audience measurement, anonymous statistics only, no cross-referencing with other processing, and no cross-site tracking. It recommends a 13-month tracker life and 25-month data retention, and says users should be informed, for example through the privacy policy, not through a banner. Bulgaria's ZET 4а(4) has no equivalent analytics carve-out.

Classification of RepKey's device-side items (from source): (a) rk_guest_session (24h, HttpOnly, CSRF plus response integrity, correction, withdrawal, shared-device reset) falls within 'explicitly requested service' and security, so it is exempt. (b) The localStorage acknowledgement flag works like CNIL's 'remember the choice' tracker and is exempt; it disappears if the bar does. (c) The sessionStorage 'guest-scan-recorded:*' marker exists only to dedupe the qualified_scans metric. It is the one item not squarely strictly necessary for the guest-requested service, and under a literal ZET reading it needs information plus a refusal option. (d) The network HMAC is server-side, with nothing stored on the device; it is in scope for Art. 5(3) only via EDPB para 55. Recommendation for counsel: remove (c) and dedupe the visit server-side, keep (d) scoped to abuse pressure, and have the count be 'portal page served to a signed session' on the server. Then everything on the device is exempt and no banner is needed. Caveat, from CNIL's multi-purpose rule (prior knowledge, not re-fetched): reusing rk_guest_session as the dedupe key mixes an exempt and a measurement purpose, so counsel should confirm the count itself qualifies as exempt, CNIL-style anonymous first-party measurement.

ANSWER TO THE GAP: an inline, non-blocking sentence is sufficient once all device storage is exempt. Neither ePD 5(3) nor ZET 4а imposes a notice duty for exempt storage. GDPR Art. 12/13 requires concise, easily accessible information at collection, which a one-line pointer next to the rating submit plus a proper /privacy section satisfies (layered-notice approach from the WP29/EDPB transparency guidelines WP260, prior knowledge). A dismissible overlay is only warranted if the product keeps non-exempt storage, and then it must offer a real refusal, which the current 'Got it' does not. The current bar is therefore the worst of both.

Required privacy-notice change (docs/legal/privacy-notice.md): add a 'Cookies and device storage' table listing rk_guest_session (purpose, 24h, strictly necessary), each browser-storage key and its purpose and lifetime, and the server-side network pseudonym (7-day expiry, abuse protection only). Today the guest section never uses the word 'cookie' and omits the storage keys.

INLINE DISCLOSURE COPY, suggested for all three directions (about 110 characters, 2 lines at 12-13px): EN 'No ads or trackers. An essential cookie keeps your response secure for 24 hours. Privacy notice'. BG 'Без реклами и проследяване. Задължителна бисквитка пази отговора ви 24 часа. Поверителност'. Place it directly below the 'Submit private rating' button, or in the receipt after submission, in the portal's muted tone, never above the stars. Placing it before the stars would shift them down when the client-only notice hydrates (CLS).

E2E CONTRACT a new layout must keep (verified in source): (1) An element with role 'region' whose English accessible name is exactly 'Portal analytics information' (a <section aria-label> or role='region' plus aria-label; BG label 'Информация за аналитичните данни на портала'). (2) Inside it, a button whose accessible name is exactly 'Got it' (BG 'Разбрах'). (3) It must become VISIBLE for any guest without the localStorage acknowledgement. e2e/helpers/guest-consent.ts settleGuestConsent waits for visible with no presence probe and is called 5 times in e2e/critical/guest-portal.spec.ts (lines 82, 101, 170, 449, 470); beta-product-journeys.spec.ts:150 clicks it unconditionally, and :522 only if visible. (4) After the click the region must DETACH from the DOM, not merely hide (waitFor state 'detached'). (5) It must not render again once acknowledged. None of this requires position:fixed. An in-flow region under the submit button passes, because Playwright scrolls to 'Got it' automatically, and it leaves the stars and submit unobstructed at 375x667. Storybook-only pins that would need editing if copy or style changes: FirstVisit asserts the text /short-lived, privacy-protected network marker/i, no reject/decline button, and the classes 'border-border' and 'bg-background'; AcknowledgeDismissesNotice asserts the localStorage key. Language-pack keys are analyticsLabel, analyticsBody and analyticsAcknowledge. Dropping the region entirely would make all seven e2e call sites time out, so the helper must change in the same PR.

Design implication for the three directions: first-screen composition no longer needs to reserve about 175-200px of bottom safe area for an overlay. The rating block can own the lower half of a 375x667 screen. The privacy line becomes a designed typographic element (caption or small-caps, the portal's muted token, a hairline above), with 'Got it' styled as a tertiary text button. Recommended: 'Got it' stays in the region to satisfy the contract, and the region collapses after the tap, which does not count toward CLS.
surprises: The brief's legal citation is wrong. Bulgaria's Art. 5(3) transposition is ZET (Закон за електронната търговия) чл. 4а, enforced by the consumer-protection commission (КЗП) with fines of 500-2000 лв for companies. ЗЕС чл. 4а is about radio spectrum.

The Bulgarian statute literally uses an inform-plus-right-to-refuse model and says only 'necessary', not 'strictly necessary'. That is looser wording than the directive, though EU-conform interpretation likely tightens it.

The only clearly non-exempt device storage in the portal is the sessionStorage marker that dedupes the visit metric. The fixed bar and its localStorage flag exist mostly to disclose that marker and the IP-derived counting, and removing the marker would remove the legal reason for any bar.

The current bar is acknowledge-only by design: the stories assert there is no reject button and the code never gates measurement. It therefore cannot serve as consent, so if consent were needed the bar would already be non-compliant, and if it is not needed the bar is surplus.

The shipped copy links the IP-derived network marker to counting visits. Under EDPB 2/2023 para 55, that framing is the riskiest one available. The data inventory says the marker's purpose is abuse pressure.
The guest privacy notice never uses the word 'cookie' and does not list the browser-storage keys, even though the bar tells guests an essential session cookie exists.
The Dutch DPA's own site serves no consent-banner markup and no third-party analytics, and relies on a footer privacy link (served HTML only).

Budget note: all 12 web calls were used, 3 of them as curl downloads to read the ZET text, the EDPB PDF and the AP pages verbatim. Not verified this session: КЗЛД cookie guidance, the WP29 04/2012 and WP260 texts, Planet49, Stripe's live page, and the CNIL multi-purpose-tracker rule. Treat those as prior knowledge for counsel to confirm. This is not legal advice.

critic.coverageVerdict: Coverage is good enough to build three directions on. The research covers the direct BG competitor (Ratestar, including its shipped gating code), review SaaS, guest apps and restaurant tools, the Google hand-off (sign-in wall, labelling friction before the guest leaves), the no-gating policy for Google, FTC, UCPD, the Bulgarian consumer law, DMCC and Tripadvisor, rating-control UX, motion, and every current guest state in the codebase. Adding more competitors would only add breadth. Three things are still open, and each could change how the directions look and are built. First, every direction's premium feel depends on typography, and that has not been checked against Bulgarian Cyrillic. Second, nobody has tested the proposed palettes (ink/champagne, paper/graphite, saturated field) against the brand model that actually ships: three free hex colours per Property, with #2563EB/#FFFFFF/#111827 as the default. Third, the UX-patterns research claims 'no cookies, so no banner', but the codebase has an essential session cookie and an analytics notice fixed to the bottom of the first screen that e2e tests pin. The notice text in guest-language-pack.ts:102 confirms this.

gaps.topic: Bulgarian Cyrillic type shortlist and mixed-script identity
gaps.why: With no photos or logos allowed in the beta, typography is the main thing that makes a page look premium. Yet the research lists candidate faces without checking them. Cormorant, Playfair and Lora are flagged as 'needs per-font check'. Only Sofia Sans and Fira are reported to have Bulgarian locl forms, and Google Fonts has an open issue about missing Bulgarian forms. Satoshi, the current guest font loaded from api.fontshare.com in src/styles.css, is probably Latin-only, so BG guests likely get a fallback font today. brandProfile.displayName is a single string per Property that is not localised, so the wordmark may be Latin (for example 'Maxi Park Hotel & Spa') above Cyrillic page text, or the reverse. If no flared or high-contrast serif with good Cyrillic and Bulgarian forms can be served within the CSP (Google Fonts or self-hosted OFL), 'Carved Stillness' and 'Editorial Paper' change character. The three-line question budget also rests on an untested guess about how long BG strings are.
gaps.whatToResearch: Build a verified shortlist of 4–6 display faces and 3–4 text faces. For each: Cyrillic coverage, whether it has a Bulgarian `locl` feature, whether the Google Fonts CSS API subset keeps that feature (compare it with a self-hosted file), licence, and WOFF2 size for the Latin plus Cyrillic subset. Render the real guest-ui-bg-v1 and guest-ui-en-v1 strings side by side at 320 and 390px in each candidate pairing: the question, 'Submit private rating', the Google card, and the private-feedback card. Also render a Latin displayName wordmark above Cyrillic body text and a Cyrillic displayName above Latin text. Confirm Satoshi's Cyrillic coverage. Record how much longer BG runs than EN, and the line counts, for each first-screen string.

gaps.topic: Directions against the real brand inputs (the default palette and real BG properties)
gaps.why: Guests only ever receive the Property Brand Profile: primary, background and text hex values, with only text on background contrast-checked at 4.5:1 or above. The default is a SaaS blue on white. The three seed directions each assume a fixed, art-directed palette and texture. Nobody has tested whether each direction can be built from those three hex values, whether it survives the default palette or a loud brand red or orange, or whether a direction has to become a curated preset. A preset would mean new tokens for surface, star accent and grain, and it would compete with 'the guest page carries the property's brand'. The answer decides whether the directions are brand-agnostic compositions or palette-specific themes, which is the most important structural choice in the design.
gaps.whatToResearch: Collect brand inputs from 8–12 real target-type properties. Include the live Ratestar clients (InterContinental Sofia, Therma Numera, DOBRO, Alpen Bansko, Maxi Park Velingrad) and a few BG boutique hotels and restaurants. For each, record the display name (script, length, words such as '& Spa'), the brand colours taken from the website or logo, and the light or dark polarity. Map each seed direction onto primary, background and text for those inputs and for DEFAULT_PROPERTY_BRAND_PALETTE. Measure contrast for each role: stars and focus at 3:1 against the surface, button text, and link headings. List any role that needs a derived or extra token. Also check how Canary (3×3 curated type) and Duve Styles or Touch Stay derive a full theme from a single accent colour.
