gaps.topic: The first-visit analytics disclosure versus the claim that no banner is needed
gaps.why: The UX-patterns research calls 'no consent banner' a premium advantage to keep. The codebase contradicts it. An essential session cookie and a short-lived network marker are disclosed in a bar fixed to the bottom of the screen. That bar, the 'Portal analytics information' region with its 'Got it' button, must stay under the constraints and is pinned by e2e. It shows on every load until the guest dismisses it and sits over the stars and submit area on small phones. No agent looked into how little that disclosure legally has to be. It might sit inline under the rating as the privacy line, or it might need to be a dismissible overlay. Either answer changes the first-screen composition in all three directions.
gaps.whatToResearch: Check the ePrivacy Art. 5(3) strictly-necessary exemption and its Bulgarian transposition (ЗЕС чл. 4а), plus EDPB/CNIL/КЗЛД guidance, to see whether an essential session cookie plus a first-party, server-side visit count needs any notice beyond the privacy notice. If it does, find out whether an inline, non-blocking sentence satisfies it. Find 2–3 compliant EU examples of inline 'essential only' disclosures on public mobile pages. Say which parts of the e2e-pinned region (its role, name, and the 'Got it' button) a new layout would have to keep, so the rating block stays unobstructed on a 375×667 screen.

synth.executiveSummary:
RepKey can take a position no competitor in the Bulgarian/EU hospitality market holds: a guest page as beautiful as the property's own printed stationery that is also provably fair. The research covers Ratestar's live portals and its shipped JavaScript, about 14 review SaaS tools, about 14 hospitality guest apps and survey suites, about 17 restaurant and link-hub tools, primary UX and policy sources, and three gap studies (Bulgarian Cyrillic type, real BG brand palettes, the analytics notice). It converges on six findings.

(1) Premium in this category is bought with photography and video. No competitor has a designed no-photo state: Ratestar shows black boxes when images fail, and TrustYou's default is a plain form. RepKey's upload block (SAFE-01) turns into an advantage if every direction is type-, colour- and texture-led first and photo-ready second.

(2) Review gating is the industry default, often sold as a headline feature. Ratestar auto-redirects ratings above 3 stars to the platform after 200ms, despite marketing that says it doesn't gate. me&u, Canary, Akia, Touch Stay, Tablein and sunday gate by score, and so does a TrustYou toggle. Google's Maps policy, FTC Example 11, EU UCPD 23c and its Guidance, Bulgarian consumer law (ЗЗП чл. 68ж), UK DMCC Sch. 20, CMA208 and Tripadvisor's identical-UI rule all condemn selective solicitation. RepKey's score-invariant Google card is compliance, a sales argument ('the version that cannot get your Google profile flagged') and a visual design rule at once.

(3) The winning first screen is identity plus one question with five large empty stars, visible word anchors, an explicit submit, and a one-line privacy promise at the action. There is no gate, no overlay, no video and no platform grid.

(4) Bulgarian is a design constraint, not a translation. Satoshi has zero Cyrillic, and most 'premium' serifs (Playfair Display, EB Garamond, Prata, Forum) show Russian letterforms to Bulgarian readers. The verified shortlist with Bulgarian forms is Cormorant Garamond, Playfair 2, Ysabeau, Source Serif 4, Lora, Sofia Sans, Manrope and Commissioner, self-hosted. BG labels render up to 1.6x wider than EN.

(5) On brand inputs, real BG property palettes pass text/background contrast at 15 to 21:1. But their primaries fail as stars or accent text on a light stage for 6 of 15 inputs, while gold, tan and orange brands pass on a dark stage. The real design choice is polarity per brand plus derived colour roles, not a set of preset themes.

(6) Guest copy must be honest: 'Opens Google, you may need to sign in', never 'Thanks for your review'.

The six candidates below share one invariant rating core: the same star geometry, the same Google card for every score, the private-note card added below it at or under the threshold, a one-line receipt with Change, and a quiet 'Your response' area. They differ in structure and visual system:
- C1 Carved Stillness: Signature Stay evolved; dark tonal cover, carved serif, grain.
- C2 Folio: editorial paper page with an index of links.
- C3 Table Card: brand colour-field poster with a light rating plate, continuous with print.
- C4 Pass: placement card object with a tear-off receipt.
- C5 One Thing at a Time: thumb-zone steps with pure type.
- C6 Window: place pattern seen through an architectural frame that later holds a photo.

Recommendation: prototype C1 (default for hotels and spas), C3 (restaurants and loud brands) and C2 (light boutique, and the polarity twin C1 needs for deep brand colours) as a curated beta family over one shared component. Keep C4 to C6 as alternates.

Separately from the redesign, fix the defects in today's guest page:
- The selected star has no visual state.
- Manager policy copy is shown to guests.
- The app's dark theme leaks into /p.
- Deadlines are shown in UTC with no zone label.
- The fixed analytics bar covers the submit button.
- Primary colour contrast is never enforced at publish.
- The admin preview does not render what guests actually see.
ratestarTakeaways: The owner's reference screenshot is Ratestar's own marketing demo (Maxi Park Hotel & Spa, Velingrad, from its mockup video), not a neutral client example. It shows the vendor's flagship template, which is reused across its hotel, restaurant and beauty pages.

Strength to beat: a strong sense of place. The hero film shows the property's physical sign, and the photo cards make each destination feel tangible. RepKey has to match that feeling without photography: a wordmark system built from displayName, tonal fields from the brand's own hex values, grain, and patterns or frames. Owned photography comes later.

Strength to beat: the review action sits above the fold at 375x812 even on a long hub page. RepKey should go further and put the whole rating block (question, stars, submit) in the first screen at 375x667 with the Safari toolbars showing, with nothing above it except identity.

Strength to beat: useful follow-on content (booking, spa, menu, map, contact) and 'same QR, new content'. RepKey's stable tokens plus draft, publish and rollback are stronger than immediate edits. Its link rows should be calmer, capped at four visible, and grouped.

Strength to beat: Ratestar sets the 'premium' bar in the BG market (InterContinental Sofia, Therma Numera, Maxi Park). Owners will compare RepKey against it side by side, so the beta must look finished, not like a form.

Weakness to avoid: public platforms come first and the portal page has no private step. The 'Google Reviews' label opens a Ratestar form on some portals and Google directly on others, and Tripadvisor is sometimes direct. The CTA label does not say what happens next.

Weakness to avoid (from the shipped JS, not exercised live): ratings above nrpThreshold (default 3) auto-redirect to the platform after 200ms. The public invite can be limited to 3 stars or more. The back button is trapped with pushState. Confetti fires on every submit, a '98% of customers trust reviews' nudge appears, and a click is recorded as a 'converted' review. That contradicts its own 'we don't gate' FAQ. RepKey should show its fairness in the UI (identical Google card), not just claim it.

Weakness to avoid: five filled gold emoji stars inside the 'Google' and 'Tripadvisor' cards prime the expected score, and they break Google's and Tripadvisor's brand guidance (no stars next to the Google name; use Tripadvisor bubbles only as supplied).
Weakness to avoid: a self-issued blue 'verified' seal next to the property name imitates platform verification. RepKey must never use seals or Google-like styling.

Weakness to avoid: emoji used as UI (pin, phone, fleur-de-lis, pointing hands, vote boxes), a crowded centred hierarchy, the property name repeated twice, and off-mission blocks (award-vote CTA, discount promo) competing with the review moment.

Weakness to avoid: the property's brand colours are ignored. Maxi Park's site uses gold #AA8453 and Cormorant Garamond; the portal is generic black with Montserrat. RepKey should derive the page from the property's own colours and use a Cyrillic-correct, curated type pairing, so two properties never look like the same template.

Weakness to avoid: the language pill swaps only the UI chrome, so there are /en pages in Bulgarian and /bg pages in English, and it uses a flag. RepKey should use native-name text controls and translated content per locale (including link labels), and flag missing translations before publish.

Weakness to avoid: a heavy autoplay mp4 hero served from storage costs LCP and roaming data on hotel Wi-Fi, and failed images leave black boxes. RepKey's no-photo variant should stay under about 150KB and render server-side instantly.

Weakness to avoid: no privacy notice on the portal, public indexing (robots follow, index), live typos on 5-star client pages ('INTERCONTINTENTAL'), gamification sold on higher tiers (scratch card, wheel of fortune, prizes), staff review leaderboards, and device fingerprinting. RepKey's noindex, first-party, no-tracker, no-incentive posture should be visible in one line on the page.

Sales takeaway: hotel buyers arrive expecting gating as a feature, because NFC and QR hardware vendors openly sell 'filtration'. RepKey's admin onboarding needs a short, confident explanation that equal access is the Google-compliant choice that protects their public profile (GBP can stop new reviews and show warnings for fake engagement).

patternLibrary.pattern: Rating block in the first screen, with only property identity above it (no gate, splash, dropdown or overlay)
patternLibrary.evidence: HappyOrNot: one question, done in three taps. sunday and me&u: star row immediately after payment. Trustpilot's evaluate page asks one question only. Ratestar's hero takes about 55-60% of the first screen. Touch Stay and Hostfully put a 'Get Started' gate first. ReviewPro opens with a 'Select your establishment' dropdown and a disabled Continue. ReviewPro vendor data: one rating plus one comment converts best.
patternLibrary.why: Guests who just scanned a card give seconds of attention. The whole block (question, stars, caption, submit) must fit 375x667 in svh units with the Safari toolbars showing. Every other element comes after it.

patternLibrary.pattern: Five empty outline stars that fill to the selection, with state shown by fill and stroke weight, not hue alone
patternLibrary.evidence: W3C APG rating radio group (currentColor strokes, 2px focus ring). The WCAG 1.4.11 Understanding page uses stars as its example. Testimonial.to pre-fills 5 stars. Today's RepKey fields draw five identical filled glyphs with no checked state, so a sighted guest cannot see the choice.
patternLibrary.why: This fixes a real defect, avoids default-positive bias, and survives forced-colours mode. The idle outline must reach 3:1 against the actual surface; a 55% text-into-surface mix passed for all 15 palettes tested.

patternLibrary.pattern: Visible word anchors at both ends plus a live caption with the chosen word
patternLibrary.evidence: Trustpilot gives each star a word (Bad to Excellent), but only in accessible names. NN/g and Qualtrics recommend labelled endpoints. Signature Stay shows only the digits 1-5. GuestRevu (vendor data) finds stars read differently from other formats.
patternLibrary.why: It removes ambiguity about what '3' means in EN and BG, and confirms the choice without a dialog. Reserve the caption's line height so longer BG words do not shift the layout. Use neutral quality words rather than emotional ones.

patternLibrary.pattern: Explicit submit; tapping a star never submits, redirects or opens Google
patternLibrary.evidence: WCAG failure F36 (auto-submit on change). Ratestar redirects ratings above threshold after 200ms. Tally never auto-submits. Apple's rating prompt is tap then Submit. Arrow keys in native radio groups check each value in turn.
patternLibrary.why: It prevents mis-taps and stray keyboard values from being recorded as real, counted responses, and it rules out any score-based automatic routing.

patternLibrary.pattern: Privacy promise stated at the action in one guest-language line
patternLibrary.evidence: Airbnb keeps a host-only note separate from the public review. Senja puts reassurance microcopy next to its CTA. Signature Stay had a 'Shared privately with...' line under the button. Today's RepKey entry card shows manager policy copy about eligibility and sequencing to guests.
patternLibrary.why: Candour depends on knowing who reads the answer. One line, e.g. 'Only the {name} team sees your rating. No ads or trackers.', replaces both the policy paragraph and the bottom analytics bar.

patternLibrary.pattern: A score-invariant Google action: same copy, slot, size, colour, icon and entrance motion for every rating from 1 to 5
patternLibrary.evidence: Google Maps UGC policy on selective solicitation. FTC 16 CFR 255.2 Example 11 (inviting everyone is fine). EU UCPD Annex I 23c plus the Commission Guidance on 'only soliciting positive reviews'. BG ЗЗП чл. 68ж. UK DMCC Sch 20 para 13 (including para 13(4) for vendors). CMA208 4.4-4.5. Tripadvisor requires identical UI. GBP can restrict profiles for fake engagement.
patternLibrary.why: It is the only design that is plainly not gating, and it doubles as a visible trust signal. Build it as one component that takes no score-dependent props.

patternLibrary.pattern: Private written note offered as an extra companion below the Google action
patternLibrary.evidence: OpenTable's form holds the public review and a confidential note in one flow, the same for every score. Birdeye and Podium show public and private options side by side. GatherUp puts 'Direct Feedback' above the review sites for low scorers. CMA208 warns against dispute resolution made contingent on not reviewing.
patternLibrary.why: Adopt the companion model but never GatherUp's ordering or 'tell us first' framing. The private card sits after the Google card, with equal or quieter weight, and appears at or below the threshold (default 3).

patternLibrary.pattern: An honest friction label before handing off to Google
patternLibrary.evidence: Grade.us labels each destination with 'Login w/...' or 'NO LOGIN REQUIRED'. Google's write-review link redirected a signed-out mobile browser straight to Google sign-in. GBP help says customers must be signed in. Podium's completion page asserts 'Thanks for your review'.
patternLibrary.why: A sign-in wall is the biggest hidden drop-off, and no vendor warns about it. Use 'Opens Google · you may need to sign in'. After the handoff, show 'Google opened' or an unchanged receipt, never a review-written claim.

patternLibrary.pattern: Review CTAs decorated with five filled stars or 'Rate us' lockups
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar's Google and Tripadvisor cards with gold emoji stars. Alpen's 'Review us on Google' plus emoji stars. Google Partner Marketing Hub: no stars next to the Google name or logo, and no unofficial badges. The EU Guidance names pre-filled positive review templates.
patternLibrary.why: Pre-filled stars prime the score and misuse the platforms' brands. Use a neutral invitation with the plain word 'Google' (the official G only after the brand-use question is settled).

patternLibrary.pattern: A grid of several public review platforms
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar's two-up platform cards. Grade.us logo tiles, including a stale Citysearch. Birdeye allows up to four site buttons. NiceJob's site list. Booking.com reviews require a booking. Yelp prohibits asking for reviews at all.
patternLibrary.why: RepKey has one verified public destination. Tripadvisor or Booking may appear only as subordinate secondary links with discovery wording ('Find us on Tripadvisor'), never styled as review destinations.

patternLibrary.pattern: Score thresholds that route, redirect, hide or reword public options
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar's nrpThreshold and invite minRating. me&u's minimum star rating, on by default. Canary asks only 5-star guests. Akia asks promoters only. Touch Stay's pop-up. TrustYou's 'share only if score > 3' toggle. Tablein, sunday, HappyOrNot Smiley Sign, Revinate's promoter-only follow-up.
patternLibrary.why: Prohibited by every relevant regime and permanently denied in RepKey. The admin must never offer a toggle that could create this, including a 'pause Google' switch (CMA208 on arbitrarily stopping and starting invitations).

patternLibrary.pattern: Celebration or motion that differs by score (confetti, bursts, 'Congratulations', badges)
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar fires a 200-particle confetti burst on every submit. Okendo's post-review 'Congratulations' with a party emoji. Uber offers compliments only after 5 stars. Bolt offers tipping only after 4-5 stars.
patternLibrary.why: Unequal celebration implies a preferred answer and drifts toward gamification. Motion should explain cause and effect, stay the same for 1 and 5, and fall back to crossfades under reduced motion.

patternLibrary.pattern: Cover-style arrival that carries the property's identity
patternLibrary.evidence: Touch Stay's full-bleed cover. Ratestar's hero film of the property's sign. A Linktree venue page: logo disc on a rich solid colour. Duve's greeting.
patternLibrary.why: Keep the 'opening a welcome book' feeling, but drop the gate, cap the atmosphere band (about 26-42svh by direction) so the stars stay visible, use no autoplay video, and make it look finished with no photo.

patternLibrary.pattern: Logo contrast safeguard: a plate or a polarity check
patternLibrary.evidence: Touch Stay's Paperbark Camp: a dark logo nearly invisible on a dark photo. Maxi Park's icon is white on transparent; Therma Numera's mark is black on transparent. Dobro's orange logotype is 2.59:1 on white.
patternLibrary.why: logoUrl is a single asset. When logos return, sample alpha-weighted luminance and either choose the stage polarity or put the logo on a plate.

patternLibrary.pattern: Useful links as quiet rows: at most 4 visible, grouped, icon plus label plus short subline, below the rating
patternLibrary.evidence: Linktree's 64px full-width rows. Birdeye: one primary action, then three utility actions. Signature Stay's hairline rows. Ratestar's 240px photo link cards compete with the review action. Beacons styles 'Rate us on Google' exactly like 'Menu'.
patternLibrary.why: 'Review gateway first, link tree second' means links serve the guest without competing with the rating. Showing them from arrival is a proposed change (e2e currently pins 'not before rating'), so every design needs a baseline variant.

patternLibrary.pattern: Useful facts as quiet chips (hours, check-in/out)
patternLibrary.evidence: Touch Stay's check-in and check-out chips. Linktree's 'Open 11:30 - LATE' descriptor. me&u's wait-time badges.
patternLibrary.why: Useful and calm, but there are no content fields for it today. Treat it as future scope; do not fake facts with links.

patternLibrary.pattern: Language control: text with native names, compact, top-right, remembered; content fully translated
patternLibrary.evidence: W3C i18n: no flags; name each language in itself; keep a visible switch. Testimonial.to: globe plus 'English'. Hostfully's bar breaks at 390px and is duplicated. Ratestar's flag pill translates chrome only, producing mixed-language pages. TrustYou can hide untranslated languages.
patternLibrary.why: The existing PortalLanguageNav semantics (hreflang, aria-current, ?locale=) fit the no-cookie posture. Restyle it as 'EN | БГ' with 44px targets and full accessible names, and add per-span lang so Bulgarian letterforms activate.

patternLibrary.pattern: Emoji used as interface icons or decoration
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar (pin, phone, fleur-de-lis, vote boxes, food emoji). Beacons. Senja. TrustYou's WhatsApp pointer. Screen readers announce emoji unreliably (tink.uk).
patternLibrary.why: Emoji render differently per OS, undercut a premium look and add noise to assistive tech. Use one 1.5px-stroke SVG icon set, aria-hidden, next to real text.

patternLibrary.pattern: Autoplay video or heavy photo hero; spinner before first content
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar's autoplay mp4 from Supabase storage and black boxes when images fail. Hostfully shows a blank white screen for 3-5s. Tapni's demo showed a spinner for more than 3s. web.dev LCP target is 2.5s at p75. Hotel Wi-Fi congestion.
patternLibrary.why: The first paint decides whether the guest waits. Budget: under about 150KB for the no-photo variant, two WOFF2 files, preload only the question face, server-rendered markup.

patternLibrary.pattern: Consent or disclosure overlay on the first screen
patternLibrary.evidence: Trustpilot's cookie wall appears before the rating. Linktree and HappyOrNot banners. NiceJob loads GTM, GA and the Facebook SDK on its review page. RepKey's fixed 'Portal analytics information' bar covers about 27-30% of a 375x667 screen over the stars. The Dutch DPA's own site serves no banner.
patternLibrary.why: Once the non-exempt sessionStorage dedupe marker is removed (counsel to confirm under Bulgarian ZET чл. 4а), an inline one-line region under the submit button is enough. Keep the e2e contract: region name, 'Got it', visible then detached.

patternLibrary.pattern: Vendor branding louder than the property
patternLibrary.evidence: NiceJob and Senja floating 'Powered by' badges, Senja's over the CTA. Podium places an advert on the completion page. ReviewPro and Customer Alliance wordmarks outrank the hotel. Linktree's 'Explore other Linktrees' promotes celebrities below a restaurant.
patternLibrary.why: Owners are proud of a page that looks like theirs. A quiet footer mark only; never a badge, an ad or cross-promotion.

patternLibrary.pattern: A closing line in the venue's own voice
patternLibrary.evidence: sunday's post-payment line thanking the guest for letting them cook. citizenM's verbal identity. STAY varies thank-you tone by score.
patternLibrary.why: Warmth belongs at the end. Pack copy stays neutral and immutable. An optional admin-authored thank-you line per locale would be a new content field and must be the same for every score.

patternLibrary.pattern: Inline receipt with Change and Withdraw instead of dialogs or a rights console
patternLibrary.evidence: NN/g prefers undo over confirmation dialogs. Google Maps lets you edit or delete a review. OpenTable allows editing. Bolt and MENU TIGER allow no change. Today's RepKey receipt stacks four bordered boxes and three UTC deadlines.
patternLibrary.why: People commit faster when change is visible. Collapse the rating to one receipt line with 'Change'. Group correction, withdrawal and shared-device reset in a labelled 'Your response' disclosure, with deadlines in local time and an inline two-step confirm for full withdrawal.

patternLibrary.pattern: Shared-device reset
patternLibrary.evidence: TrustYou kiosk mode auto-reloads 15-20s after submit. RepKey's reset is a buried link today.
patternLibrary.why: Make it an explicit, calm action ('Using a shared device? Clear this response') with a clear success state. No timer, which could wipe a guest who is still reading.

patternLibrary.pattern: Topic chips for the private note
patternLibrary.evidence: Tripadvisor's aspect chips (Rooms, Service, Cleanliness...). Toast's reason chips. Yotpo Smart Prompts filter negative topics and fill a progress bar to 200 characters.
patternLibrary.why: Neutral chips cure blank-page anxiety but need a new data model; future scope. Never add progress bars, length targets or sentiment filtering.

patternLibrary.pattern: Self-asserted verification seals or Google look-alike styling
patternLibrary.evidence: Ratestar's blue verified check. Customer Alliance's 'CERTIFICATE'. GBP API policy prohibits replicating the Business Profile look and implying Google endorsement.
patternLibrary.why: They imply verification RepKey cannot provide and create brand-policy exposure.

patternLibrary.pattern: Public ratings, review counts or testimonials on the gateway page
patternLibrary.evidence: NiceJob shows a 4.9 score and a wall of 5-star reviews before the ask. MENU TIGER publicly shows self-collected averages. UCPD Art. 7(6), ЗЗП чл. 68е ал. 7 and DMCC create duties once reviews are shown.
patternLibrary.why: It anchors the rating and triggers disclosure duties. Beta shows no public rating, count or quote.

patternLibrary.pattern: Curated type pairings and derived colour roles instead of free pickers
patternLibrary.evidence: Canary's reported 3x3 type choice (unverified). TrustYou's three font slots with a warning that some fonts lack Cyrillic. Touch Stay's preset combinations. Duve's 16 fonts. Touch Stay's free colour pickers carry only a contrast tip. The gap-2 matrix shows primaries fail as stars in 6 of 15 inputs on light stages.
patternLibrary.why: Curated compositions carry type and texture as constants. Colour roles (accent 3:1, accent text 4.5:1, idle star, on-accent) are derived from the three hex values and checked at publish, with no new admin-facing colour pickers.

patternLibrary.pattern: Placement-aware wording instead of fake personalisation
patternLibrary.evidence: Duve's 'Welcome Alex' with stay dates. Canary's 'Hello, Emily'. HappyOrNot uses a different question per touchpoint.
patternLibrary.why: RepKey has no reservation identity. Use the portal override title for placement ('Spa reception'). Never show a guest name, room or booking.

patternLibrary.pattern: Printed collateral that matches the page
patternLibrary.evidence: HappyOrNot sells table talkers, tents, wobblers and outdoor boards. Google's review sticker kit reportedly now redirects away. Ratestar sells branded cards. DENSO: 4-module quiet zone. NN/g: dark-on-light codes.
patternLibrary.why: The scan should feel continuous from table card to screen. Print templates per composition, with the QR on a light plate, a short printed URL and honest CTA copy.

patternLibrary.pattern: Traffic-light colours by score
patternLibrary.evidence: Trustpilot's tiles turn red-orange at 1 and green at 4-5. TrustYou's default red/orange/green buttons.
patternLibrary.why: Red reads as judgement and clashes with premium palettes. One calm accent for all selections.

patternLibrary.pattern: AI writing help or pre-filled review text
patternLibrary.evidence: Testimonial.to's 'Improve writing'. The EmbedSocial AI Reviews Generator. Famewall drafting. Tripadvisor's 'Help me write'. EU Guidance on pre-filled positive templates.
patternLibrary.why: It undermines authenticity and approaches review manipulation.

patternLibrary.pattern: Contact capture at the end of feedback
patternLibrary.evidence: Birdeye callback request. TrustYou's email is mandatory by default. Podium's promo SMS opt-in. GuestRevu asks for name, email and room first. Toast's contact opt-in.
patternLibrary.why: Safety-blocked in RepKey. The private-note placeholder should actively say no name is needed.

patternLibrary.pattern: Server-rendered, instant first paint for QR and NFC arrivals
patternLibrary.evidence: Tapni's JS-only profile spinner. Hostfully's loading screen. Ratestar's video-first render. NFC now needs a notification tap on iOS and Android 17, which adds delay.
patternLibrary.why: The guest has already spent a tap. Identity, question and stars must be in the initial HTML, and any client-only disclosure must render below the stars to avoid layout shift.

opportunities: Be the only premium portal in the BG/EU market that visibly guarantees equal Google access: the same card after 1 and after 5 stars. Pitch it as the choice that protects the owner's Google profile. Show it in the admin preview by putting the low-rating and high-rating after-rating states side by side.
Own the no-photo state. No competitor designs one. Launch the beta with typographic, tonal and pattern identities that owners are proud of, so the upload block reads as a feature, not a gap.

Do Bulgarian typography right: self-hosted OFL faces with Bulgarian locl forms (Cormorant Garamond, Playfair 2, Ysabeau, Sofia Sans, Manrope), lang on the page root and per span, and Cyrillic-aware wordmark sizing. Ratestar, Satoshi and most vendors render BG in Russian forms or system fallbacks.

Ship a first screen with no banner and no trackers: remove the non-exempt sessionStorage dedupe (subject to counsel), move the disclosure inline under the submit button, and stop loading fonts from third-party CDNs on /p. This is calmer and faster than Trustpilot, Linktree or NiceJob.

Make the handoff to Google honest. Tell guests Google may ask them to sign in, record only the selection, and never thank them for a review. The receipt copy becomes a trust asset against vendors who claim 'Thanks for your review'.

Turn guest rights into a quiet premium feature: one-line receipt with Change, a 'Your response' disclosure with local-time deadlines, an inline two-step withdraw, and a calm shared-device reset. Competitors either allow no edits (Bolt, MENU TIGER) or bury them.

Localize fully, not just the chrome: localized link labels and category titles (a new capability), missing-translation checks before publish, and a bilingual, brand-free unavailable page chosen by Accept-Language. This fixes Ratestar's mixed-language pages.

Derive each page from the property's own brand with contrast guarantees: automatic stage polarity, derived accent roles, and a logo plate. Ratestar ignores brand colours, and Touch Stay and Duve offer pickers with only a contrast tip.

Sell durability: stable QR and NFC tokens, draft and published snapshots, rollback, and 'publish changes while live'. Compare against ReviewPro's irreversible 'Save & Publish' and against link-in-bio platforms that died with printed codes (Koji 2024, Tap Bio 31 Oct 2026).

Offer premium print collateral per composition (table tent, reception card, spa card, NFC card copy). Google's branded review kit is reportedly gone, and owners want objects that match their interior.
Hit a performance budget competitors miss: under about 150KB, no video, two font files, server-rendered first paint, LCP well under 2.5s on congested hotel Wi-Fi and in in-app QR browsers.

Report honestly as a positioning point with GMs: 'Guests who opened Google', never 'reviews collected'. No staff leaderboards or quotas (banned by Google and denied by RepKey). Availability by exception and a 10-rating comparison floor.

Support multi-placement properties well: one property identity, many placement portals (reception, spa, restaurant, pool bar) with local wording, portal groups and per-placement print pieces. Competitors mostly offer one page per location.

Be the calm alternative to the dense, emoji-heavy BG link-hub aesthetic: one question, one accent, real icons, at most 4 visible links. That contrast alone reads as premium next to Ratestar in a sales demo.
Fix today's visible defects as quick wins before the redesign ships: no selected-star state, policy copy shown to guests, app dark-theme leak on /p, UTC deadlines, and the bottom bar over the CTA.
synth.photoStrategy:
Beta photo strategy: design every direction to be finished with no photograph, then add owned photography as a later layer that plugs into a slot each composition already defines.

Tier 0 ships now and needs no uploads. Identity comes from:
- displayName set by wordmark rules: auto-fit, a 2-line layout up to 35+ characters, and a separate size cap for Cyrillic names (about 22-26px on one line at 320px).
- An optional monogram seal of the initials, which works for both Latin and Cyrillic names.
- Tonal fields derived from the three brand hex values by shifting OKLab lightness only.
- A pre-rendered grain tile of about 2KB at 4-8% opacity. Do not use a live feTurbulence filter.
- For C6, a curated library of small SVG place patterns (mountain contours, sea lines, geometric weave, ink marbling, vineyard rows, stone), tinted by the brand.
- Architectural frame shapes that hold colour today and a photo later.

Tier 0 also covers the historical hero_image_url. It must render only inside the composition's photo slot, with explicit dimensions, object-fit cover, a scrim into the surface so text never sits on a raw photo, a solid-colour placeholder, and fetchpriority=high only when it is the LCP element. og:image keeps using it; new portals could later get a server-rendered typographic share card.

Do not use Google Business Profile photos:
- The GBP APIs are scoped to creating, managing and reporting on listings.
- They forbid caching beyond 30 days and any manipulation or aggregation, and cropping, tinting or overlaying is arguably manipulation.
- googleUrl values change over time.
- Customer media carries attribution that must not be altered and belongs to guests.
- Tools must not replicate the Business Profile look or imply endorsement.

Places API Place Photos is lawful but a poor fit. It is billable, needs Google Maps attribution plus an author credit and link on every photo, allows no storage, returns uncontrolled user-contributed images, and puts Google branding onto a non-Google experience. If photo reuse matters commercially, ask Google in writing through the existing correspondence in docs/external/google. The default answer is no.

Do not use stock photography either: Birdeye's stock banners show that stock reads as 'not our place'.

Tier 1 comes after the SAFE-01 upload path. The property uploads its own originals, which it owns or licenses; uploading to Google does not transfer ownership. The upload needs:
- A rights attestation and a takedown path.
- Moderation, EXIF stripping and a focal point.
- Server-side resizing to AVIF/WebP at two widths, capped at 2x the rendered size.
- One photo per property first, with per-placement overrides later.
- Wiring the organisation logo from Identity into portals, with a luminance check that decides stage polarity or a logo plate.

Slot rules per composition:
- C1: the atmosphere band, 26-34svh or less, with a scrim.
- C2: a small 4:5 inset plate beside the standfirst, never full-bleed.
- C3: optional duotone inside the poster, tinted to primary.
- C4: the card header band at 16:7.
- C5: none.
- C6: inside the frame.

No carousels, no video and no autoplay at any tier. Printed collateral always uses the Tier 0 identity, so the printed code never depends on a photo.

candidates.name: Carved Stillness (Signature Stay, evolved)
candidates.thesis: Keep what the owner chose in Signature Stay and remove its dependence on generated resort photography. The luxury comes from restraint: a tonal stage built from the property's own colours, a carved serif, fine grain, one metal accent, and a rating block that is the hero of the first screen.
candidates.bestFor: Premium resorts, spa and thermal hotels, mountain lodges and fine dining. It suits brands whose accent is gold, bronze, tan, orange or thermal blue, which pass on a dark stage: Maxi Park #AA8453 5.16:1, Alpen #9C7C57, Staria Chinar #BA9774, Therma Numera #4DB8DD. Deep-colour and monochrome brands (Les Fleurs purple, Щастливеца oxblood, InterContinental black) get the same composition on the light stage (bronze-derived accent on ivory or the brand background). It works for restaurants through the same identity strip.
candidates.structure:
One continuous scroll that transforms in place, with no gate and no steps. First screen at 375x667, top to bottom:
(1) A 56px identity strip. Left: a spaced small-caps wordmark from displayName, or a 40px monogram seal when the name exceeds about 24 characters on a 320px screen. Right: an 'EN | БГ' text control with 44px targets and full language names as accessible labels.
(2) An atmosphere band capped at 26svh (tonal field plus grain, or the legacy hero with a scrim). The h1 (the localized title, e.g. 'Spa & Thermal Baths') sits at its foot in small caps. It is rendered once when it equals displayName, so the name never repeats.
(3) The rating block. The question (language-pack copy, 30-32px serif, text-wrap balance, 3 lines max, capped at 32-34px for BG at 320px). Five 56x56 outline stars with 12px gaps. Endpoint labels 'Poor' and 'Excellent'. A reserved caption line. A full-width 52px 'Send privately' button. One privacy line.
Below the fold: the localized short description as a quiet paragraph, which protects the first screen from 500-character descriptions. Then a hairline and 'Also useful' with up to four link rows (label, small destination type, arrow), with category titles in small caps when there are several. Then a footer: privacy, language, a quiet RepKey mark.
After a rating: a one-line receipt, then the Google card, then the private-note card when at or below the threshold, then the same links, then a collapsed 'Your response' disclosure.
Baseline variant: links stay hidden until after the rating (current e2e pin) and sit after the private card.
candidates.visualSystem:
Polarity is chosen per brand from the three Brand Profile hex values.
- Dark stage: surface = the brand text hex, ink = the brand background hex, so the validated text contrast of 15-21:1 carries over exactly.
- Light stage: used when the primary cannot reach 3:1 on dark.
Colour roles, all derived:
- Accent: the primary shifted only in OKLab lightness to 3:1 against the actual surface for stars, focus ring and rules, and to 4.5:1 for small accent text.
- Button label: black or white chosen automatically (ink on champagne).
- Idle star outline: text mixed 55% into the surface.
- Text on dark: 18px body at weight 400 or more, warm off-white, no pure black or white.
Type:
- Cormorant Garamond 600 for the wordmark and question. Self-hosted so small caps and oldstyle figures survive, with a Cyrillic subset that makes Bulgarian forms the default, so a Cyrillic name renders correctly on an EN page.
- Ysabeau Office 400/600 for body text and buttons, with tabular figures for times and '4/5'.
- About 107KB, split by unicode-range so EN guests skip the Cyrillic files.
Details:
- Hairline rules at 16% ink. 4px radius on buttons and cards.
- No drop shadows on dark: depth comes from two tonal surface steps.
- Grain tile at 5% opacity.
- Hierarchy through scale contrast (32px question against 12px small caps), never colour alone.
candidates.imagery: No photo by default. The band is a radial tonal field from the brand primary at low chroma, plus a grain tile and an optional monogram seal: initials in the display serif inside a 1px ring, working for 'MP' and 'МВ' alike. A historical hero_image_url renders in the band with explicit dimensions and a gradient scrim into the surface. After SAFE-01, one owned photograph per property, never video or carousel. A future logo sits on a plate if its luminance fails against the stage.
candidates.signatureMoment: The settle. After 'Send privately' succeeds, the five stars slide together and condense into one receipt line: four filled and one outline, then '4 · Very good · sent privately · Change'. This is a same-document View Transition of about 280ms with deceleration. 60ms later the Google card rises 8px and fades in over 220ms. The private card follows with the identical entrance when eligible. Timing, styling and motion are exactly the same for 1 and 5 stars. Under reduced motion it becomes a 100ms crossfade, and focus moves to the new state's heading.
candidates.stateNotes:
Shared rating core, used by every candidate:
- Entry: stars unselected, submit always enabled. Pressing it with no choice shows 'Choose a rating from 1 to 5 stars.' as an alert under the stars.
- Selected: stars 1..n filled with a heavier stroke, and the caption word appears (EN Poor / Fair / Good / Very good / Excellent; BG strings need native review).
- Submitting: the button keeps its width and reads 'Sending…'.
- Save failed: the selection is kept, an inline 'Couldn't send — check your connection and try again' appears with a Retry button.
- After rating: a status message 'Rating sent privately'. The Google card sits on a neutral surface identical for 1-5: title 'Share your experience on Google', subline 'Opens Google · you may need to sign in', button 'Continue to Google' with an external-link arrow and screen-reader text. The URI comes only from the server selection call.
- Private card, at or below the threshold only, below Google: 'Tell the team privately what could be better'. It expands in place to a labelled textarea marked optional, with a counter shown near the 2,000 limit, placeholder 'No need to include your name', and a 'Send privately' button. Sent: 'Sent privately to the team. It won't be shown again on this device.'
- Google degraded: the same slot shows 'Public reviews aren't available right now. Your private rating reached the team.' with no link rendered.
- 'Your response' disclosure: change the rating (1 hour), withdraw only the note (24 hours), withdraw everything (24 hours, inline two-step confirm; its copy notes that nothing already posted on Google is affected), and clear for the next guest. Deadlines are in Europe/Sofia local time with a zone label.
- Withdrawn: a calm card with 'Start a new response' for shared devices; links stay available (proposal).
- Unavailable: brand-free, identical for every reason, bilingual by Accept-Language, calmer typography.
- Analytics disclosure: an inline region named 'Portal analytics information' under the privacy line, with a tertiary 'Got it' that detaches after the tap.
- The /p page ignores the app's dark-theme script.
C1 specifics:
- Dark stage: the textarea and cards use the second tonal step, not app tokens.
- Long names: the wordmark goes to 2 lines or the monogram.
- BG: the question is capped at 32px at 320px (2 lines in Cormorant).
candidates.betaFeasibility:
High for the no-photo version. Everything guests see comes from data that exists today: three hex values, displayName, localized title and description, links and categories, threshold, and the Google binding. New work:
- A derived-token helper (extend portal-contrast.ts with an OKLab lightness shift and 3:1 non-text checks).
- Self-hosted fonts (the CSP already allows font-src 'self').
- Isolating /p from THEME_INIT_SCRIPT and app tokens.
- guest-ui-en-v2 / guest-ui-bg-v2 language packs for the new copy, with matching e2e name updates. 'Send privately' changes the pinned 'Submit private rating'; keeping the old label is a zero-e2e fallback.
- A composition field on the Brand Profile, or ship C1 as the only composition first.
Links from arrival is optional; the design works with today's rule. This is the lowest-risk path to a premium beta.
needsNewCapability: Derived colour roles (stage polarity, accent 3:1, accent text 4.5:1, idle star, on-accent) with publish-time checks
Self-hosted Cormorant Garamond and Ysabeau Office subsets with Bulgarian forms made default
guest-ui v2 language packs (new button, endpoint and caption words, Google subline, private-card wording) plus e2e updates
Composition choice stored on the Property Brand Profile
Guest page isolated from the app theme script and shadcn tokens
Optional: links from arrival (BETA/ADR 0044 reconciliation plus e2e change)
Future: owned photography and logo via SAFE-01, with a logo luminance check
candidates.risks: On the dark stage the default SaaS-blue palette (#2563EB on #111827, 3.43:1) reads as an app dark mode, not luxury; replacing the default palette with a neutral hospitality default helps. Deep primaries fail on dark and need the automatic switch to the light stage, so admins must understand that polarity follows their brand. Black logos vanish on ink and need a plate. Thin serif weights and small text on dark hurt readability; keep display at 600 and body at 18px. Similar brand hex values can make properties look alike, so the monogram and grain are the differentiators. The champagne look is honest only for gold and bronze brands; it must never be forced onto a blue or red primary.
candidates.relationToSignatureStay: Direct evolution. It keeps ink and champagne (when the brand supplies it), the spaced-caps wordmark, the serif question, outline stars, the privacy line under the button, and hairline link rows. It changes five things: the photo becomes optional; colours come from the property's own hex values rather than a fixed palette; word endpoints and a caption replace the digit labels; 'Send privately' replaces 'Share my rating', which implied posting publicly; and a light-stage twin exists for brands the dark stage cannot carry.

candidates.name: Folio (editorial paper)
candidates.thesis: The portal as a page from the property's own stationery: warm paper, graphite ink, one display serif moment, hairlines, dotted leaders and asymmetric whitespace. Premium through typography rather than atmosphere, like Aesop or Kinfolk, and calm enough to feel hand-set.
candidates.bestFor: Boutique and design hotels, guesthouses, B&Bs, wine bars, cafés and bistros. It fits properties with deep or near-monochrome brands on light backgrounds: Sense Hotel olive-grey on cream (7.37:1), Les Fleurs purple (8.34:1), Щастливеца oxblood on cream (7.77:1), Lucky Bansko brown (9.83:1). It is also the light-stage twin C1 needs.
candidates.structure:
A flush-left editorial column, with the left edge aligned to a 4px baseline grid.
- Masthead: a small-caps kicker holding the h1 (localized title, e.g. 'THE GARDEN RESTAURANT'), then displayName as the wordmark in the display serif (34px, 2 lines max, Cyrillic capped at 26px at 320px), then a 1px rule.
- Rating block, set like a form printed in a book: question in serif at 30px; five stars with small numerals 1-5 beneath and endpoint words; caption line; a 'Send privately' button (48px tall, auto width, not full-bleed); privacy line in small caps.
- The short description as a standfirst paragraph.
- An 'Index' of links: numbered rows 01-04 with label, dotted leader, arrow and a small destination line. Category titles act as small-caps section heads.
- A colophon footer: language control, privacy, 'Made with Reputation Key'.
The index shows from arrival as a proposal; baseline: it appears after the rating, below the Google panel.
After a rating:
- The rating block is replaced by a printed stub with a perforated rule.
- The Google panel follows, with a double hairline border and identical copy for every score.
- The private note (at or below threshold) follows as a ruled 'letter': a textarea with baseline rules.
candidates.visualSystem:
Light stage by default, with an optional 'night edition' (ink paper) for polarity.
Surface: the brand background. If that is pure #FFFFFF, apply a paper grain tile and warm hairlines rather than a colour cast, because warmth cannot be derived from white. Admins may explicitly accept a suggested paper tone.
Colour: ink = brand text. Accent derived to 3:1 for stars and rules and to 4.5:1 for index numerals and the kicker.
Type:
- Playfair 2 at display optical size 36, weight 500, self-hosted static. About 68KB including oldstyle figures. Google's static request serves the text optical size, so self-host.
- Sofia Sans 400/600 for text and buttons. Its default Cyrillic glyphs are the Bulgarian forms, and it has the narrowest BG button labels (228px at 16/600).
Devices: 1px hairlines, dotted leaders drawn with CSS, a double rule on the Google panel, perforation dashes. Radius 2px, no shadows.
Hierarchy by scale contrast (34px wordmark against 12-13px small caps), and a deliberately wider left gutter (20px) than right (16px).
candidates.imagery: None by default; the masthead typography is the identity. A future owned photo appears only as a small inset plate (4:5, about 40% of the column) beside the standfirst with a caption line, like a magazine figure, so the page never depends on it. A legacy hero_image_url renders as that inset plate, never full-bleed.
candidates.signatureMoment: The stub. On success a perforated rule draws across the column (stroke-dashoffset, 300ms), and the rating block becomes a printed stub: 'Received privately · 19 September, 14:32 · 4 · Very good · Change', in local time. It is identical for every score. A quieter second moment: the dotted leaders in the index line up like a hotel directory or a menu card.
candidates.stateNotes:
Uses the shared rating core (see C1) with these differences.
- Selected: the numeral under each chosen star switches to the accent, and the caption word is set in small caps.
- Error: shown inline beneath the button in text (not red-only), with the selection kept.
- Google panel: the same component as C1, framed by a double rule. When degraded, the same panel carries the gentle unavailable copy and no link.
- Private 'letter': ruled lines sit behind the text; the persistent label reads 'Private note to the team (optional)'.
- Receipt disclosure: 'Your response' as a small-caps section after the index.
- Withdrawn: the stub is struck through with a hairline and reads 'Withdrawn · your rating and note were removed', with 'Start a new response' below.
- Unavailable: brand-free.
- Analytics disclosure: an inline small-caps line under the button, with 'Got it' as a text button.
- Long BG index labels: at 320px, a wrapping row drops its leader and keeps the arrow.
- 200% text: the column reflows with no fixed heights.
candidates.betaFeasibility: High. Everything comes from existing data (categories, links, title, description, three hex values). Dotted leaders and rules are plain CSS. Needs the same token helper, font self-hosting, pack v2 and theme isolation as C1. The index is central to the composition, so links from arrival matter more here; the baseline fallback still reads well. Localized link labels are strongly desirable, because the index is text-heavy and today's labels are single strings shown to both EN and BG guests.
needsNewCapability: Derived colour roles with publish-time checks
Self-hosted Playfair 2 display instance (optical size 36) and Sofia Sans
guest-ui v2 language packs plus e2e updates
Composition choice on the Brand Profile, with an optional explicit 'paper tone' suggestion for white backgrounds
Localized link labels and category titles (EN/BG)
Links from arrival (proposal) for the index-first layout
Future: inset owned photo via SAFE-01
candidates.risks: Owners who expect photography may see a 'nicely typeset form'; the masthead must be generous. White-background brands can look cold unless they accept a paper tone. High-contrast serif hairlines break down at small sizes, so the serif is kept at 22px and above. Dotted leaders and numbered rows get busy with long BG labels at 320px. Flush-left composition is less familiar in a market used to centred Ratestar pages. A text-width submit button is a smaller target than full-width, but still 48px tall and centred in the thumb zone.
candidates.relationToSignatureStay: A sibling, not an evolution. It keeps the serif question, the privacy line at the action, and the hairline link rows. It swaps the dark atmosphere and photography for paper and typography. In practice it is the light-stage answer for brands C1 cannot carry, and a second composition in the same family.

candidates.name: Table Card (colour field and rating plate)
candidates.thesis: The page continues the printed card the guest just scanned. The property's colour fills a poster, its name is set huge, and the rating sits on a calm light plate that rises over the poster. Bold, local and instantly recognisable, it is built for restaurants and lively city hotels and matches the table tent on the table.
candidates.bestFor: Restaurants, bistros, bars and grills, food halls, cafés, and city or lifestyle hotels. It suits loud or saturated brands: Dobro orange #F5821F, Happy Bar & Grill red #E31E25, Щастливеца oxblood, Les Fleurs purple. Monochrome brands become an elegant black poster. Hotels use it for poolside and restaurant placements.
candidates.structure:
Poster and plate.
- Poster: the top 38svh (capped so stars stay visible at 375x667) is a field in the brand primary.
  - The wordmark is set in onPrimary, which is black or white chosen automatically and always 4.58:1 or better.
  - The wordmark auto-fits to 2 lines. It is lowercase or as entered; Cyrillic keeps its capitals.
  - Below the wordmark sits the h1 place line (localized title) at 15px.
  - The 'EN | БГ' control sits top-right in onPrimary.
- Plate: a sheet in the brand background colour with 24px top radii, overlapping the poster by 24px. It holds the question, stars, caption, submit and privacy line, with the stars at about 60-72% of screen height (thumb zone).
- Below the rating, still on the plate: the short description, then up to four 60px link rows (curated line icon, label, short subline such as 'Menu · kitchen until 23:00' if the admin writes it into the label) and the footer.
- After a rating the poster stays still and the plate carries every state: receipt line, Google card, private card at or below the threshold, links, 'Your response'.
- Nothing is sticky.
- Baseline variant: link rows move below the Google and private cards after rating.
candidates.visualSystem:
Colour:
- Field = primary. Plate = brand background. Text = brand text.
- Stars and focus on the plate = accent derived to 3:1 against the plate. Dobro's orange becomes #E27100, still orange; the 4.5:1 text role shifts further to burnt orange. The poster keeps the true brand colour.
- Buttons: primary fill with an automatic black or white label (ink labels on orange and gold, which pass).
Type: one Bulgarian-designed family, about 60KB self-hosted.
- Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 800 for the wordmark: tall, efficient with long and Cyrillic names, Bulgarian forms by default.
- Sofia Sans 400/600 for everything else.
Shape and texture:
- Large plate radius (24) against 14px buttons and 0 on the poster: deliberate, not uniform, radii.
- A soft plate shadow for layered depth.
- An optional fine halftone or grain on the field at 4%.
- Icons: one 1.5px-stroke set rendering iconKey (menu, booking, directions, website, phone-free call link, social).
candidates.imagery: None needed: the field and wordmark are the brand. Future owned photography may fill the poster as a duotone tinted to the primary, so every property's photo still reads as 'their colour', or it can stay out entirely. A legacy hero_image_url renders as that duotone. Print collateral (table tent, bar card) uses the exact poster-and-plate composition, with the QR on the light plate.
candidates.signatureMoment: Print-to-screen continuity. The table tent shows the poster on top and the QR on the light plate below; scanning opens a page that looks like that card, now interactive. On load the plate rises 16px into place (220ms, ease-out, once; none under reduced motion). After submission only the plate content changes, and the poster never reacts to the score.
candidates.stateNotes:
Uses the shared rating core (see C1) with these differences.
- The poster is static in every state.
- Selected stars use the derived plate accent, not the raw primary.
- Validation and save errors appear in plate text with an icon, never red alone, because red can be the brand colour (Happy Bar & Grill).
- The Google card is a neutral card on the plate: same copy, identical for 1-5. The degraded copy uses the same card.
- Private card: same size as the Google card with a quieter border.
- Withdrawn: the plate shows a calm card, 'Start a new response' and the links.
- Unavailable: brand-free, with no poster, so nothing reveals the property.
- Analytics disclosure: inline on the plate under the button.
- Long names: a 35-character name ('Aparthotel Lucky Bansko SPA & Relax') fits 2 lines at about 40px Extra Condensed at 320px; a hard cap then shrinks it.
- Cyrillic names on an EN page stay correct because Sofia Sans defaults to Bulgarian forms.
- A red primary is never used for error states.
candidates.betaFeasibility: High. It needs only the three hex values and displayName. The main new pieces are a wordmark auto-fit algorithm (Latin and Cyrillic, 5-120 characters), the derived plate accent, self-hosted Sofia Sans (Extra Condensed plus regular), pack v2, and rendering of the iconKey that is stored but unused today. Print templates live in the admin Share tab. Links from arrival strengthens the restaurant use case (the menu is what diners want) but is not required.
needsNewCapability: Wordmark auto-fit and 2-line rules for Latin and Cyrillic display names
Derived plate accent (3:1 and 4.5:1) with publish-time checks
Curated line-icon set rendering the stored iconKey, editable in the Links tab
Self-hosted Sofia Sans Extra Condensed and Sofia Sans
guest-ui v2 language packs plus e2e updates
Print templates (table tent, bar card) sharing the composition
Links from arrival (proposal)
Future: duotone owned photography via SAFE-01
candidates.risks: A loud field can overwhelm a calm hotel and may read as fast casual. It suits restaurants better than luxury hotels. For orange, tan and gold brands the plate accent is visibly darker than the poster colour, which owners may notice. Monochrome brands produce a black poster that feels severe. If link rows get too prominent it becomes 'a nicer Linktree'. The poster must never push the stars below 375x667: cap it and test BG names. Red brands collide with error semantics.
candidates.relationToSignatureStay: A departure that serves the half of the market Signature Stay does not: restaurants and loud brands. It keeps the invariant rating core, the privacy line and the quiet links. It replaces serif luxury with poster typography, and it grows out of round one's Local Character direction (large wordmark, warm appetite colour) rather than Signature Stay.

candidates.name: Pass (placement card)
candidates.thesis: Give the guest one object instead of a web page: a pass for this place, like a key card or a boarding pass. It carries the placement ('Spa · Reception'), the property and the rating. After rating, a stub tears off the pass and becomes the receipt. Modern and calm, with product-grade depth, and honest about where the guest is without pretending to know who they are.
candidates.bestFor: Hotels and groups with several placements (reception, spa, restaurant, pool bar, meeting rooms) under one property and portal group. Also business and lifestyle hotels, serviced apartments, chains, and restaurant table cards. It suits brands of any polarity because the colour lives in a header band.
candidates.structure:
A centred card on a softly tinted backdrop. The card is max 358px wide and full-bleed below 360px, with radius 20 and a layered shadow; it fills most of the first screen.
- Header band: in the brand primary, with the placement line (h1: the portal's localized title, e.g. 'SPA · RECEPTION') and displayName in onPrimary. The language control sits in the band.
- Card body: question, stars, caption, 'Send privately', privacy line.
- Below the card: 'Nearby' links from arrival (proposal) as a compact icon-and-label list, not a grid, at most 4; then the description; then the footer.
After a rating:
- A perforation forms across the card body. The upper part becomes the stub ('4 · Very good · sent privately · Change'), which holds the 'Your response' disclosure.
- The Google card and, at or below the threshold, the private card appear as two further cards of the same width stacked beneath, each with the same radius.
- The private card is visually quieter, never louder, than Google.
- Baseline: links after these cards.
candidates.visualSystem:
Colour:
- Backdrop: brand background with at most 4% primary tint, with the accent re-checked on the tinted surface.
- Card surface: white or the brand background.
- Header band: primary, with an automatic black or white label.
- Stars and focus: derived accent at 3:1.
Type: Manrope 400/600 only, about 30KB self-hosted variable. It is geometric and closest to today's Satoshi feel, has Bulgarian forms via locl, and uses tabular figures in the stub.
- Manrope wraps long BG labels at 320px. Setting button labels at 15px and using the shorter v2 copy ('Изпрати поверително' rather than 'Изпрати непубличната оценка') keeps them on one line.
Depth: two-layer shadows on the card (ambient plus key), none on the stacked secondary cards (hairline only), a perforation drawn with a dashed mask. Radii 20 (card) / 12 (buttons) / 8 (rows).
Dark stage: the same card on an ink backdrop.
candidates.imagery: No photo: the band is colour, with an optional monogram at its right edge. The future owned photo sits in the header band at 16:7 with a scrim under the placement text, like a photo key card. A legacy hero renders there. Print: an NFC or QR card that is literally the pass ('Hold your phone near the card, then tap the link that appears'), with the QR on a light area and the printed short URL.
candidates.signatureMoment: The tear. On success a perforation line draws across the card (200ms), and the stub separates 6px downward with a deepening shadow (transform only, 280ms), carrying the receipt. The Google card slides up from behind the pass with the standard 220ms entrance. Identical for every score; a crossfade under reduced motion.
candidates.stateNotes:
Uses the shared rating core (see C1) with these differences.
- The placement line always comes from the portal's localized title. If a portal has no override, the property title is used and the band shows only the name.
- Selected: stars in the derived accent, caption under the stars.
- Save error: inside the card body, with the selection kept.
- Google card and degraded copy: in the second stacked card, same for 1-5.
- Private card: third, only at or below the threshold.
- Feedback sent: that card collapses to a single line.
- 'Your response': opens inside the stub (rights, deadlines in local time, inline two-step withdraw, clear for next guest).
- Withdrawn: the stub greys out with 'Withdrawn' and 'Start a new response'.
- Unavailable: a brand-free pass shape with no band colour.
- Analytics disclosure: inline inside the card body under the privacy line.
- 200% text: the card grows in height; nothing is fixed-height.
- The pass must never show a guest name, room, reservation or date of stay.
candidates.betaFeasibility: High. The card-in-page maps onto the current PublicPortalContent order. The placement line reuses the portal override title that exists today; a dedicated placement field would be cleaner. Needs the token helper, Manrope self-hosting, pack v2 (shorter BG labels), and theme isolation. Portal groups and several portals per property already exist in the domain, so the multi-placement story is real today.
needsNewCapability: Derived colour roles incl. the tinted-backdrop re-check
Self-hosted Manrope
guest-ui v2 language packs with shorter BG labels plus e2e updates
Optional dedicated placement label (today: the portal override title)
Print template for the pass / NFC card
Links from arrival (proposal)
Future: header-band owned photography via SAFE-01
candidates.risks: Card-on-backdrop with shadows is a common app pattern and can read as SaaS if radii and shadows stay at library defaults, so it needs deliberate depth and type. At 320px the card metaphor wastes width unless it goes full-bleed. The tear animation can feel gimmicky if overdone. A pass may imply a reservation or identity the product does not have, so copy must stay placement-only. Geometric sans alone gives less 'luxury' than the serif directions.
candidates.relationToSignatureStay: Borrows Signature Stay's single accent, privacy line under the button, and the admin idea of 'one property, every welcome'. It departs structurally (an object rather than a page) and visually (geometric sans, layered depth, a colour band instead of atmosphere). It can use Signature Stay's ink and champagne as its dark stage for premium placements.

candidates.name: One Thing at a Time (thumb-zone steps)
candidates.thesis: Each moment gets the whole screen and one decision. Very large type sets the question high on the screen; the thumb zone holds the stars and one button. Nothing competes, so a guest at the reception desk or leaving a café finishes in two taps. Swiss restraint rather than hospitality decoration.
candidates.bestFor: Fast, high-traffic moments: reception check-out desks, spa exits, casual restaurants, cafés, takeaway counters, conference venues. Also properties with little brand material: it looks good even with the default palette, because type does the work.
candidates.structure:
Three full-height views swapped in place on one page (not routes), each with min-height 100svh that grows with content.
(1) Question view: a slim 48px identity header (displayName, 'Menu & more' text button, language control). The h1 (title) in small caps. The question at 36-40px, 3 lines max (BG capped at 33-36px at 320px). The lower half holds the stars, caption, 'Send privately' and the privacy line, above the safe-area inset. 'Menu & more' opens a bottom sheet with links from arrival (proposal), so links never compete with the question.
(2) After-rating view: the receipt line at the top, then the Google card at mid-screen, then the private note offer below it (at or below the threshold) that expands in place. The Google card is never behind a step.
(3) Your-response view: opened from the header (rights, deadlines, withdraw, clear for next guest).
No progress bar, no step counter, and no 'step 2 of 3': it must not imply that every guest follows every step, and it must not gamify.
Baseline: the 'Menu & more' sheet appears only after rating.
candidates.visualSystem:
Swiss/International. The brand background is a flat field; brand text is the ink; one derived accent. No texture, no rules except a single 1px column rule.
Type: Commissioner as one variable family, 400-700. It has Bulgarian locl, and its neutral humanist sans suits Swiss type; its flare axis is not relied on. Scale contrast is the whole system: 40px question against 13px labels.
The caption is the display element: the selected value's numeral at 96px outline beside the word ('4 · Very good'). It changes the same way for every value.
Buttons: full-width 56px, radius 0-4 for a strict grid. Sheets use a 16px top radius.
Works in light or dark polarity automatically; the default blue passes on white (5.17:1).
candidates.imagery: None, in beta or later. A future owned photo could appear only as a small square in the header, because the direction's premise is focus. A legacy hero renders at the top of the question view capped at 20svh. The same no-photo identity prints as a minimal card: wordmark, question, QR on white, short URL.
candidates.signatureMoment: The numeral. When a star is selected, a large outline numeral and its word crossfade in beside the stars (120ms): '1 · Poor' through '5 · Excellent', the same size, weight and motion for every value. It makes the choice unmistakable at arm's length, for older guests too, without colour. On submit, the question view slides up 12px and fades out as the after-rating view fades in: a same-document View Transition, 280ms.
candidates.stateNotes:
Uses the shared rating core (see C1) with these differences.
- Focus moves to each view's heading on swap, and a status message announces 'Rating sent privately'.
- Save error: stays in the question view, with the numeral and selection kept.
- After-rating view: Google card with identical copy for 1-5. The degraded copy sits in the same place. The private note expands inline under Google; it is never a separate screen that could stand in for Google.
- Feedback sent: collapses to one line.
- 'Menu & more' sheet: a focus-trapped dialog with a close button, Escape support, and links as 64px rows.
- Withdrawn: a calm full view with 'Start a new response'.
- Unavailable: brand-free, same Swiss type.
- Analytics disclosure: inline in the question view below the privacy line, detaching after 'Got it'.
- 200% text and landscape: views become normal scrolling sections; they never clip.
- The browser back button behaves normally, with no history traps.
candidates.betaFeasibility: High. View swapping uses the existing controller states; the e2e flow and accessible names are unchanged apart from pack-v2 labels. Needs Commissioner self-hosted, the token helper, pack v2 and theme isolation. The links sheet from arrival is a proposal; baseline puts it after rating.
needsNewCapability: Self-hosted Commissioner variable subset
Derived accent roles
guest-ui v2 language packs plus e2e updates
Accessible bottom-sheet dialog for links
Links from arrival via the sheet (proposal)
candidates.risks: Stepped screens can feel like a survey, which premium hotels dislike, and they may seem abrupt. Hiding links in a sheet reduces discovery. Full-height views can disorient screen-magnifier users unless focus and headings are handled carefully. A giant '1' could feel stark; neutral words and identical treatment mitigate that. Swiss neutrality risks a template look if brand colour is weak. It is the least 'hospitable' direction.
candidates.relationToSignatureStay: Rejects Signature Stay's atmosphere and photography in favour of pure focus. It keeps word endpoints, the privacy line at the action and the score-invariant Google card. Its value is a fallback style for properties with no brand material and for high-traffic placements; it could be the default before an admin picks a composition.

candidates.name: Window (place pattern in a frame)
candidates.thesis: Replace missing photography with a sense of place drawn as pattern. Each property picks a pattern family (mountain contours, sea lines, geometric weave, ink marbling, vineyard rows, carved stone) tinted by its own colours and seen through one architectural frame. The same frame later holds an owned photo and surrounds the QR code on print, so the no-photo and photo versions are one design.
candidates.bestFor: Properties with a strong place story: mountain lodges and spa towns (Bansko, Velingrad, the Rhodopes), seaside hotels (Varna, Sozopol), wineries, heritage guesthouses, family resorts, traditional restaurants (mehana). It works on light or dark stages.
candidates.structure:
Centred, calm and vertical.
(1) Identity strip: language control top-right.
(2) A frame shape (arch by default; also a rounded portal and a square window, chosen with the pattern), 58% of the width and about 30svh tall, centred, containing the pattern.
(3) Beneath the frame: displayName in a warm serif, centred, 2 lines max; the h1 (title) as a small-caps place line.
(4) The rating block, centred: question, stars, caption, 'Send privately', privacy line.
(5) The description.
(6) 'Around {name}' links from arrival (proposal) as hairline rows with icons, at most 4.
(7) Footer.
After a rating the frame stays; the rating block becomes the receipt line, followed by the Google card, the private card when eligible, the links and 'Your response'.
Baseline: links after the cards.
candidates.visualSystem:
Colour:
- Pattern in the derived accent at 3:1 plus one lighter tint of it, on the stage surface.
- The frame edge is a 1px accent line.
- Everything else follows the shared derived roles.
Type: Lora 500 for the name and question (warm, literary; self-hosted about 29KB; Bulgarian forms), plus Manrope 400/600 for text (about 59KB total).
- Lora is wide, so the Cyrillic one-line cap is about 22px at 320px and the name uses a 2-line layout.
- Short v2 BG labels keep Manrope buttons on one line.
Shape: the frame is the only large shape. Hairline rows, 10px button radius, no shadows, no grain (the pattern is the texture).
Patterns: 8-12 curated SVG families, each under 6KB, parametrised by the brand hex and a seed from the property id so two lodges never get identical drawings.
candidates.imagery: The pattern is the beta imagery: no uploads needed, tiny, and owned by RepKey's design library. Patterns come from landscape and material, not sacred or ethnographic motifs; any textile-derived geometry is drawn with a Bulgarian designer's review. A future owned photo fills the frame (object-fit cover, focal point). A legacy hero_image_url renders inside the frame. Print: the frame surrounds the QR (quiet zone kept clear inside it) on table tents and reception cards.
candidates.signatureMoment: The drawing. On first load the pattern draws itself inside the frame once: stroke-dashoffset over about 600ms, one pass, then still. It is static under reduced motion and never repeats on return. Motion after submission is identical to the shared core and has nothing to do with the score. The frame is the continuity device between printed card, page and future photo.
candidates.stateNotes:
Uses the shared rating core (see C1) with these differences.
- The frame and pattern are static in every state after the first draw.
- Selected stars and focus use the same accent as the pattern, so the page reads as one colour.
- Google card: neutral surface, identical for 1-5. The degraded copy uses the same card.
- Private card: after Google.
- Withdrawn: a calm card; the frame remains, which reassures the guest they are still on the property's page.
- Unavailable: brand-free with no frame or pattern.
- Analytics disclosure: inline under the privacy line.
- Long names: 2 lines under the frame; the frame shrinks to 24svh when the name wraps, to keep the stars in the first screen.
- The pattern SVG is aria-hidden with no text.
- Forced colours: the pattern disappears and the frame outline stays.
candidates.betaFeasibility: Medium. The guest mechanics are identical to C1, but the pattern library is real design work: 8-12 families, drawn, performance-tested and reviewed for cultural sensitivity. It also needs a new Brand Profile field (pattern family plus frame shape) and admin UI to choose it. Font self-hosting, the token helper, pack v2 and theme isolation are as in C1. It could ship in beta with 3-4 families.
needsNewCapability: Curated SVG pattern library parametrised by brand colour and a property seed
Pattern family and frame shape fields on the Brand Profile, plus an admin chooser with preview
Derived accent roles
Self-hosted Lora and Manrope
guest-ui v2 language packs plus e2e updates
Print templates using the frame around the QR
Links from arrival (proposal)
Future: owned photo inside the frame via SAFE-01
candidates.risks: Patterns can tip into wallpaper, folklore kitsch or cultural appropriation without careful art direction. The arch is a recognisable social-media trend and could date quickly. It adds another admin decision (pattern plus frame). Complex SVGs can cost paint time on low-end phones, so cap node counts. The pattern and the wordmark may compete for attention. Seeded variation may produce a drawing an owner dislikes, so offer a 'regenerate' action.
candidates.relationToSignatureStay: Keeps Signature Stay's centred serif name and question, outline stars, privacy line and quiet link rows. It answers its biggest weakness, dependence on generated photography, with a frame that holds a place-specific drawing today and the photo Signature Stay imagined once SAFE-01 allows uploads.

adminImplications: Treat the guest look as a Property-level brand decision: a curated composition (e.g. Carved Stillness, Folio, Table Card) plus the existing three hex values. Retire the legacy per-Portal Theme presets and the list-row swatch, which do nothing for guests on v2 snapshots. Show the real brand in the list instead.

Build a derived-token engine behind the three colour fields rather than adding colour pickers. It covers stage polarity, accent at 3:1, accent text at 4.5:1, idle star at a 55% mix, and the black-or-white label. Enforce primary contrast at publish: today assertCompletePortalPublicationExperience only checks that the ratio parses. Show admins a pass or a suggested fix, never raw ratios. Consider replacing the SaaS-blue default palette, and the mismatched #6366F1 renderer fallback, with a neutral hospitality default.

Make the preview render the real guest page: the published or draft snapshot, localized title and description, brand profile, the chosen composition and fonts, the language switch, and every state. States: entry, selected, error, after rating at 1 star and at 5 stars side by side (to show Google is identical), degraded Google, private note, receipt, withdrawn, unavailable. Add a 'Try as guest' simulation that writes no responses or analytics and never navigates to Google.

Map the fields honestly in the editor. The wordmark is displayName (Property Settings, not localized). The h1 is the localized title or portal override, so guide admins to write a placement or welcome line ('Spa reception') instead of repeating the name. The short description is a secondary paragraph. The question, buttons and receipts come from immutable language packs and are not editable. Round one's editable question and character counters are not in the model.

Creation should follow placement, experience, review, then publish and distribute. Lead with where guests meet the portal, not with name, slug and theme. Turn the scattered publish prerequisites into one guided checklist: token issued, responsible manager, verified Google destination, complete brand profile, content for every enabled locale. Say who can fix each item (AccountAdmin versus Property Manager).

Add 'Publish changes' while live so admins no longer have to disable and re-publish, with a brief outage. Expose the existing rollbackPortalPublication as an append-only action in a Timeline-style publication ledger. Show property-wide edits with the list of affected portals, and never silently update live snapshots.

Rebuild Settings around scope. Property-wide items (brand, composition, fallback content, approved destinations) go in one AccountAdmin area. Portal-local items (placement wording, links, threshold, managers, languages) go in another. One primary action per area replaces six or more separate save buttons, following the inbox rules: hairlines not boxes, facts versus controls.

Links editor: add localized EN/BG labels and category titles, and render iconKey from a curated icon set. Show each link's approval status in place, since unapproved or lapsed links are silently dropped today. Recommend at most 4 visible links. Offer keyboard move controls next to drag. Replace the 'Review sites' empty-state suggestion with 'Useful links'. Allow Tripadvisor or Booking only as 'Find us on' links, never styled as review asks.

Explain equal access with confidence at the threshold setting. Relabel it along the lines of 'Offer a private note at N stars or below; Google stays available to every guest'. Never add score-dependent Google visibility, copy or a 'pause Google' toggle. Short onboarding copy should explain why this protects the owner's Google profile, since buyers arrive expecting gating vendors' 'filtration'.

Share and distribution: print templates per composition (table tent, reception card, NFC card), the QR on a light plate with a 4-module quiet zone, error correction M by default or Q/H with a centre mark, the short URL printed as text, and NFC instructions that match the iOS and Android 17 notification tap. Allow placement naming. Revisit the 'shown once' address rule so printers can re-download without rotating: a security decision that needs design.

Analytics should add a property-level portals overview and group scope, not just per-portal tabs. Show qualified scans, then private ratings, then Google opened, plus private-feedback volume.
