Label the Google measure 'Guests who opened Google', never 'reviews' or 'Review Clicks'. Align the range model and default with the dashboard (?range=, rolling 30 days). Keep availability by exception with provenance on demand. Keep the 10-rating comparison floor. No leaderboards, staff attribution or quotas.

Monitoring: surface Portal Health (healthy, degraded or unavailable, with reasons such as google_destination_unavailable, responsibility_needed or public_address_unavailable) as a column and a filter in the portal list and on the property overview, not only as notifications. Later additions: secondary-link selections (already in the aggregate) and a QR versus NFC split by access artifact.

Keep the admin neutral and purple, following the inbox language, while the guest page carries the property brand. Admin previews should frame the guest page in a device outline at 320/390, not restyle the admin around the property's palette.

Fonts and performance: self-host the curated OFL faces with unicode-range splits and stop loading Satoshi from api.fontshare.com on /p. Satoshi has no Cyrillic and is a third-party request on a no-tracker page. Isolate /p from THEME_INIT_SCRIPT and from shadcn app tokens.

Language readiness: show missing translations per locale in review and publish. Batch every guest-copy change into one guest-ui v2 pack version, since live portals keep v1 until republished. Offer a 'republish to adopt new copy' action in the portal list. Get a native-speaker review of BG strings for neutrality before they ship.

Analytics disclosure: coordinate with counsel to remove the sessionStorage visit-dedupe marker and dedupe server-side. Then move the 'Portal analytics information' region inline under the submit button, keeping its accessible name, the 'Got it' button and the detach behaviour so the seven e2e call sites still pass. Add a 'Cookies and device storage' section to the guest privacy notice.

Future photography (after SAFE-01): property-owned uploads with a rights attestation, moderation and focal point. Each composition declares its photo slot and crop, so an upload never breaks the no-photo design. Wire the organisation logo into portals with a luminance check. Never pull photos from the GBP or Places APIs without written confirmation from Google.

scores.strengths: It has the strongest no-photo answer of the six. Type, rules and whitespace are the identity, so the page is finished on day one without SAFE-01. The dotted-leader index is a real hospitality object: it reads as a menu card or a hotel directory. That makes it memorable and suits both a boutique hotel and a bistro or wine bar, the only direction with a credible claim on both. The flush-left, asymmetric column and 2px radii are as far from a centred SaaS card as any candidate. The timestamped stub ('Received privately · 19 September, 14:32') feels like the property's own letterhead, not a form confirmation. Deep and monochrome BG brands (Sense olive-grey, Les Fleurs purple, Щастливеца oxblood) look better here than on any dark stage. The first screen fits comfortably: masthead, question, stars, button and privacy line total about 490px of the roughly 550px visible on a 375x667 phone with Safari's toolbars showing. Sofia Sans gives the narrowest BG labels.
scores.weaknesses: For the tired guest at night it is a bright cream or white page at a dim table or bar. The 'night edition' is optional, but evening restaurants would need it by default. The action is cluttered: numerals 1-5 under the stars, endpoint words and a caption word are three labelling systems exactly where the thumb is. Drop the numerals. The wordmark (34px serif) and the question (30px serif) are two display moments of almost equal weight, which contradicts the 'one serif moment' thesis and blurs hierarchy; one should be far smaller. The auto-width button is a smaller target than the full-width buttons in the other directions and looks less like 'the thing to press'. The Playfair lineage leans toward wedding stationery and wine labels, and owners who expect a wow photo may read it as 'a nicely typeset form'. Its signature element, the index, depends on two new things: links from arrival and localized link labels. The baseline variant loses much of the charm. Pure-white brands look cold unless the admin accepts a paper tone.

scores.strengths: It carries forward the direction the owner already chose, so there is recognition and no re-litigation. It is the best candidate for the night scan: a dark, low-glare stage with warm off-white 18px text that is kind to tired eyes at a bar or checkout. The rating block is the undisputed hero, and the first screen fits at 375x667 with toolbars showing (about 530px of roughly 550px available), though with little spare. Deriving polarity from the property's own hex values is the honest way to get champagne only for gold, bronze and tan brands such as Maxi Park, Alpen and Staria Chinar. The settle transition (stars condensing into one receipt line) is the most refined motion in the set and fully score-invariant. Swapping 'Share my rating' for 'Send privately' fixes a real honesty problem in Signature Stay. It is the most feasible direction, with nothing new beyond the shared core.
scores.weaknesses: It removes the thing that made Signature Stay beautiful. In that image the architectural photograph did most of the work, and the replacement (a radial tonal gradient plus grain plus an optional monogram) is the weakest no-photo answer of the three serif directions. Dark gradient, gold outline stars and Cormorant is also a stock 'luxury spa template' look, so two gold-brand properties will look near-identical and memorability is low. Cormorant is fragile and overused in wellness branding. Keeping it at 600 helps, but it still reads as generic spa. It fits restaurants poorly outside fine dining: a bistro or mehana on an ink-and-champagne stage feels overdressed. Auto-polarity means deep and red brands land on a light ivory stage that is essentially a centred, weaker C2, so the concept's identity fragments. With the default palette (SaaS blue on ink) it looks like an app's dark mode. First-screen margin is tight, and a 3-line BG question plus a legacy hero leaves about 20px spare.

scores.strengths: It is the most memorable and recognisable direction. The property's colour plus a huge wordmark makes the page theirs within 200ms, with no photo needed. Print-to-screen continuity (the table tent is the poster and plate) is a genuine hospitality insight no competitor has, and it makes the scan feel like one object. It has the best thumb ergonomics of the brand-led directions: stars at about 60-72% of screen height on a plate that starts about 186px down. Sofia Sans is a Bulgarian-designed family with Bulgarian Cyrillic defaults, which is a real local story for owners, and Extra Condensed handles long and Cyrillic names. It is excellent for restaurants, bars, grills and loud brands (Dobro orange, Happy red), the half of the market C1 and C2 serve badly. Refusing to use red for errors is a sharp detail.
scores.weaknesses: A colour header with a 24px-radius sheet overlapping it and a soft shadow is the Wolt, Glovo and Bolt Food restaurant-page pattern, ubiquitous in Bulgaria. It risks reading as 'order food here' or a generic mobile app, not a premium welcome, so the plate needs less radius, no generic shadow and some paper texture to escape that. For a boutique or luxury hotel a 38svh saturated field feels fast-casual and loud. Hotels would likely reject it except for poolside and restaurant placements. At night a large saturated orange or red field glares. Lowercase heavy condensed wordmarks are a 2020s DTC trend that will date. Owners will notice that the derived plate accent (#E27100) is not their orange. Monochrome brands get a severe black poster. With four 60px link rows it drifts toward 'a nicer Linktree'.

scores.strengths: It has the highest ceiling for place and memorability. A Rhodope contour or Black Sea line drawing tinted in the property's own colour says 'this place' in a way a gradient or colour field cannot, and it is the only direction whose no-photo imagery is specific to the property. The frame is a smart continuity device that holds a pattern today, a photo after SAFE-01 and the QR on print, so no-photo and photo are one design. Lora plus Manrope is warm and literary with Bulgarian forms. It fits mountain lodges, spa towns, wineries and mehanas better than any other candidate. The one-time draw-on is a nice arrival beat.
scores.weaknesses: The arch frame is the 2021-24 Instagram and Canva 'boho arch' trope, so it risks looking templated and dated within a season. The beauty depends entirely on pattern art that does not exist yet: 8-12 families, cultural review, and a seeded generator that can produce drawings an owner dislikes. Folklore or kitsch risk is real in the BG market. The centred frame, serif name, question and button read as a wedding invitation. The first screen does not reliably fit: identity strip (about 44px) plus a 30svh frame (about 166px) plus a 2-line serif name, place line and 3-line question puts the button at about 565px, below the roughly 550px visible on a 375x667 phone with Safari's toolbars showing, even after the 24svh shrink. It adds admin decisions (pattern plus frame). Structurally it is close to C1 (centred, image slot on top, serif name), so it adds less distinctness to a family than its visuals suggest. Feasibility is medium.

scores.strengths: It is the most effortless first interaction: huge question, stars and one full-width button in the thumb zone, done in two taps. That is ideal for check-out desks, spa exits and café counters. The large word caption ('4 · Very good') is legible at arm's length and for older guests, and it does not rely on colour. It still works with no brand material or the default palette. Careful handling of focus, headings and the back button, and no progress bar, avoid survey gamification. Its thumb-zone placement and big caption are lessons every other direction should borrow.
scores.weaknesses: It is the least hospitable and least on-brand. It looks like Typeform or a kiosk survey, the generic-SaaS feel this round is meant to escape, and premium hotels dislike survey-feeling pages. There is nothing memorable about the property: identity is a 48px header strip, so a boutique hotel and a café look the same. A 96px outline numeral puts a score in the guest's face and makes '1' feel stark, like grading the staff. Full-height views plus a hidden links sheet reduce discovery (the diner wanting the menu must find 'Menu & more'), and swapping views can disorient magnifier users. Commissioner's Swiss neutrality needs a strong brand colour that most beta properties will not have. It is best kept as a fallback or kiosk mode, not a beta direction.

scores.strengths: It has a clear object metaphor, and it is the only direction that tells the multi-placement story (Spa · Reception) that portal groups already support. The tear-off stub is a concrete, score-invariant receipt moment. It works with any polarity because colour lives in a header band, and the band gives future photography an obvious key-card slot. The NFC pass as print collateral is coherent.
scores.weaknesses: It is the most SaaS-looking candidate: a centred card on a tinted backdrop, 20px radius, two-layer shadow and Manrope only is Stripe checkout, an Apple Wallet pass or a fintech card, the look the brief bans. There is no hospitality warmth or typographic character, so it is neither beautiful for a boutique hotel nor appetising for a restaurant. The pass or boarding-pass metaphor implies a reservation or identity the product explicitly lacks, which a tired guest may misread as something to keep or show. On a 375px phone the card wastes width and on 320px it goes full-bleed, which kills the metaphor. Tear-plus-stacked-cards adds three card surfaces after rating, making the page heavier where the others get lighter. The tear animation risks gimmickry. Its best ideas (the placement line, the stub receipt) can be lifted into other directions.

out.note:
I rated each direction through the guest and brand lens by measuring its first screen against a 375x667 phone with Safari's toolbars showing, about 550px of visible height (svh). I also checked it against the Signature Stay concept image in docs/design/portal-experience/concepts/signature-stay.png. That image's appeal comes mostly from the architectural photograph, so every direction was judged mainly on how finished it looks with no photo.

**Best distinct three:** Folio (C2), Carved Stillness (C1) and Table Card (C3).
- C1 and C2 share a serif lineage, but they differ where it matters. C1 is a dark, centred atmosphere stage that suits the night scan and spa or resort hotels. C2 is a light, flush-left editorial page built around typography and a link index, suiting boutique hotels and wine bars.
- C3 is the only strong answer for restaurants and loud brands.
- Window (C6) is the runner-up. It has the most property-specific imagery but was not picked for three reasons: it is structurally close to C1, its first screen overflows on a small phone, and its arch frame risks looking dated.
- Pass (C4) looks the most like generic SaaS, and One Thing at a Time (C5) looks like a survey. I recommend dropping both as directions.

**Grafts that would raise the three:**
- C1: replace the generic radial gradient and grain band with an optional place pattern taken from C6. This is C1's weakest point.
- C2: make the night edition the default for evening restaurant placements, drop the numerals under the stars, and make the wordmark and the question clearly different in size.
- C3: avoid the food-delivery-app look. Use a smaller plate radius, no stock soft shadow and a paper texture on the plate, and keep the wordmark from following trends.
- All three: borrow C5's thumb-zone placement and large caption word, and C4's placement line in the title.

Scores differ on purpose: no direction reached 8, because each serves only part of the market until these grafts are applied.

scores.strengths: Best balance of premium and buildable. Everything guests see comes from data that exists on main: the three Brand Profile hex values (text/background is already validated at 4.5:1 or better, and contrast is symmetric, so the dark stage inversion keeps it), displayName (max 120), localized title (max 120) and description (max 500), links and categories, threshold and Google status. The shared core is fully compliant. The Google card takes no score props, sits in the same slot for every score and moves identically for 1 and 5, which matches ADR 0044's anti-gating rule and its architecture test. The private card sits below Google, so Google's ordering never changes. The copy is honest: 'Send privately' replaces the misleading 'Share my rating', 'Opens Google · you may need to sign in', and the withdraw copy says nothing already posted on Google is affected. No personal data ('No need to include your name'), no public scores, no seals. Accessibility is strong: 56px outline stars with a 55% idle-mix outline at 3:1 or better, fill plus stroke weight (not hue alone), word endpoints, a reserved caption line, focus moved to the new heading after the settle, a 100ms crossfade under reduced motion, and 18px body text on dark. The correction windows it quotes (change 1h, withdraw 24h) match the code. It is the owner's chosen direction without the invented photography, and it ships with no photo.
scores.weaknesses: 1. The no-photo band is a radial tonal field from the primary. Without careful art direction that is the 'gradient blob' hero this team's design rules ban, and it can read as empty. 2. It does not cover every brand alone. Deep brands flip to a light stage that is effectively a second composition to design, QA and explain to admins ('why is my page dark?'). 3. The Brand Profile default primary #2563EB on the dark stage reads as an app dark mode. The domain also has a second default (#6366F1 in the Portal constructor), so the token helper must pick one source of truth. 4. Heaviest type payload of the six (about 107KB across Cormorant Garamond with small caps, oldstyle figures and Cyrillic, plus Ysabeau). It fits the budget only if unicode-range splitting and preloading just the question face are enforced. 5. The first screen is tight at 375x667 with Safari toolbars (56px strip + 26svh band + a 3-line question + stars + caption + 52px button is roughly the whole viewport). A 3-line BG question can push the submit below the fold, so it needs a measured gate. 6. The label change breaks four e2e pins, and a v2 pack is a new recorded languagePackVersion on every response, not a string edit. 7. The monogram 'seal' must never gain a check or ring styling that reads as verification. 8. Grain over text on dark must be excluded from text areas, or measured contrast drifts.

scores.strengths: The most distinct of the six, and it serves the half of the market Signature Stay does not: restaurants and loud brands. The black-or-white onPrimary wordmark is sound: the worst case of the better of black or white is about 4.58:1, and the wordmark is large text. The plate accent is derived to 3:1 and 4.5:1 while the poster keeps the true brand colour. It handles a red brand properly: errors use text plus an icon and never red alone. The poster never reacts to the score, and the Google card is a neutral card identical for 1 to 5. The unavailable state is brand-free and reveals nothing about the property. Print-to-screen continuity is a real product benefit, and QR on a light plate follows the scan guidance. It needs only three hex values and displayName, with one self-hosted Bulgarian-designed family (about 60KB).
scores.weaknesses: 1. First-screen risk is the worst of the recommended set. A 38svh poster, a 2-line auto-fit name (displayName can be 120 characters) and a plate overlap leave about 330px for the question, stars, caption, submit and privacy line at 375x667 with toolbars. Stars may show while the submit does not, which breaks the 'whole block in the first screen' rule. 2. The icon set assumes a curated iconKey, but on main iconKey is a free-form string of up to 50 characters that the guest UI never reads. It needs an enum, a migration of existing values, and a Links-tab picker. 3. The 'call link' icon cannot be built: destinations must be allowlisted HTTPS, so tel: is rejected. 4. It suggests writing facts into link labels ('kitchen until 23:00'). That is the fake-facts pattern the research rejects, and it freezes stale hours into an immutable published snapshot. 5. The concept leans on links from arrival (diners want the menu), which conflicts with the current e2e pin, and the baseline variant weakens it. 6. The auto-fit wordmark for Latin and Cyrillic names up to 120 characters is real algorithm and test work. 7. A 24px plate radius with a soft shadow can slide into a template look. 8. The accent on the plate visibly differs from the brand orange or gold, which owners will query. 9. It is a poor fit for luxury hotels, so it cannot be the default.

scores.strengths: A light editorial stage that suits deep and monochrome brands (Les Fleurs, Щастливеца, Sense) that a dark stage cannot carry. It is feasible on today's data with plain CSS (rules, dotted leaders, perforation). The type decisions are responsible: the serif is used only at 22px and above, and Sofia Sans uses Bulgarian forms by default with the narrowest BG button labels, which is the lowest overflow risk at 320px. The stub receipt is identical for every score. The Google panel keeps the shared score-invariant component and the same degraded copy. The private 'letter' has a persistent label. Error text is never red alone, and the column reflows at 200% text. An inset-plate photo slot means the page never depends on imagery. This is a credible answer to the light stage C1 needs.
scores.weaknesses: 1. The composition hinges on a text-heavy link index, but link labels and category titles are single strings on main, so a BG guest gets a mixed-language index. It truly needs localized labels (a schema and admin change), not just nice-to-have. 2. The index-first layout also needs links from arrival (it conflicts with the e2e pin), and the baseline variant, with the index after Google, loses the concept's main idea. 3. The numerals 1 to 5 under the stars will duplicate the radio names ('1 star' plus '1') unless they are aria-hidden. 4. The index must be a real ordered list with decorative leaders. 5. The stub prints the exact time of the previous guest's response on a shared device until it is cleared. 6. White-background brands need a new 'paper tone' admin decision, or they read as cold. 7. The auto-width 48px button is a smaller target than the others (it still passes 2.5.8). 8. Bulgarian locl support in Playfair 2 at a static optical size of 36 is asserted, not yet verified in a build. 9. It is the closest to C1 of all the candidates (serif, hairlines, small caps, privacy line). It stays distinct only if it keeps flush-left paper and the index; otherwise it collapses into C1's light stage. 10. The risk that it reads as a 'nicely typeset form' works against the owner's premium goal.

scores.strengths: Maps closely to today's PublicPortalContent order, so structural risk is the lowest. The placement line reuses the localized Portal override title that exists on main, and Portal Groups with several portals per property are real today. It has the lightest type payload (Manrope, about 30KB), tabular figures in the stub, and shorter v2 BG labels that fix wrapping at 320px. Card order is explicit and compliant: receipt, then Google, then a quieter private card. It explicitly bans guest name, room, reservation and date. NFC print copy is honest about the notification tap. Nothing is fixed-height at 200% text.
scores.weaknesses: 1. The metaphor itself is a truth risk. A 'pass', 'key card' or 'boarding pass' implies a booking, ticket or saved identity RepKey does not have, and guests may try to save or keep it. 2. The 'Nearby' heading misdescribes links (booking, website and social are not nearby), which is a copy-honesty defect. 3. A shadowed card on a tinted backdrop with 20/12/8 radii is the most SaaS-template pattern of the six, against the owner's premium goal. 4. The tinted backdrop adds another surface on which every derived role must be re-checked at publish. 5. Most portals will have no override title, so the band degrades to just the name and the placement idea disappears. 6. At 320px it goes full-bleed and the object metaphor is lost. 7. Rights UI inside the stub crowds a small area, and the greyed 'Withdrawn' stub risks sub-4.5:1 text. 8. The tear animation reads as a gimmick.

scores.strengths: The strongest first-screen and thumb-zone guarantee. It works with the default palette (#2563EB on white at 5.17:1) and needs the least new capability. Accessible names and the e2e flow are unchanged apart from the v2 pack. The accessibility spec is careful: focus moves to each view heading, a status message is announced, the Menu sheet traps focus with Escape support, history is not trapped, and views become normal sections at 200% text and in landscape. It has no step counter or progress bar, which avoids survey gamification. The Google card is never behind a step, and the private note expands under it rather than replacing it. The numeral and word treatment is identical for 1 to 5.
scores.weaknesses: 1. It fails the owner's explicit brief: Swiss restraint on a flat field is the least premium and least hospitable option, and neutral full-height steps read as a survey or template. 2. A 'Menu & more' button in the header from arrival moves the link tree above the rating in the DOM and visual order, which is more prominent than a below-fold list. That is at odds with 'review gateway first, link tree second', and the dialog adds a focus-trap surface. 3. The 96px outline-only numeral is thin stroked text that is hard for low-vision guests to read and must meet 3:1 as a non-text graphic. 4. Swapping full-height views can disorient magnifier users. 5. 100svh views push links and the 'Your response' area far down. 6. It is best kept as the fallback composition for properties with no brand material, not as a flagship direction.

scores.strengths: The most original answer to the photo block: a place pattern inside a frame that later holds an owned photo and also frames the QR in print. It gives the most honest feasibility rating of the six (Medium). The pattern is aria-hidden and disappears in forced-colours mode while the frame outline stays. The draw is one-shot and static under reduced motion. It considers cultural sensitivity, with landscape rather than sacred motifs and a Bulgarian designer's review. It uses the shared compliant core, and the unavailable state has no frame.
scores.weaknesses: 1. It cannot ship on the existing model. It needs a curated SVG pattern library of 8 to 12 drawn, reviewed and performance-tested families, which is external design and cultural-review work with no owner in the beta. It also needs two new Brand Profile fields, an admin chooser with preview, seeded generation and a 'regenerate' action. 2. The first screen overflows. A strip, a 30svh frame, a 2-line centred Lora name (Cyrillic capped at about 22px) and a place line above the rating block exceed 375x667 with toolbars, so the submit falls below the fold even with the 24svh shrink. 3. The stroke-dashoffset draw animates paint rather than a compositor property. 4. 'Around {name}' mislabels non-local links. 5. The arch is a dating social-media trend, and patterns risk folklore kitsch. 6. It adds another admin decision in a beta that already asks for three colours.

out.note:
I checked the candidates against main: CONTEXT.md, BETA.md, ADR 0044, portal-contrast.ts, portal-theme-style.ts, the portal-experience DTOs, guest-language-pack.ts, guest-response-lifecycle.ts and e2e/critical/guest-portal.spec.ts.

**Why these three.** C1, C3 and C2 cover dark and premium, loud and restaurant, and light and deep brands, all over one shared component. Condition on the pick: C2 is the closest to C1. Keep it flush-left paper with the index. Also, C1's own 'light stage' should *be* C2, not a third serif composition. If the owner prefers the three most different options over coverage, swap C2 for C5, not C4.

**Defects in the shared core (all six inherit these; fix before prototyping):**
- **Duplicate button name.** The core uses 'Send privately' for both the rating submit and the private-note submit. While 'Change' is open after a rating, two buttons share one accessible name. Use 'Send note privately' for the note.
- **"No ads or trackers".** The privacy line says this, but rk_guest_session cookies exist, and ADR 0044 forbids claiming anonymity when session identifiers are stored. Use 'No ads or third-party trackers' and get counsel sign-off.
- **Breaking label changes.** Renaming 'Submit private rating', the 'Private feedback' textbox and 'Send private feedback' breaks e2e pins in guest-portal.spec.ts and beta-product-journeys.spec.ts. The language pack version is recorded and validated on each response, so v2 packs are a versioned rollout, not a string edit.
- **Links from arrival.** Every design's 'links from arrival' breaks the explicit e2e assertion that destinations are absent before rating. Ship the baseline variants first.

**Model facts that limit feasibility:**
- **Contrast.** The Brand Profile schema enforces text/background contrast at 4.5:1 but never checks the primary, which confirms the need for derived roles.
- **Two default primaries.** The Brand Profile default is #2563EB; the Portal constructor default is #6366F1.
- **Logos.** logoUrl and defaultHeroImageUrl accept only null.
- **Link labels** are single, unlocalized strings. This hurts C2 most.
- **iconKey** is a free string of up to 50 characters that the guest UI never renders.
- **Destinations** are HTTPS-only, so there are no tel: links.
- **THEME_INIT_SCRIPT** in __root.tsx runs on /p.

**Open doc tension, not scored.** BETA.md says rating first, then Google. ADR 0044 says private rating is optional and the review link must be invariant across response 'values and states'. No candidate lets a guest reach Google without rating first. That is consistent with BETA but should be reconciled in the ADR before an external compliance claim ('cannot get your profile flagged') is used in sales.

**Before any direction is called done:** add a measured 375x667-with-toolbars and 320px gate that proves the whole rating block (question, stars, caption, submit) is visible, in EN and BG. C1 and C3 are the tightest of the chosen three.

scores.strengths: Lowest-risk route to a premium beta, and it continues the direction the owner already chose (Signature Stay). The rating block is the hero and has no competition from a platform grid, so in a side-by-side with Ratestar's crowded video page it wins clearly on calm and legibility. It shows the score-invariant Google card as a trust signal instead of five gold emoji stars and a verified tick. Colours are derived from the three Brand Profile hex values, so admins get no new pickers. Polarity follows the brand, which is a real answer to the finding that 6 of 15 primaries fail as stars on light stages. The contrast claims hold when I recompute them (#2563EB on #111827 is 3.43:1). The photo slot is defined for later, and a legacy hero_image_url degrades cleanly. The 'settle' receipt moment treats a 1-star and a 5-star rating the same, which is honest and compliant. 'Send privately' fixes the misleading 'Share my rating'. It suits spa and thermal hotels, the exact segment in the Ratestar reference: Maxi Park's #AA8453 is one of its own examples.
scores.weaknesses: With no photo, the atmosphere band is a gradient plus grain plus an optional monogram. Next to Ratestar's festive lobby video, a GM may read it as empty or as 'the app in dark mode'. It gives no sense of place. Premium on the dark stage only works for gold, bronze, tan and thermal-blue accents. Everyone else, including a family hotel on the default blue, drops to a light stage. That light stage is an unspecified twin, so C1 alone does not cover the market. Properties with similar hex values will look alike (ink, Cormorant, grain), and the monogram is the only thing telling them apart. That hurts in a group demo. First-screen fit is unproven. A 56px strip, a 26svh band and a three-line 32px question sit above 56px stars, a caption, a 52px button and a privacy line. That is tight on the real Safari visible height of an iPhone SE (about 548 CSS px, not 667). It needs measuring, not asserting. The fonts are the heaviest of the six at about 107KB. Cormorant stays delicate on dark even at weight 600. Admins will need an explanation of why polarity flips with their brand.

scores.strengths: The only direction built for restaurants and loud brands, roughly half the buyers, and the one that beats Ratestar most visibly with no photo. The GM's own colour and a huge wordmark fill the top of the screen instantly. A small family venue with a weak or missing logo still gets a strong identity, because the name and colour do the work. Print-to-screen continuity (the table tent and the page share one composition) is a concrete sales tool against Ratestar's branded cards. The admin surface is minimal: three hex values, the display name and link icons. The choice of automatic black or white on the primary is guaranteed at 4.58:1 or better, and the Dobro orange-to-#E27100 derivation checks out at about 3.2:1. It uses one Bulgarian-designed type family (Sofia Sans, about 60KB) with Bulgarian forms by default, which is a nice local story. It handles red brands against error semantics explicitly.
scores.weaknesses: Weak for calm, premium hotels: a saturated field reads as fast casual. It is only as good as the brand hex. The default SaaS blue or a garish SMB colour yields a generic app or Linktree-venue look, and a solid colour with the name on it is a known Linktree pattern, so differentiation depends entirely on the wordmark and plate craft. The bottom-sheet plate over a poster is a common delivery-app pattern and can look templated. The derived plate accent is visibly darker than the poster colour, which owners will notice. At 38svh the poster plus a 24px overlap leaves a tight first-screen budget for three-line BG questions. Auto-fitting a 5-120 character wordmark in Latin and Cyrillic is real engineering and a visual-QA risk. Monochrome brands give a severe black poster. It contributes little to the resort and spa segment where Ratestar's reference sits.

scores.strengths: The most typographically distinctive, fully no-photo identity. It is premium through setting rather than atmosphere, which turns the upload block into a design stance. It is the natural light-stage answer for deep and monochrome brands that C1 cannot carry (Les Fleurs purple, Щастливеца oxblood, Sense olive-grey), so together they cover both polarities. The numbered link index with dotted leaders reads like a hotel directory or menu card. That is charming for restaurants, B&Bs and wine bars, and unlike anything in the competitor set. It is cheap to build in plain CSS, with small type, Sofia Sans with Bulgarian forms, and no pattern or photo library. Hierarchy comes from scale contrast, not colour. The Google panel's double rule keeps it neutral for every score.
scores.weaknesses: In a side-by-side with Ratestar's video in front of a Bulgarian GM, it risks reading as 'a nicely typeset form' or a document. Its appeal is designer-led, not mass-market. The composition leans on two things that do not exist yet: links from arrival (a proposed rule change against the current e2e pin) and localized link labels. The baseline variant is visibly weaker. White-background brands look cold unless the admin accepts a paper tone, which adds a control. The flush-left layout and a text-width submit button are unfamiliar and a smaller, less thumb-friendly target than a full-width button. It carries two display ideas (Playfair 2 plus Sofia Sans) with high-contrast hairlines that fail below 22px. Dotted leaders get busy with long BG labels at 320px. The perforated stub duplicates C4's tear. It shares serif and hairline DNA with C1, so it must keep its paper and flush-left identity or the family collapses into one look.

scores.strengths: The strongest emotional answer to 'Ratestar has a video of our lobby': a place-specific drawing (Rhodope contours, Black Sea lines) gives a Velingrad spa or a Sozopol hotel a sense of place with no upload. Buyers will find that desirable and locally resonant. The frame unifies today's pattern, the future owned photo and the printed QR, which is a coherent roadmap pitch. It scales from a family guesthouse (the pattern adds richness a weak brand lacks) to a resort, and works on light or dark stages. Seeding the pattern from the property id avoids identical drawings.
scores.weaknesses: Medium feasibility. It needs 8-12 hand-drawn, performance-tested SVG families, cultural review of anything textile-derived, and a 'regenerate' escape hatch, which is serious design debt for a closed beta. The arch-in-a-frame is a 2021-23 Instagram trend that will date. It can tip into wallpaper or folklore kitsch. It adds admin decisions (pattern family, frame shape, regenerate), which widens the control surface. It has the tightest first screen: strip, a 30svh frame, a two-line serif name, a place line and a three-line question all sit above the stars, and it already needs a shrink rule. Structurally it is C1 with a different image slot (centred serif name and question, hairline rows), so it is not meaningfully distinct from C1. Its pattern idea is better absorbed later as optional content for C1's atmosphere band. Lora with Manrope is a conventional pairing.

scores.strengths: It is the only direction that sells RepKey's real multi-placement model: several portals and portal groups per property, and placement-aware wording such as 'Spa · Reception', which hotel groups can buy. The colour is confined to a header band, so it works for any polarity and weak brands. It has a small payload (Manrope, about 30KB). The NFC or QR card that is literally the pass is neat collateral. The tear-off receipt is memorable and treats every score the same.
scores.weaknesses: A card on a tinted backdrop with layered shadows is a stock SaaS or Apple Wallet pattern, which undercuts 'looks like the property, not a template'. The pass or boarding-pass metaphor implies a reservation or identity RepKey does not have, which is exactly the fake personalisation the research says to avoid. Geometric sans alone gives the least luxury. The card wastes width at 320-375px. After rating it stacks three same-radius cards, which drifts toward the banned uniform-card look. The tear animation risks gimmick, and the perforated stub duplicates C2. In a Ratestar side-by-side it reads as clean but app-like, not hospitable. Its multi-placement strength is an admin and data story that any composition can show through the portal title.

scores.strengths: The fastest and most accessible flow: huge type, the thumb-zone action, and an explicit word plus numeral that makes the choice readable at arm's length. It works with zero brand material (the default blue passes at 5.17:1 on white, which checks out). It is cheap to build on the existing controller states. It is honest: no progress bar, the Google card is never behind a step, and the private note stays inline under Google. Its caption treatment and brand-free rigour are useful for the unavailable state and as a default fallback.
scores.weaknesses: The weakest demo against Ratestar. It reads as a survey kiosk or Typeform, not a property's welcome, and a GM will not buy on it. Swiss neutrality with a weak brand looks like a template, which is the banned pattern. Full-height view swaps feel stepped and abrupt to premium hotels and complicate focus and magnifier use. Hiding links in a sheet cuts discovery of the link tree. A 96px outline '1' beside 'Poor' makes a low score feel stark and conspicuous. It offers no photo path at all. It is a mode or fallback, not a visual direction to sell.

out.note:
Why these three: they cover the axes a buyer cares about with one shared rating core. C1 is dark, quiet and centred, for resorts and spas. C2 is light, editorial and flush-left, for boutique hotels, B&Bs and deep or monochrome brands, and it is C1's missing polarity twin. C3 is a loud colour field, for restaurants, bars and city hotels. Together they make a sensible, limited admin choice of three named compositions with derived colours and no pickers. None of them needs the pattern library or photo uploads.

Why C2 over C6 for the third slot: C6 is the more desirable demo piece, but it is structurally C1 with a different image slot (centred serif, hairline rows). It has medium feasibility and kitsch and trend risk, and the tightest first screen. Its place-pattern idea should instead become an optional post-beta layer inside C1's atmosphere band, with C4's placement wording and C5's word caption and brand-free rigour absorbed into the shared core. C2 earns its place partly because it is needed, not because it is the strongest demo. Its appeal is designer-led and it leans on links from arrival and localized labels, so prototype its baseline variant honestly.

What to verify before committing:
(1) Measure first-screen fit at the real iPhone SE Safari visible height (about 548 CSS px), not 375x667, for C1 and C3, with three-line BG questions and 35-character names.
(2) Replace the default SaaS-blue palette with a neutral hospitality default. On the default brand, C1 reads as an app dark mode and C3 as a generic blue poster, and most beta properties will start there.
(3) Test the family on three contrasting real BG properties side by side (a spa hotel, a family guesthouse with a weak logo, an orange or red restaurant) against the Ratestar screenshot. A no-photo C1 band is the most likely place a GM says 'empty'.
(4) Consolidate type: the trio uses five families today (Cormorant + Ysabeau, Playfair 2 + Sofia Sans, Sofia Sans Extra Condensed). Make Sofia Sans the shared text face in all three, dropping Ysabeau, to cut payload, QA and Bulgarian-form risk.
(5) Keep one receipt metaphor. C2's perforated stub and C4's tear overlap, and C1's 'settle' is the calmer default.

I recomputed the key contrast claims (3.43:1, 5.17:1, 2.59:1, #E27100 at about 3.2:1, and the 4.58:1 floor for automatic black or white labels) and they hold. I did not verify the Bulgarian-form (locl) support claims for each font.

briefs.selectionRationale:
Chosen: Carved Stillness (C1, 22.5 total: guest 7, truth 8, market 7.5), Folio (C2, 21: 7.5 / 7 / 6.5) and Table Card (C3, 21: 7 / 7 / 7). The runners-up scored Window 17.5, Pass 16.5 and One Thing at a Time 16. All three judges independently named these same three as the best distinct set.

The three differ on four axes at once:
- **Polarity:** a dark ink stage, light paper, or a brand colour field over a light plate.
- **Composition:** a centred stage under an atmosphere band, a flush-left editorial column, or a poster over a plate joined by a fold.
- **Identity carrier:** atmosphere (a photo, or the property's initial carved into the stage), typesetting (masthead, printer's rules, a numbered index), or colour plus a giant wordmark.
- **Type voice:** Garamond with its companion humanist sans, a high-contrast transitional serif with a Bulgarian grotesque, or an extra-condensed Bulgarian grotesque used alone.

Together they cover resorts and spas, boutique hotels and evening venues, and restaurants, bars and loud brands. Every brand hex has a home without adding colour pickers.

**What was taken from the runners-up:**
- **Window:** its idea of 'place without photography' became A's carved initial. This is typographic, derived from displayName and needs no pattern library. Window's contour patterns remain a possible post-beta layer for A's band.
- **Pass:** its placement line became every direction's h1 (the portal's localized title). Its rule of 'no guest name, room or booking' became a shared guard.
- **One Thing at a Time:** its thumb-zone discipline and large caption word became the reserved caption slot in every rating block and the measured submit gate.
- **Folio's perforated stub** stays in Folio only, so each direction has exactly one receipt metaphor. Pass's tear is dropped.

**Judges' fixes applied:**
- **A:** replaces the 'gradient blob' band with the carved initial. It gives up its own light stage: brands that cannot carry a dark stage go to Folio, which is what the truth judge asked for.
- **B:** drops the numerals under the stars, separates wordmark (56px) and question (26px) sizes, makes the submit full-width, removes the submission timestamp from the stub, and gains a night edition for evening venues.
- **C:** drops the 24px bottom-sheet radius, the soft shadow and the forced lowercase in favour of a flat fold like a table tent. It removes fact-like link sublines and any tel: link.

**Truth fixes adopted by all three:**
- The note button reads 'Send note privately', which is different from 'Send privately'.
- The privacy line reads 'Shared privately with {name}.' rather than claiming no one else can see it.
- 'No ads or third-party trackers' is subject to counsel sign-off.
- The drawn baseline keeps links after the rating. Links from arrival appears only as a labelled proposal (C6).

directions.name: Carved Stillness
directions.oneLiner: The owner's Signature Stay, rebuilt so it does not depend on photography. It uses a dark tonal stage from the property's own colours, a carved Garamond, and one metal accent, and the private rating is the hero of the first screen.
directions.axis: Polarity: dark ink stage. Composition: centred column under a 232px atmosphere band. Identity carrier: atmosphere, meaning the property's photo or, with no photo, its initial carved tone-on-tone into the stage. Voice: quiet luxury through restraint.
directions.rationale:
This direction has the highest total (22.5). The truth judge ranked it first as the best balance of premium and buildable, it is the kindest to a night-time scan, and it continues the direction the owner already chose.

All three judges named the no-photo band ('radial gradient plus grain plus optional monogram') as its weak point. It is replaced by a mandatory carved initial: the first letter of displayName, set in the display serif at 176px and debossed into the tonal field. It is specific to each property, works in Latin and Cyrillic, needs no uploads and no pattern library, and literally delivers the 'carved' in the name.

Other changes:
- The light-stage twin is removed. Brands whose accent cannot reach 3:1 on dark are routed to Folio, so the family stays distinct.
- 'Send privately' fixes Signature Stay's misleading 'Share my rating'.
- Endpoint words and an italic caption word replace the digit labels.
directions.tradeoff:
- **Brand fit:** this only suits brands whose accent reaches 3:1 on dark (gold, bronze, tan, thermal blue, sage). Deep, red and near-black brands must use Folio, and admins need to be told that the stage follows their brand.
- **Looking alike:** two gold properties will look similar, differing only in initial, name and photo.
- **Genre:** Cormorant is a familiar spa face.
- **Payload:** the heaviest fonts of the three (about 95KB self-hosted with unicode-range splits).
- **First screen:** tight on a 375x667 phone with a two-line Bulgarian question, so the measured gate is mandatory.

property.name: Avela Resort (brand flex: Хотел Сарива Спа)
property.kind: Premium resort with pool and spa. The brand flex is a mountain thermal-spa hotel with a non-gold (thermal blue) brand.
property.place: Fictional southern-coast resort: stone colonnade, olive trees, a dusk pool. The flex is a fictional hotel in a Rhodope spa town. Both names are invented.
property.voice: Unhurried and warm, first-person plural, short sentences, no exclamation marks. Example: 'Stone, olive shade and water that keeps the last of the light. Thank you for spending part of your day with us.'

typography.display: Cormorant Garamond. Weight 600 for the wordmark (spaced capitals), the question and card titles. 500 italic for the chosen-word caption only, the single italic on the page. Fallback: 'Cormorant Garamond', Georgia, serif.
typography.body: Ysabeau Office 400/600 for body, buttons, placement line, meta and receipt. It is by the same designer as Cormorant (Christian Thalmann), so the pairing is native. Fallback: 'Ysabeau Office', system-ui, sans-serif. Never list Inter, Roboto or Arial.
typography.scale:
- Wordmark: Cormorant 600, 14px, uppercase, letter-spacing .28em.
- Placement line (h1): Ysabeau 600, 12/16, uppercase, .18em.
- Question and 'Thank you.': Cormorant 600, 32/38, letter-spacing -0.005em.
- Google and degraded card title: Cormorant 600, 24/30.
- Private card title: Cormorant 600, 22/28.
- Caption word: Cormorant 500 italic, 22/26.
- Description: Ysabeau 400, 17/26.
- Card body: Ysabeau 400, 16/24.
- Buttons: Ysabeau 600, 17/20 (secondary 15–16).
- Receipt and privacy: Ysabeau 400, 14–15/20.
- Endpoints and meta: Ysabeau 400, 13/18.
- Section label: Ysabeau 600, 12/16, uppercase, .18em.
- Footer: 12/16.
- No text below 12px. Body on dark is never lighter than weight 400.
typography.cyrillicNote:
Both families ship Cyrillic through Google's unicode-range subsets and carry a Bulgarian (BGR) locl. Put lang="bg" on <html> for BG boards, and on every Cyrillic span in EN boards (the 'БГ' link), so Bulgarian letterforms activate.

Google-served Cormorant has no smcp feature. Make 'small caps' with text-transform uppercase plus letter-spacing; never use font-variant: small-caps, which would be synthesized.

Measured with HarfBuzz:
- EN question at 32px = 332px, one line in 342.
- BG 'Как беше преживяването ви?' at 32px = 394px, two lines (balanced).
- 'Изпрати поверително' at 17/600 = 173px.
- 'ХОТЕЛ САРИВА СПА' at 14px/.24em = 192px, which fits beside the language control.

In production, self-host with the Bulgarian forms as default so a Cyrillic name renders correctly on an EN page.

directions.layoutSystem:
**Grid.** 390 wide, 24px gutters (content x24–366, 342px), 8px rhythm with gaps of 12, 16, 20, 24 and 32. The question, stars, receipt and 'Thank you.' are centred. Card contents are left-aligned. Radius 4 on buttons, cards and panels. No shadows. Depth comes only from tonal steps: stage #121614, then raised #1A1F1C, then field #232925. Hairlines are 1px #363835. **Components** (y positions in the EN artboard): - **A.band 0–232:** full-bleed photo or carved initial, plus grain. - **A.strip 0–56**, overlaid on the band: - Wordmark (displayName via CSS uppercase) at x24, vertically centred: Cormorant 600, 14px, .28em, #F2ECE1. It is a

, not a link. - Right:

with two 44x44 links, 'EN' and 'БГ' (lang="bg", hreflang, sr-only suffix ' English' / ' Български'). Ysabeau 600 14px. - Current link: #F2ECE1 with aria-current="page" and a 1px #CDAE78 underline 6px below. Other link: #D6CFC3. A 1x14 divider in rgba(214,207,195,.4) sits between them. The group ends at x366. - **A.h1 248–264:** the portal's localized title (placement line), centred. - **A.rating:** legend 276–314, stars 334–390, endpoints 396–414, caption slot 420–446, submit 462–514, privacy line 526–546. BG: the legend is 2 lines (276–352) and everything below moves +38. - **A.analytics** (arrival, until 'Got it'): - Hairline at y578. - Text 594–632: Ysabeau 400 13/19 #9D968A, left-aligned. - Actions row 636–680: 'Privacy notice' link on the left (14/600 #D9BE8C, underline offset 3). 'Got it'
directions.ratingControl:
**Structure.** A <fieldset> (no border, padding 0). Its <legend> is the question: 'How was your experience?' / 'Как беше преживяването ви?', Cormorant 600 32/38 #F2ECE1, centred, width 342, text-wrap balance.

**Radios and labels.** Five <input type="radio" name="rating" class="sr-only" id="r1"…"r5">, each followed by a <label for> of 56x56 (flex-centred, radius 6).
- Each label holds a 40x40 star SVG (viewBox 0 0 24 24, shared star path, stroke-linejoin round) and sr-only text: '1 star, Poor', '2 stars, Fair', '3 stars, Good', '4 stars, Very good', '5 stars, Excellent'. BG: '1 звезда, Слабо' … '5 звезди, Отлично'.
- The row is centred with a 10px gap (x35–355).

**Star states:**
- Idle: fill none, stroke #8D8C85 (5.4:1), stroke-width 1.1 (about 1.8px).
- Selected (stars 1..n of the checked value, with `checked` on input n): fill #CDAE78, stroke #CDAE78, stroke-width 1.4.
- Hover (pointer only): idle stroke #F2ECE1.
- Pressed: transform scale(.94), 90ms.

**Endpoints.** 'Poor' / 'Слабо' under star 1, left-aligned to x35. 'Excellent' / 'Отлично' under star 5, right-aligned to x355. Ysabeau 400 13/18 #9D968A, aria-hidden (the radio names already carry the words).

**Caption slot.** A 26px slot is always reserved so nothing shifts. The chosen word appears in Cormorant 500 italic 22/26 #D9BE8C, centred, aria-hidden.

**Error.** Shown in the same slot, which may grow to 2 lines. role="alert": a 16px alert icon in #CDAE78 plus Ysabeau 600 14/20 #F2ECE1 'Choose a rating from 1 to 5 stars.' The radios get aria-describedby pointing to it.

**Submit.** A <button type="submit"> of 342x52, radius 4, bg #D4B57E, label 'Send privately' / 'Изпрати поверително' in Ysabeau 600 17 #121614.
- Hover #DFC38F; active #C9A96F plus translateY(1px).
- Always enabled. It never submits on star tap.
- While sending, the label reads 'Sending…' and the width does not change.

**Privacy line.** Under the submit: a 14px lock icon (#CDAE78, 1.5 stroke) plus 'Shared privately with {name}.' in 14/20 #B8B0A3, centred.

**Helmet CSS:**
```
:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #EBD6A8;outline-offset:3px}
input[type=radio]:focus-visible + label{outline:2px solid #EBD6A8;outline-offset:2px}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){*{transition:none!important;animation:none!important}}
```
Plus the sr-only rule and a{color:#D9BE8C}.
signatureDetails: **Carved initial (the no-photo identity).** The first letter of displayName in Cormorant 600 at 176px, one tonal step off the band field. The shadow pair (0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.55) and 0 1px 0 light at 8%) makes it read as cut into stone. It is derived from data, works for 'A' and 'С' alike, and never has a ring or badge.

**The settle (production motion; A2–A4 draw its end state).** On a successful send the five 56px stars translate and scale into the 16px receipt stars: a same-document View Transition, 280ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). 60ms later the Google card rises 8px and fades in over 220ms, and the private card follows with the identical entrance. The motion is identical for every score. Under reduced motion it becomes a 100ms crossfade. Focus moves to 'Thank you.'
**One italic word.** The chosen-word caption ('Very good') is the only italic on the page. It confirms the choice in the property's serif voice without a dialog.
**The Signature Stay lineage, in type.** A spaced-capital wordmark (tracking .28em) and a champagne placement line (.18em) over a quiet stage, with 1px hairlines at 16%.
**Tonal depth, no shadows.** Three ink steps (#121614, #1A1F1C, #232925) do all the layering. The only gradients are the band field and the scrims.
**Focus built for photos.** A 2px champagne ring, offset 3px. Over the photo it always sits on the 82% scrim, so it holds 5:1 or better.

guards: **One Google card for every score.** A.google renders at y394–658 with identical copy, size, colours, icon and entrance in A2 (2 stars), A3 (5 stars) and A4 (4 stars). It takes no score input. The only score-dependent pixels on the page are the mini-star fill count and the caption word.

**Stars show only the guest's own choice.** No filled stars appear anywhere except the guest's own selection and receipt. Never put stars near the word Google. No Google logo; the plain word 'Google' plus an external-arrow icon is enough.
**Private card placement.** The private card appears only at 3 stars or below, always below the Google or degraded card, and never with a filled button.
**Degraded state.** Renders no link, URL or disabled button. The copy says the rating arrived privately.
**Carved initial.** It never gets a ring, border, check or badge (no seal look), and it is always aria-hidden.
**Photo and text.** No text sits on the raw photo. Only the strip sits on the 82% scrim, and the h1 and everything after it start below the band. There is at most one photo, never video.

**Champagne is earned.** Champagne appears only because Avela's brand is gold or bronze. Other accents keep their own hue with lightness shifted to 3:1 (A5). Brands that cannot reach 3:1 on dark are routed to Folio; A never draws its own light stage.
**Name once.** The wordmark appears once. The h1 is the placement ('Colonnade Pool & Terrace'), never the property name again.
**Measured first screen.** Submit bottom at 514 (A1) and 552 (A5), both within 640. Production gate: 548 or less at 375x667 with Safari toolbars.
**Rights stay close.** The receipt shows no submission time, which protects shared devices. Deadlines are shown only inside Your response, in local time with a zone label.
**Equal motion.** Motion is identical for 1 and 5 stars. No confetti, burst or celebration.
proposedBehaviourChanges: 'Send privately' replaces 'Submit private rating', and 'Send note privately' replaces 'Send private feedback'. This ships as one versioned guest-ui v2 language pack with e2e accessible-name updates. Keeping the old label is the zero-e2e fallback.
Visible endpoint words and a reserved caption word replace the digit labels. The selected stars get a visible fill and heavier stroke, fixing today's missing checked state.

The receipt collapses to one line with 'Change'. Correction, withdrawal and 'Start over on this device' move into a 'Your response' disclosure placed directly after the cards, with deadlines in local time. Manager policy copy is removed from the guest page.

The analytics notice becomes an inline region under the privacy line, keeping its name 'Portal analytics information' and its 'Got it' button, and it is never fixed over the submit button. This depends on counsel confirming removal of the non-exempt sessionStorage marker.

A 'Carved Stillness' composition is stored on the Property Brand Profile. The dark stage is chosen automatically when the derived accent reaches 3:1 on the brand text colour; otherwise the property renders as Folio.
Derived colour roles (accent 3:1, accent text 4.5:1, idle star 55% mix, black-or-white button label) are computed from the three existing hex values and checked at publish.
The no-photo band gets a carved initial generated from displayName.
Self-hosted Cormorant Garamond and Ysabeau Office subsets with Bulgarian forms as default. The /p page is isolated from THEME_INIT_SCRIPT and the app tokens.
Links stay after rating in these boards (current contract). Links from arrival is only the C6 proposal.

directions.name: Folio
directions.oneLiner: The portal as a page from the property's own stationery: warm paper, graphite ink, one masthead in a high-contrast serif, printer's rules and a numbered index of links. Premium through typesetting rather than atmosphere, with a night edition for evening venues.
directions.axis: Polarity: light paper by default, with an inverted night edition. Composition: a flush-left editorial column with an asymmetric margin. Identity carrier: typesetting (a 56px two-line masthead, an Oxford rule, a double-ruled panel, a numbered index). Voice: literate and hand-set.
directions.rationale:
The guest judge ranked it highest (7.5): it has the strongest no-photo answer, and it is the only direction credible for both a boutique hotel and a bistro or wine bar. The truth and market judges keep it as the necessary light twin that deep and monochrome brands need (oxblood, purple, olive-grey on cream all pass here and fail on dark). It is also where the neutral hospitality default palette lands.

Judges' fixes applied:
- No numerals under the stars.
- The wordmark (56px) and question (26px) clearly differ, so there is one serif moment.
- The submit is full-width.
- The stub carries no timestamp.
- A night edition exists for evening placements.
- It keeps its paper and flush-left identity so it never collapses into A's light stage.
directions.tradeoff:
- **Owner perception:** owners expecting a 'wow' photo may read it as a beautifully typeset document. The masthead has to be generous.
- **Links depend on data:** the index shines only with localized link labels and category titles (a new capability). With today's single-string labels a BG guest can see mixed-language rows.
- **Unfamiliar layout:** flush-left is less familiar than centred pages in this market.
- **White brands:** white-background brands need the paper tone, or they look cold.
- **Night edition:** it is a second colourway to QA.

directions.layoutSystem:
**Grid.** A flush-left editorial column with a left gutter of 28 and a right gutter of 24 (x28–366, 338px). The asymmetric margin is deliberate. 4px baseline grid; 32px between sections.

- An **Oxford rule** (2px graphite, 3px gap, 1px graphite) under the masthead and above the colophon.
- A **double rule** (border 3px double #1D2528) on the Google panel's top and bottom only.
- A **perforation** (a 1px div with background repeating-linear-gradient(90deg,#1D2528 0 4px,transparent 4px 8px)) bounding the stub.

directions.ratingControl:
**Structure.** A <fieldset> (no border). Its <legend> is the question: 'How was your experience?' / 'Как беше преживяването ви?', Playfair 400 26/32 #1D2528, left-aligned, text-wrap balance.

**Radios and labels.** Five sr-only radios (name="rating", ids r1–r5), each followed by a <label for> of 56x56 (radius 2).
- The labels are left-aligned from x28 with an 8px gap (row x28–340).
- Each holds a 36x36 star (shared path, viewBox 24, round joins) and sr-only text: '1 star, Poor' … '5 stars, Excellent'.

**Star states:**
- Idle: fill none, stroke #7D7F7D (3.5:1), stroke-width 1.2 (about 1.8px).
- Selected (1..n): fill #1F5E78, stroke #1F5E78, width 1.4.
- Hover: idle stroke #1D2528.
- Pressed: scale(.94).
- No numerals under the stars.

**Endpoints.** 'Poor' starting at x28, and 'Excellent' ending at x340. Sofia 400 13/18 #5F676A, aria-hidden.

**Caption slot.** 24px, always reserved. It holds a 16x1 #1F5E78 rule, then 8px, then the chosen word in Sofia 600 13/16 uppercase .14em #1F5E78 (for example '— VERY GOOD'), aria-hidden.

**Error.** Shown in the same slot, role="alert": a 16px alert icon (stroke #1F5E78; claret #E3A597 at night) plus Sofia 600 14/20 in the text colour. The radios reference it with aria-describedby.

**Submit.** Full column, 338x52, radius 2, bg #1D2528, label 'Send privately' in Sofia 600 17 #F3EEE4, centred.
- Hover #2C373B; active translateY(1px).
- Always enabled. 'Sending…' while pending.

**Privacy line.** 'Shared privately with {name}.' in Sofia 400 14/20 #4A5356, left-aligned. No icon: the rule-and-type language carries it.

**Helmet CSS:**
```
:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #1F5E78;outline-offset:3px}
input[type=radio]:focus-visible + label{outline:2px solid #1F5E78;outline-offset:2px}
```
Night: #F0C3B8. Plus the reduced-motion rule, the sr-only rule and a{color:#1F5E78}.
signatureDetails: **The masthead.** A small-caps placement kicker over a 56px two-line Playfair wordmark, closed by an Oxford rule (thick, gap, thin). The page reads as the property's letterhead.

**The stub.** After sending, the rating block becomes a stub bounded by two perforated rules, with 'Thank you.' and a one-line receipt. It never prints a time, so a shared device never shows the previous guest's moment. Production: the perforation draws once with stroke-dashoffset over 300ms; crossfade under reduced motion; identical for every score.
**The double-ruled Google panel.** Framed only by printer's double rules above and below, with no box. It is calm, neutral and the same for 1 to 5.

**The index.** Useful links set as a numbered table of contents: '01 Breakfast & bar menu ······ Menu ↗'. The dotted leaders line up like a hotel directory or a menu card, and the right-hand word is the admin's own category title.
**The ruled letter.** The private note is written on baselines (a repeating 32px rule), so it looks like writing a note, not filling a form.

guards: **One Google panel for every score.** It renders at y402–633 with identical copy, rules, button, icon and subline in B2 (2 stars), B3 (5 stars), B4 and B6. It takes no score input.
**Private note placement.** The letter appears only at 3 stars or below, always after the Google panel, as an outline button or composer, and never a filled primary before Google.
**Scale contrast.** No numerals under the stars. The wordmark is 56px and the question 26px, never within 1.5x of each other.
**Full-width submit.** The submit is always full column width (338x52), never auto-width.
**No timestamp on the stub.** The stub never prints a date or time.
**Index structure.** The index is a real <ol> of links. Leaders are decorative and aria-hidden. The right-hand word is the admin category title, not an invented fact (no hours, prices or ratings).
**Figure.** The figure is never full-bleed and never above the rating. At most one image.
**Night edition.** It keeps every contrast role: stars 6.9:1, text 14.3:1, meta 6.1:1 or better.
**Serif size.** The serif is used only at 20px and above. All UI text is Sofia Sans.
**Measured first screen.** Submit bottom at 470 (B1) and 502 (B5), both within 640. Production gate: 548 or less at 375x667.
**Structure without boxes.** No drop shadows, no rounded cards, no filled panels except the inline confirm box.
proposedBehaviourChanges: A 'Folio' composition on the Brand Profile. It is the automatic stage for brands whose accent cannot reach 3:1 on dark, and the stage for the new neutral hospitality default palette.
A night-edition switch per composition, proposed as the default for placements the admin marks as evening (bar, restaurant).
Localized EN and BG link labels and category titles (a new capability), strongly needed because the index is text-first. Missing translations are flagged before publish.
An optional, explicitly accepted 'paper tone' suggestion for brands with a pure #FFFFFF background.
The stub receipt replaces the stacked receipt boxes and never prints the response time. Rights move into 'Your response' with local-time deadlines and an inline two-step remove.

Shared with A: the guest-ui v2 pack ('Send privately', 'Send note privately', endpoint and caption words, Google subline), the inline analytics region, derived colour roles checked at publish, self-hosted Playfair (2) and Sofia Sans, /p isolated from the app theme.
Links stay after rating in these boards (current contract). The index-from-arrival variant is covered by the C6 proposal decision.

directions.name: Table Card
directions.oneLiner: The page continues the printed card the guest just scanned. The property's colour fills a poster with its name set huge, and the rating sits on a light plate below a fold, like a table tent unfolded. It is bold and local, and recognisable in 200ms with no photo.
directions.axis: Polarity: brand colour field over a light plate. Composition: poster over plate, joined by a card-stock fold. Identity carrier: colour plus a giant extra-condensed wordmark. Voice: confident, appetising, print-continuous.
directions.rationale:
This is the only strong answer for restaurants, bars, grills, city and lifestyle hotels and loud brands, roughly half the buyers. All three judges put it in the best three, and it is the direction that beats Ratestar most visibly without photography.

Print-to-screen continuity (the table tent and the page share one composition) is a concrete sales tool. It needs only three hex values and displayName, set in one Bulgarian-designed superfamily.

Judges' fixes applied:
- The Wolt/Glovo bottom sheet is removed: no 24px overlap radius, no soft shadow. Instead there is a flat crease with a 16px fold shade, like folded card stock.
- The wordmark is set as entered, never forced to lowercase.
- Link rows carry no fact-like sublines and no tel: links.
- Errors never use red, because red can be the brand.
- The derived plate accent is shown openly (C5), so owners see why their stars are darker than their poster.
directions.tradeoff:
- **Fit:** too loud for calm luxury hotels; hotels will mostly use it for pool-bar and restaurant placements.
- **Colour:** a saturated field can glare at night. The derived plate accent is visibly darker than the brand colour for light brands such as orange, gold and ochre. Monochrome brands get a severe black poster.
- **Engineering:** wordmark auto-fit for Latin and Cyrillic names up to 120 characters is real algorithm and visual-QA work. iconKey needs a curated enum and a picker.
- **Links:** the concept is strongest with links from arrival (C6), which is a contract change.
- **Photos:** no photos are shown this round.

directions.ratingControl:
**Structure.** A <fieldset> (no border). Its <legend> is the question: 'How was your experience?' / 'Как беше преживяването ви?', Sofia 700 28/32 #221A16, left-aligned.

**Radios and labels.** Five sr-only radios followed by <label for> of 56x56 (radius 6).
- The labels are left-aligned from x24 with a 10px gap (x24–344).
- Each holds a 42x42 star (shared path, round joins, stroke-width 1.3, about 2.3px: the poster's weight) and sr-only text: '1 star, Poor' … '5 stars, Excellent'.

**Star states:**
- Idle: fill none, stroke #837D76.
- Selected (1..n): fill and stroke in the plate accent (#C8402A for Forma; derived #9A6A0C for Вардела).
- Hover: idle stroke #221A16.
- Pressed: scale(.94).

**Endpoints.** 'Poor' starting at x24, 'Excellent' ending at x344. Sofia 600 13/18 #6E625A, aria-hidden.

**Caption slot.** 32px, always reserved. The chosen word appears in Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 800 30/32 in the plate accent (large text, 3:1 or better), aria-hidden.

**Error.** Shown in the same slot, role="alert": an 18px alert icon in #221A16 plus Sofia 700 15/20 #221A16 'Choose a rating from 1 to 5 stars.' Never red, because red can be the brand.

**Submit.** 342x56, radius 6, bg #C8402A, label 'Send privately' in Sofia 700 18 #FFFFFF.
- Hover #B53A26; active translateY(1px).
- Always enabled; 'Sending…' while pending.
- When the primary is below 3:1 against the plate (ochre in C5), the button keeps the primary fill, uses the black-or-white label that passes, and adds a 1.5px border in the derived accent.

**Privacy line.** 'Shared privately with {name}.' in Sofia 400 14/20 #5A4E47.

**Helmet CSS:**
```
:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #221A16;outline-offset:3px}
input[type=radio]:focus-visible + label{outline:2px solid #221A16;outline-offset:2px}
```
Poster links use an inline style outline in the on-poster colour. Plus the reduced-motion rule, the sr-only rule and a{color:#B53A26}.
signatureDetails: **The fold.** Poster, crease and plate read as the table tent unfolded: a 1px crease plus a 16px fold shade where a bottom sheet would normally sit. The printed tent uses exactly this composition, with the QR code on the plate.
**The name as poster.** A 96px Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 800 wordmark, set as entered, auto-fitted for Latin and Cyrillic names. The property's own colour fills the top 280px.
**The poster never reacts.** The poster is identical in every state. Only the plate's contents change, crossfading over 200ms, identical for every score; instant under reduced motion.
**The caption in the poster's voice.** The chosen word ('Very good') is set in the wordmark face and the plate accent, readable at arm's length.
**Red-safe feedback.** Validation and save errors use an espresso icon and text, never red alone, so a red brand never reads as an error.
